News.title: Burnham: UK must end ‘moral failure’ of Neets crisis
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Andy Burnham has said the UK must “invest in success” rather than “failure through the benefits system” as he set out his commitment to end the youth unemployment crisis.

The prime minister described the number of young people not in employment, education or training (Neet) as an “economic catastrophe and a moral failure” .

Almost one million young people are currently classed as Neet, according to the Office for National Statistics, contributing to the size of the welfare bill and making efforts to boost youth employment a key priority for the government.

Pledging to guarantee young people support “up front”, the prime minister wrote in The Times: “We face a choice. We either invest in the success of our young people or pay for failure through the benefits system. We cannot afford to do both. I choose the first.”

He added: “Today, the welfare system provides an assessment, a payment and, after that, a goodbye. Too often there is no support, no offer of skills and no opportunity to get a job.”

The government is expected to publish a series of “jobs plans” for key sectors over the course of the week, beginning with the professional services and construction industries.

open image in gallery The prime minister described the number of young people not in employment, education or training (Neet) as an “economic catastrophe and a moral failure” . ( AFP/Getty )

The plans will see 22,400 apprenticeships a year made available by accountancy, legal services and consultancy firms for under-25s.

Further jobs plans for the digital, technology and defence industries are expected to be published later in the week.

The plans come ahead of the publication of a report into the Neet issue from former cabinet minister Alan Milburn, who is expected to make a series of recommendations after the Budget at the end of October.

Speaking to the Guardian, Mr Milburn suggested his report was likely to recommend cutting benefit spending in order to channel the money into supporting people back into work.

He said: “We’ve got to have a different conversation about the welfare system, it just isn’t working for young people.

“We need to redistribute money from the welfare system to more employment support if we are going to end the Neet crisis.”

Mr Milburn also called for employment, mental health and benefits support to be more integrated.

He said: “Over the medium term, it is entirely possible that you can reduce the benefits bill, but in order to do that, you’ve got to provide the support for young people.

“You’ve got to increase the opportunities that are available for young people and then provide the support for them to enable them to grab those opportunities.”

open image in gallery Former health secretary Alan Milburn (Jeff Moore/PA) ( PA Wire )

Work and pensions secretary Pat McFadden said: “Too many young people have been locked out of opportunities for too long. These commitments will help change that by creating clear pathways into apprenticeships, training and good jobs.

“It’s encouraging to see even more industries backing young people with new opportunities to gain the skills, training and experience needed to succeed in the growing sectors of our economy.”

Shadow business secretary Julia Lopez said: “Labour have been a disaster for youth jobs.

“Their tax hikes and red tape have made it harder for businesses to hire, invest and grow, destroying opportunities for young people looking to take their first step on the career ladder.

“After increasing costs on employers and burdening firms with more red tape, Labour are now trying to paper over the cracks.”

News.title: Cindy Crawford breaks silence on son Presley Gerber’s death at 27
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Cindy Crawford has spoken out about the death of her son, Presley Gerber, at age 27.

Nearly a month after Presley died September 20 of a suspected overdose, Crawford shared a tribute to him on Instagram on Sunday that was co-signed with Presley’s father, Rande Gerber, and sister, Kaia Gerber.

With a black-and-white picture of Presley, the family wrote: “We are beyond heartbroken to lose our beloved son and brother.

“We feel so blessed to have had Presley in our lives for 27 years,” the post continued. “He is a sweet, beautiful soul who loved and is loved, now and forever. We are so proud of how he showed up in the world, with kindness and vulnerability.”

The post concluded: “We are grateful for the outpouring of love and support from so many who know and love our family and even strangers who feel our pain. Til we meet again our sweet boy. We love you forever, Mom, Dad and Kaia.”

open image in gallery Presley Gerber is the son of Cindy Crawford and Rande Gerber ( Getty )

Presley, the son of supermodel Crawford and businessman Rande, was in a rehab facility in Los Angeles at the time of his death, the county’s medical examiner confirmed to The Independent.

A representative for Crawford, 60, Rande, 64, and Kaia, 25, told The Independent in a statement at the time: “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time.”

open image in gallery Rande Gerber, Cindy Crawford and Kaia Gerber shared a statement Sunday remembering Presley Gerber ( PA Archive )

In addition to the family’s statement shared on Crawford’s page, Kaia shared her own tribute to her brother on Instagram on Sunday.

“I love you the bluest, to the moon and back and back again, forever big brother,” the actor shared in the post, which included a childhood video and picture of her and Presley together.

Kaia went on to say, “I don’t have the words” to address “the magnitude of losing you.”

“You know how much I loved being your sister. It has always been, and will forever be, my favorite thing about myself,” she said. “I came into this world with a white-knuckle grip around you. I had more love for you than I knew what to do with. And now that it has nowhere obvious to go, I’m certain it’s going to swallow me whole.”

She continued: “To say loving you was the easiest thing in the world would imply that it required any effort at all. I was born loving you. I will die loving you. There was never anything else.”

Kaia went on to say that she “would walk knowingly toward this grief if it meant that on the other side of it I got to be your sister.”

“My darling brother, I do adore you,” she wrote. “I love my brother. My brother is dead. And this party sucks so bad without you, prez.”

Presley was open about his struggles with substance abuse and mental health issues in the years before his death. In March, he posted a video of himself using experimental drug Ibogaine in a drug withdrawal treatment in Cancun, Mexico.

He captioned the post, in part, “letting go of control didn’t come easy, but I trusted there was something bigger than me guiding it. I knew why I was there. I faced what I had been running from, and somewhere in all of it, I started finding my way back to myself.”

“Praying it’s the last time I have to come back,” he wrote. “Next time I’d like to choose.”

If you or someone you know is suffering from drug addiction, you can seek confidential help and support 24-7 from Frank, by calling 0300 123 6600, texting 82111, sending an email or visiting their website here.

In the US, the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration can be reached at 1-800-662-HELP.

News.title: Mulberry sales lift 18% as turnaround progress accelerates
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Luxury handbag maker Mulberry has revealed a surge in sales for the past six months amid continued progress with its turnaround strategy.

The group said it has seen momentum continue into the second half of the financial year despite a “challenging” macroeconomic backdrop.

Boss Andrea Baldo said he was “very pleased” with recent progress by the business.

The Somerset-based business revealed that group sales lifted by 18% for the 26 weeks to September 26, compared with the same period a year earlier.

Mulberry said it was buoyed by “strong customer demand” across both its seasonal and core fashion collections, with positive sales of new products including its Raffia, Crochet and Stevie bags.

It added that recent trading also benefited from increased visibility following the Mulberry by Christopher Kane runway show at London Fashion Week.

UK sales increased by 10% over the half-year, with like-for-like growth of 9%.

Meanwhile, it was boosted by a 28% sales jump in the US and a 23% in Europe, excluding the UK.

Franchise and wholesale demand also grew strongly, with 52% sales growth across the division.

The fashion brand, known for its leather handbags, is undergoing a major turnaround plan it launched early last year as part of efforts to shore up its finances and return to profit

Mr Baldo, chief executive of Mulberry, said: “The strength of our performance reflects the work undertaken over the past year to refocus the group around product, brand and customer, while maintaining a disciplined approach to trading and cost management.

“The growth in full-price sales is particularly encouraging, demonstrating that our collections are resonating with customers across our key markets.

“There remains much more to achieve as part of our strategic plan, and we are operating in a challenging trading environment.

“However, we enter the second half with a strong product pipeline, increased brand desirability and a clear focus on delivering our strategy.”

News.title: At least 19 dead as sudden downpour triggers stampede at Hindu festival in India
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

At least 19 people died and nearly two dozen suffered injuries in a stampede during a major Hindu festival in eastern India’s West Bengal state.

The stampede in the state capital of Kolkata took place on Saturday night when a crowd near a pavilion, locally known as pandal, in Chorbagan ran for cover as it began raining during Durga Puja, an annual festival celebrating the goddess Durga. Some worshippers fell on the road, triggering the stampede, police said.

The dead included 11 women and two children.

Police registered a case of culpable homicide and detained seven people, including members of the Chorbagan pandal organising committee, who were sent by a local court into police custody for 10 days.

State chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said a special investigation team headed by a judge of the High Court would look into what caused the stampede.

Indian prime minister Narendra Modi described it as a "tragic" incident and said the state government was providing help to the affected families.

open image in gallery An ambulance carrying Durga Puja pandal stampede victims arrives at the Calcutta Medical College and Hospital ( AFP/Getty )

Police said they were examining a video of a purported announcement from the pavilion asking the assembled people to leave because the bamboo structure was about to collapse.

"We are trying to identify who made the announcement and what prompted it," an unnamed official told the broadcaster NDTV.

"We have gathered sufficient evidence pointing to gross mismanagement by the puja organisers. There was no clear plan to manage the large number of visitors and everything was handled verbally.”

The chief minister claimed the stampede was triggered “after an announcement made by a private security agency”.

Mr Adhikari announced a compensation of Rs 2.5m (£19,700) and a state job each for the families of the dead and Rs 500,000 (£3,950) each for the injured.

The government imposed restrictions in parts of north Kolkata, prohibiting assemblies of five or more people within a specific area. The restrictions will continue until 20 October.

Authorities also advised several of Kolkata’s most heavily attended pandals to temporarily close to visitors.

Kolkata comes alive in a grand spectacle of light as thousands of elaborate, temporary pavilions rise up every year for the five-day worship of Durga. There are around 3,500 pandals dotting the city this year.

Durga Puja in Kolkata is on the UN’s list of the “Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity”.

open image in gallery Police officers inspect the site of a stampede in Kolkata ( Reuters )

Stampedes are rare during Durga Puja celebrations in Kolkata even though crowd crushes are relatively common at religious festivals in other parts of India.

In January last year, at least 30 people were killed as tens of thousands of Hindus rushed to bathe in a sacred river during the Maha Kumbh festival, the world’s largest religious gathering. Two years ago, a crowd crush at a Hindu religious gathering killed 121 people in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.

In 2013, pilgrims attending a Hindu festival at a temple in central Madhya Pradesh state panicked amid fears that a bridge would collapse, leading to at least 115 people being crushed or drowning in the river below.

News.title: Infant among six migrants dead after boat collision near Greece
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Six migrants, including an infant, have died after a speedboat carrying people from Turkey overturned following a collision with a Greek coast guard vessel off Lesvos early on Monday, Greek authorities said, as the government vowed "zero tolerance" towards migrant smugglers.

The collision occurred roughly 3.5 nautical miles south of Agrilia, Lesvos.

Rescuers recovered the bodies of four men, one woman and an infant, according to the coast guard, while eight survivors were taken to hospital.

Authorities have arrested a 37-year-old Turkish national among the survivors, identifying him as the suspected smuggler and operator of the boat.

Greece's shipping minister Vassilis Kikilias blamed migrant traffickers for the deaths and said evidence so far indicated the speedboat struck the left side of a coast guard vessel with its bow, adding that the exact circumstances were under investigation.

"Our position is non-negotiable: zero tolerance for smugglers," he said in a post on X.

Greece has long been a favoured gateway to Europe for migrants and refugees from the Middle East, Africa and Asia.

In 2015-16, it was at the frontline of Europe's migration crisis and nearly 1 million people landed on its islands, mainly from Turkey.

News.title: Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City
News.content:
In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough
News.content:
Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

News.title: Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation
News.content:
Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

News.title: Steely Chelsea triumph despite losing Martinez to head injury
News.content:
This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

This was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”

Asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso said: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”

News.title: Wallabies humiliated in ‘unacceptable’ thrashing by New Zealand
News.content:
New Zealand blew Australia off the field in an extraordinary first-half display in Sydney as they claimed a 13th successive win against the Wallabies and completed a 2-0 Bledisloe Cup clean sweep.

The annual series had already gone New Zealand’s way for a 24th successive year at Eden Park last weekend, but Australia did enough in a highly competitive first half in Auckland to suggest they could give the All Blacks a game on their home turf. And in a breathless opening six minutes in Sydney, it looked as if they might.

The ball-in-play time during that opening spell was incredible as both teams committed to fast, attacking rugby, offloading from everywhere. Like two heavyweights going toe-to-toe in the opening round of a boxing contest, throwing haymakers to see who would get knocked out first.

Ryan Lonergan produced an excellent turnover for the Wallabies to trigger an Australia counter, and the irrepressible Peter Lakai responded with one for the visitors, as the ball travelled from one end of the pitch to the other in one long unbroken spell.

But after New Zealand wing Josh Moorby finally crossed the whitewash, it was Australia who found themselves out on their feet, punch drunk.

Sports.title: NBA on Sky Sports: Live matches and big moments in 2026/27
Sports.content:
The 2026/27 NBA season is here and Sky Sports viewers have lots to look forward to.

With up to 130 live regular season games, plus matches from the playoffs including the Conference Finals and NBA Finals, there is a feast of live action heading your way.

All bases are covered with five live games on Christmas Day, plus coverage of All-Star Weekend and MLK Day, so with no further ado, here's your guide to some of the biggest moments this season…

Opening Night

The most immediate - and perhaps the most unmissable - instalment of NBA on Sky is the league's opening night on Tuesday.

The Detroit Pistons - who topped the Eastern Conference last year with an impressive 60-22 record - play host to the 2024 champions Boston Celtics at 8pm on Sky Sports Mix. The Celtics are sporting a new-look side featuring Paul George after his arrival in a high-profile trade that facilitated the departure of last year's leading scorer Jaylen Brown.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player LeBron James got 10 points, five assists and four rebounds in the first half in Philadelphia 76ers debut in preseason match against Brooklyn Nets

Later that evening, Brown joins up with LeBron James, Joel Embiid, and the rest of his new Philadelphia 76ers team-mates as they travel to Madison Square Garden to face the reigning champion New York Knicks.

The slate ends with yet another fascinating match-up: a rematch of last year's seven-game epic Western Conference Finals series between reigning MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's Oklahoma City Thunder and Victor Wembanyama's San Antonio Spurs.

Christmas Day

Christmas Day is already a staple in the NBA calendar - but this year in particular is a feast for UK fans, with five games across 12 hours of live basketball on Sky.

The day kicks off with a rematch of the 2026 Finals - Wembanyama's Spurs will look to exact their revenge on Jalen Brunson's Knicks in New York at 5pm, before Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami Heat visit the Celtics in Boston.

Later, LeBron returns to Los Angeles as an opposing player for the first time in eight years to take on the Lakers at Staples Center, with the Thunder playing Anthony Edwards' Minnesota Timberwolves and the Denver Nuggets taking a trip to San Francisco to face Steph Curry's Golden State Warriors in the early hours of the morning.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the NBA Finals Game 5 match-up between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs

All-Star Weekend

All-Star weekend - the NBA's mid-season showpiece - will once again be shown live on Sky.

The NBA All-Star game on Sunday night headlines the weekend - but there are five other events for fans to get stuck into across the three-day event

The All-Star weekend kicks off with the Rising Stars game on Friday, with its own round robin featuring a draft selected by a plethora of honorary coaches and NBA legends to be selected closer to the time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nikola Jokic reminded everyone of his extraordinary playmaking ability in Sunday's preseason opener, whipping a sensational behind-the-back crosscourt assist to Cameron Johnson for three

The four teams are made up of players in their first and second years in the NBA - last year, the field was headlined by Mavericks No 1 pick Cooper Flagg, bar one team, which is made up entirely of players from the NBA's development affiliate, the G-League.

Saturday features the Shooting Stars contest, the three-point contest and the dunk contest.

If that wasn't enough, Friday's action finishes with the NBA All-Star Celebrity Game, before the Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCU) classic takes place early on the next day.

Play-in tournament

The play-in tournament at the beginning of April - taking place just after the end of the regular season, but before the playoffs - represents one of the most emotional and consequential weekends of the NBA season.

While the teams that finish Nos. 1-6 in the standings of each conference are guaranteed a playoff spot, the teams that finish Nos. 7-10 in the standings are entered into the play-in. These teams will battle for the seventh and eighth playoff seeds.

Here is the NBA's overview of how it works:

Each conference's No. 7 team in the standings will host the No. 8 team. The winners secure the No. 7 seed in the playoffs. The losers will get another chance to earn a playoff spot.

E ach conference's No. 9 team in the standings will host the No. 10 team. The winners will advance to the final stage of the Play-In Tournament. The losers are eliminated.

The losers of the No. 7 vs. No. 8 matchups will host the winners of the No. 9 vs. No. 10 matchups. The winners secure the No. 8 seed in the NBA playoffs for its conference. The losing teams are eliminated.



2027 NBA Finals

After 1,230 regular season games and a potential 98 playoff games - it will all come down to the 2027 NBA finals, which will be live on Sky Sports.

Last season's finals saw the Knicks only require five games to beat the Spurs and secure their first NBA championship in 54 years, prompting frenzied celebrations in America's biggest city that New York will be keen to recreate in 2026.

Sports.title: US GP talking points: How will Hamilton, Norris move on from woes?
Sports.content:
Formula 1 returns to Austin's Circuit of The Americas for the United States Grand Prix with a historic championship crowning potentially in the offing, along with several other hot topics on the agenda.

All eyes on Antonelli as history beckons

The event in Texas kicks off the second of three triple-headers to end the season, with races in Mexico and Brazil immediately following this one.

There is every chance that Antonelli will become F1's youngest ever world champion on one of the next three Sundays, but it would require something quite dramatic for that to be in Austin.

Antonelli would need to win the United States Grand Prix and for his Mercedes team-mate George Russell to finish ninth or lower, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton also finishing fifth or lower.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell takes over from Kimi Antonelli's engineer during the Sprint rain delay in Singapore.

However the weekend plays out, it will be fascinating to see how Antonelli handles the pressure of the title being attainable for the first time.

Ultimately, there has been little evidence to suggest the 20-year-old will back far away from the aggressive approach that has served him so well this season, and why should he?

Will Mercedes' upgrades work better?

A key factor in determining when Antonelli seals the title could be the performance of his Mercedes car, and more specifically the upgrades that have been brought to it in recent weeks.

The Silver Arrows had projected plenty of confidence over the major package they added to the W17 at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, but it appeared to have a negative impact as they delivered arguably their least performative weekend of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff explains Mercedes issues after big upgrade package at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia.

That led to the team taking the quite extreme step of running a full test of the upgrades the following weekend in Singapore as Antonelli drove with the new parts on his car and Russell drove with the pre-Sepang specification.

The extreme heat and nature of the surface in Malaysia made it tricky for all the teams to analyse their performance, while Singapore's Marina Bay Street Circuit is also something of an outlier on the calendar.

A return to a more traditional circuit in Austin therefore makes it a crucial weekend for Mercedes, whose plans for the development of their 2027 car will be significantly impacted if this package simply doesn't work.

Can Verstappen make it a hat-trick?

There is no longer any doubt that Max Verstappen and Red Bull are well and truly back.

The four-time world champion had to wait until the 16th round of the season for his first Grand Prix victory of 2026, but it was then just seven days before his second came along.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Max Verstappen wins his first ever Singapore Grand Prix.

There's no doubt that the upgrades Red Bull have gradually added to the car are working, with Verstappen having been in a league of his own over the past two weekends.

Antonelli might be on the brink of glory, but there is already a growing sense in the paddock that Verstappen could end this year and start next season as the driver to beat.

Antonelli himself admitted that it would be "very scary" if Verstappen was challenging him for the title in this form.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the Sky Sports F1 Show Podcast, Bernie Collins gave huge flowers to Red Bull and their strategy after Max Verstappen's clean sweep in Singapore.

Verstappen is just eight points behind third-placed Lewis Hamilton and 17 points behind second-placed Russell in the drivers' standings, with both at major risk of being overhauled by the Dutchman in the coming weeks.

While the positions below first in the Drivers' Championship count for little, Verstappen appears as though he may be in the process of laying down a major psychological marker for next year.

How will Hamilton handle strategy error?

In contrast to the late-season momentum that Verstappen is building, his old rival Hamilton's campaign is fizzling out.

The latest downturn came in Singapore when the seven-time world champion made an inexplicable decision to ignore Ferrari's call for him to come into the pits during a Virtual Safety Car period.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chadhok dissects Lewis Hamilton's Singapore GP race.

While stopping would have almost certainly condemned him to finishing behind team-mate Charles Leclerc, getting rid of his already worn tyres would have likely sealed a podium finish, or at worst, fourth place.

Instead, he took the chequered flag in sixth, before not showing up for his post-race interviews amid concern over his physical condition following the gruelling race.

The saga has led to speculation over a possible breakdown of trust between Hamilton and the Ferrari pit wall, with the 41-year-old having been unhappy with their choices on several other occasions this season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player On the F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins considers whether Lewis Hamilton has lost trust in Ferrari after overriding a team strategy call in Singapore.

Given the fact he didn't speak after the race in Singapore, there will be extra attention on his press briefings on Thursday in Austin.

While that might be intriguing, the more pressing issue is that Ferrari need to sort their act out for 2027 with the threat of Verstappen looming.

Repercussions for Norris?

If Red Bull need a warning against taking anything for granted after Verstappen's successive wins, it's glaring at them in the form of the papaya McLarens.

Either side of the summer break, it was Lando Norris who claimed his first two victories of the season in successive races in Hungary and the Netherlands.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri make contact on the final lap of the Singapore Grand Prix Sprint race.

He should have had a third in Madrid soon after, with his hugely impressive pace at each of those events leading many to believe McLaren were going to be the team to beat for the remainder of the season.

Instead, the last triple-header saw them drop painfully backwards. Norris didn't qualify higher than fifth at the three events and his best result was fourth in Singapore.

The Brit was also guilty of creating negative headlines for the team by attempting a late overtake in the Singapore Sprint on his team-mate Oscar Piastri that resulted in the pair crashing and cost them both points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports F1's Karun Chandhok dissects who was at fault for the collision between the two McLaren's which saw Oscar Piastri crash out of the Singapore GP Sprint race.

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella and chief executive Zak Brown made it clear they were extremely unhappy with the collision, but opted against publicly criticising Norris.

Now that the team have had more time to review the incident, it will be interesting to see if Norris feels the need to make further apologies, or whether there are firmer words from the top.

Sports.title: What next for Kartal after 'unbelievable week' in Wuhan
Sports.content:
Sonay Kartal is the new British No 1 after her remarkable run to the Wuhan Open final where she was narrowly beaten by Poland's Maja Chwalinska in three sets.

Kartal became just the second Briton, after Johanna Konta, to play in a WTA 1000 final with superb wins over Tokyo Olympic champion Belinda Bencic, two-time Grand Slam finalist Jasmine Paolini, world No 6 Elina Svitolina and former French Open champion Jelena Ostapenko.

It is arguably the most impressive tournament performance from a British female player since Emma Raducanu won the 2021 US Open, particularly given Kartal only returned to action last month following six months out due to a stress fracture in her back.

"We have had an unbelievable week. Not many people expected me to be here and bring these levels," said the 24-year-old after losing 2-6 6-4 6-2 to this year's French Open runner-up Chwalinska.

"I hope I can be in many more of these finals. It was not the result I wanted today but those people in my box are the reason I am healthy, I am here and why I am back to fitness."

Kartal has slowly climbed up the WTA rankings over the last five years but emerged onto the public stage with runs to the third and fourth round at Wimbledon in 2024 and 2025.

She became known for her variety, athleticism and aggressive forehand from awkward angles - strengths that helped her last week in Wuhan.

Image: Sonay Kartal is up to 50th on the WTA rankings after her run to the final in Wuhan (Chinatopix Via AP)

Kartal's stress fracture in her back saw her retire from the fourth round of Indian Wells in March against Elena Rybakina and led to her longest period out of tennis.

The long spell on the sidelines means Kartal can use her protected ranking - a provision that allows players to use the ranking they had at the time of their injury, if they have been out for at least six months, to enter tournaments over the next 12 months.

"The rehab was tough. I think the main priority was to just get back on court and maybe I didn't do the big heavy lifting, which now I can do," said Kartal.

"I wanted to use these weeks to see where I'm at physically and what I need to improve and to see if I'm feeling how I was on the court from in March. The remainder of this year I'm going to work on those things and I'm excited to start next year already."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sonay Kartal discussed her back injury after reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open and whether she will get a celebratory tattoo if she wins.

How good could Kartal be?

We have been here before with British tennis players - Katie Boulter won a WTA 500 event in 2024, Raducanu memorably won the 2021 US Open as a teenager, and reached the final at Queen's Club this summer before a stress fracture in her right leg forced her to miss Wimbledon, the US Open and likely the remainder of this season.

Kartal's week in Wuhan was arguably against stiffer opposition than what Boulter and Raducanu faced, plus it was only her second tour tournament back after injury.

"There is no doubt in my mind that we will have the pleasure of watching Kartal have these sorts of runs in the future," said former doubles player and Sky Sports Tennis' Colin Fleming.

"She is playing at such a high level and will get better."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player The match between Sonay Kartal and Maja Chwalinska in the Wuhan Open final started in style with this rally.

At 30 years old, Boulter is likely in the peak years of her career while Raducanu and Kartal should still have more to come.

For Kartal, her serve and ball-striking on both wings are two key areas which will need improvement if she's to become an established top player.

British tennis could benefit from an injury-free Raducanu and Kartal, both pushing each other on in 2027 because both have now shown tremendous potential, it's now a question of hitting those heights more consistently.

In the immediate future, Kartal may withdraw from this week's Japan Open in Osaka to recover from her Wuhan efforts before looking to conclude her season in one of the WTA 500 or WTA 250s in China, Hong Kong and India - all live on Sky Sports Tennis over the next three weeks.

"I had one goal with this Asian swing was to just defend the points that I did from last year and I've done better than that so it's set me up incredibly for next year and put me in a very good spot," said Kartal.

Sports.title: Dubois vs Itauma is a heavyweight rivalry for the future
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois and Moses Itauma could become the heavyweight rivalry to define British boxing in the years to come.

The sport in the UK has been dominated by the personalities and talents of Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury over the last decade. Although Fury and Joshua didn't box each other when they were both reigning world champions, they will finally fight in December in Cardiff.

That really will be a swansong bout for Fury and Joshua. While it's hard to imagine Dubois and Itauma matching the levels of fame Fury and AJ enjoyed, they can emulate them as two British rivals taking over the top of the heavyweight division.

They can also differ from Fury and AJ in a crucial regard - they don't have to leave actually fighting each other until the autumn of their careers. Both Dubois and Itauma are young, especially for heavyweights. Dubois is 29 years old and Itauma just 21.

They can fight in their primes, and they've got the time to box twice, even three times, in their careers if merited.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the IBF heavyweight world title fight between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic (Video courtesy of DAZN)

Dubois is riding high now. His two defeats to Oleksandr Usyk feel long distant after Dubois won an epic brawl in a first fight with Fabio Wardley to claim the WBO world title and most recently demolished Wardley in a rematch to defend the belt.

Itauma has to come back from defeat to Filip Hrgovic, a first professional loss for the fast-rising star.

Fighting for the IBF world title, Itauma outboxed Hrgovic, only to suddenly tire and unravel. Hrgovic, after absorbing punishment for eight rounds, stopped Itauma in the ninth.

Itauma now finds himself with questions to answer and a point to prove, just as Dubois did in his first career defeat when he took a knee against Joe Joyce in 2020.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After securing a TKO win over Itauma, Hrgovic offered his advice to the 21-year-old Brit and thinks it will be 'hard for anyone to beat him again' should he learn from the loss

Dubois is backing Itauma to come back and return to the heavyweight title picture.

"I hope so," Dubois said. "You need dance partners."

Frank Warren promotes both Dubois and Itauma. He believes Itauma will be improved by the defeat. "That's what makes you a better fighter," Warren said.

"He's 21 years of age. He'll have a comeback fight [in January] and I'm sure he'll come through it and then we'll look at all the various scenarios. But he'll want to be involved in it.

"What a great position that British boxing's in," Warren added. "This is not something that just happened overnight, we worked hard for this.

"We are on a mission to get these heavyweights under an umbrella but make the fights happen."

Sports.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun.

Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.

How do you solve what is, on revenue versus results, the worst-run club in world football? By changing the name of the latest patsy on the touchline, of course. For now a hard-fought point is perhaps enough to stave off that pre-programmed emergency response.

Stand down the cowboy cops. Call off the blue and white saloons. Although with a run of Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool next up in the league it will no doubt soon be time to go out there and arrest Lee Harvey Oswald again. What’s that you say? OK, well, dig him up again. Re-arrest him. Whatever it takes. Someone has to stop these lone gunmen, these managerial magic bullet merchants from derailing the Manchester United supremacy.

This was a dual-track football match between Leeds and Manchester United, on the face of it a good, even game between two teams of well-matched players. A 1-1 draw was fair in the end, although Leeds played well and probably should have won. But of course they won’t be the story.

Instead this game had already been billed as that familiar thing, a referendum on the future of Michael Carrick. A stay of execution for a week or two. Or another livestreamed firing squad for the Super Sunday cameras.

There has been a predictable sense of low comedy about Carrick’s own transformation in the United dugout this season. It was always going to be the case that his widely praised qualities in victory, blazer, T-shirt, jawline, inscrutable sense of calm, would become his fatal flaws in defeat.

Where’s the passion, the whirling arms, the range of tailored collars? At Elland Road Carrick simply looked drained in the second half as United were pegged back and overrun at times, the beard a little more ragged, the hair unkempt but still sweeping, the look of a brave, doomed tugboat captain resigned now to the approaching tsunami wave on the horizon.

A point leaves United 13th in the league and still struggling to reverse a dreadful start to the season. But it was a good game for two people. First for Carrick, who remains a million miles away from creating the problems afflicting this club, even if you accept that his presence as head coach is one of them.

Michael Carrick did not hire Michael Carrick. Getting rid of Michael Carrick is, by definition, not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. But it might just help to prolong them. Whatever his ultimate ceiling, it is surely worth keeping him just to try, for once, to do something different.

View image in fullscreen The Manchester United director of football, Jason Wilcox (centre), and chief executive officer Omar Berrada (right) watch on at Elland Road. Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA

This was also a good game for Lisandro Martínez, who went off injured at half-time with United 1-0 up, and who was also vindicated in his allegedly controversial (translation: entirely correct) comments on the club hierarchy in midweek.

United’s energetic first-half performance clarified one half of this. The players are committed in support of the manager, at least to the best of their ability. The second half made the other half of the argument, that this remains a mismatched, lopsided, cut-and-paste squad, always likely to be pulled apart by opponents as urgent as this Leeds team, which fully deserves its current seventh place in the table.

The problems are so obvious it is barely worth repeating them. But here goes. The third-richest club in the world played a second half with three of its back four out of position. Harry Maguire, signed under Ole Gunnar Solskjær, remains the best straight defender. But Maguire is also essentially a man-shaped solid wood armoire in a pair of shorts at this stage in his career, always the slowest person on any pitch, which means you will not be able to cover space, play a high line or counterattack without leaving yourself exposed to the counter-counter.

So good luck, guys. And remember Omar, who gave you this whisky bottle and loaded pistol of a squad, will be watching.

This was made painfully clear after half-time as Martínez went off and Noussair Mazraoui came on. Leeds scored an equaliser that felt structurally inevitable. They found space down their right side repeatedly. At times they seemed to be constantly peppering the seats behind the United goal, like a group of kids hammering a ball against a garage door. By the end Leeds had more possession, more shots on target and just looked a happier, better structured entity than the travelling heritage exhibit at the other end.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The key point here is to accept that all of this is entirely logical. This is not a mystery, a haunted house, a place of bad voodoo. Why do we talk about Manchester United so much? For obvious reasons. It’s a massive part of the English football landscape. Mainly, though, because this is a story of mind-bending waste, real-time elite-level incompetence played out on a weekly basis.

Yes, you could sack Michael Carrick. It won’t change much. Let’s destroy Eddie Howe for a bit instead. But the available evidence suggests every single person making executive decisions here is outmatched and outmanoeuvred.

There is a reason Manchester United feels like one of those high street legacy chain shops just before it collapses, piles of Quality Street by the door, a rat in the lingerie department, destined to become a pop-up vape shop run by Albanian money launderers. There’s a reason it feels so badly run. This is because: it is.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez, who criticised the Manchester United hierarchy in midweek, went off injured at half-time against Leeds. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

We know the Glazer ownership has zero interest in minding the details, that this has been a wonderful acquisition whatever the performance on the pitch, an asset supremely sweated. We know also that Sir Jim Ratcliffe is pub-level incoherent on the details he promised to fix. Remember when he was going to sit down and decide what the “style of football” would be? How’s that working out?

Instead Carrick is left shuffling a first XI acquired by endlessly revolving administrations. Here United had four defenders signed under Erik ten Hag, two Ruben Amorim recruits, two from the mist-shrouded age of Solskjær. No players were recruited under Ralf Rangnick, of course. But then Rangnick wanted to sign Erling Haaland, Luis Díaz, and Julian Álvarez, which all sounds far too sensible.

An organisation can be built with many hands. But not when so many of those hands appear to be so far from best in class it’s hard to work out which class they’re supposed to be attending. John Murtough, the former Manchester United football director, is currently director of global development at Atalanta, who have a 24,000-seat stadium and almost zero global presence. Meanwhile Berrada, the axeman, seems entirely invulnerable from the axe himself, despite the fact his job seems to orbit around resolving the consequences of his own mistakes.

United probably will sack their current manager before the year is out. This is the way this machine has to operate, always looking to buy itself, and those in the executive seats, a little more time on the payroll, an entity that has been hollowed out and allowed to rust, run on buzzwords and brown paper and string. Meanwhile, over to you Michael. We’ll see you next week, and maybe even the week after that, for more of exactly the same.

Sports.title: Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory
Sports.content:
The theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It was a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their own stadium this season. Arsenal, meanwhile, had drawn 0-0 on their previous two visits to this part of the east Midlands. They had only one win in five here.

Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full-throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the home support.

It was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions. Arsenal did not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot on target. How Noni Madueke made it count.

On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap holds off Ezri Konsa at the City Ground. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Forest refused to accept the inevitable. Chris Wood, on as a substitute, delayed too long and saw Rice block. Murillo, of all players, danced inside from the left and curled off target. Delap was denied at the death by a thunderous Ezri Konsa block tackle. But it did feel inevitable. Forest, who missed the injured Morgan Gibbs-White, might have played all night and not scored. Arsenal had not forgotten their previous away fixture – the 3-0 defeat at Brighton. It remains the only blot on their season.

Arsenal had kicked off six points behind Manchester City, who have been perfect on the field in the league this season. Will it matter when the sanctions for their rule breaches are meted out? All Arsenal can do is play the situation as it stands and this was an occasion when the result was everything.

Mikel Arteta’s team dominated the ball. As they were always likely to do. They were determined to be patient. And yet they were flat and predictable until the closing stages. The lack of incisive movement was glaring. That said, Forest were compact out of possession in a 5-4-1 formation and hard to break down. They were resolved not to give up any easy yards.

Arsenal played their patterns. They tried to suck the life out of the home crowd, working on the principle that it is difficult for fans to get animated if their team do not have the ball. The first half drifted by in a lazy Sunday afternoon haze, no shots on target for either side.

Delap carried the physical fight; the Forest centre-forward was a willing and direct runner and he won a free-kick off Rice just outside the Arsenal box on 44 minutes. Neco Williams thumped it at Bruno Guimarães, who went down and stayed down. The Forest support were unhappy at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. “Are you City in disguise?” they chanted.

View image in fullscreen Noni Madueke fires home – via a deflection – the only goal of the game. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Could a set piece provide the breakthrough? It felt the likeliest route. Murillo headed wide from a Forest corner in the 20th minute and was bloodied into the bargain; there was a whistle for a foul in the mass of bodies inside the six-yard box. At the other end, Kai Havertz headed over from a Rice free-kick on 37 minutes. He had a good look at the ball and was well-placed. It was a decent chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal have been a little barren in the first half this season. This was the seventh time in 10 matches since the Community Shield that they had failed to score in one. It has not been a problem. They needed to raise their levels for the second half.

Arteta’s first change was Madueke for Eberechi Eze on the left wing; an admission that the latter had failed to exert an influence. There was also a triple substitution on 66 minutes, the manager sending on Jurriën Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyökeres for Ben White, Guimarães and Havertz. He needed to shake things up because nothing was happening for his team. It was Forest who pushed after the restart, with Delap continuing to put himself about. He asked questions of Gabriel Magalhães, albeit the Arsenal defender tended to have the answers.

The minutes ticked down, the contest narrowing to a fine point and we waited to see whether there could be a moment, one big chance. Martin Ødegaard almost provided it in the 72nd minute when he released Timber with a lovely pass up the inside right. When he pulled back, Rice lifted wastefully high.

Glasner’s decision to introduce Ibrahim Sangaré for Dan Ndoye shortly afterwards was telling. Sangaré’s mission was to bolster the Forest midfield and yet he was slow to react to a half-cleared ball. When Rice played the pass, Madueke took over.

“We showed a champion spirit,” Madueke said. “Maybe last season, this game might not have gone for us. We have the extra belief and mentality.”

Sports.title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.

Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.

The concerning news for Sage, whose decision to field the teenager Honest Ahanor and 20-year-old Canvot in defence backfired spectacularly, is that two of his predecessors – Patrick Vieira and Roy Hodgson – were relieved of their jobs not long after losing against Brighton. Palace have conceded more goals than any other Premier League side this season and it is understood that there have been some disagreements behind the scenes since the Frenchman took over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, although it remains to be seen whether the chair, Steve Parish, will act on suggestions from the gleeful Brighton supporters during the second half that he will be sacked in the morning.

“It’s not my decision. I don’t know,” said Sage when asked if he will be given time to fix Palace’s leaky defence. “I will always give my best. I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face. My feeling after the game is shame.”

It was Hürzleler who was on the receiving end of that chant in February after Palace’s smash-and-grab victory on the south coast. How things have changed. His vibrant side now find themselves in the conversation for Champions League qualification and they have a squad that also looks capable of coping with the demands of European football.

View image in fullscreen Yasin Ayari’s deflected effort results in Brighton’s third goal. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

“The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism. It wasn’t easy,” said Hürzeler. “Now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud to beat Palace. I experienced some derbies and I’m part of this club, I’m part of the journey, that’s why I’m also part of the history. The players deserve it for the hard work they did in the last month because they really stuck together, they faced adversity. They were always there for each other.”

The usual hostility greeted the travelling fans after Sussex police had warned they would be deploying extra officers to deal with what remains very much a grudge match. But a torrential downpour before kick-off didn’t dampen Brighton’s desire for revenge. They tore into Palace’s inexperienced defence from the first whistle and Canvot was caught flat-footed as he headed a pinpoint free-kick from Pascal Gross past Walter Benítez.

The Palace goalkeeper could then only watch in horror when Olivier Boscagli fed Gómez on the halfway line after Adam Wharton had lost possession cheaply and the ball sailed over his head into the net after the sweetest of contacts. No wonder that Hürzeler has been urging his players to take more shots from long range this season – they were already the division’s top scorers with efforts from outside the box this season with four. Gómez’s strike from 51 metres was the Premier League goal from furthest out since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Things got even better for Brighton when a flowing move down the right allowed Kostoulas to tee up Ayari to sweep home via a deflection off the unfortunate Canvot. Sage looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up.

If he hoped things might improve after the break then he was mistaken. It took Kostoulas only four minutes to make it 4-0 after the ball deflected into his path after good work from Gross. To the delight of the Brighton fans, Jean-Philippe Mateta contrived to hit the crossbar with the goal gaping on his return from injury before Eddie Nketiah also fluffed the chance to grab a consolation.

Sage’s assistant, Paddy McCarthy, had to be held back from confronting the Brighton bench, with tempers threatening to spill over. Plenty of Palace fans had already seen enough by then as they made their escape after a nightmarish afternoon. They missed Hinshelwood scoring from close range six minutes from the end to round off the perfect afternoon for Hürzeler, who could not hide his emotion as he celebrated with his players at full time.

Sports.title: European football: 10-man Lyon hold off Nice to move top of Ligue 1
Sports.content:
Ten-man Lyon held on for a 2-1 comeback victory over Nice to move top of Ligue 1 on Sunday, as previous pacesetters Monaco lost for the first time this season. Five teams are level on 14 points at the top of the table with Lyon heading Paris Saint-Germain, Paris FC, Lille and Monaco on goal difference.

It was a close run affair for Lyon, playing in front of local boy and French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas, following Keito Nakamura’s dismissal 20 minutes from time.

Côte d’Ivoire forward Elye Wahi, who opened the scoring for Nice on 18 minutes with his second goal of the season, was denied a stoppage-time equaliser by a tight offside call.

Two goals in three minutes turned the game around by half-time as Pavel Sulc equalised by prodding home a rebound and Tanner Tessmann headed the hosts in front.

Veteran Belgium midfielder Axel Witsel headed against the bar early in the second half while Wahi hit the post with a close-range header, shortly after Nakamura was dismissed for a high boot.

Noah Cadiou’s second-half penalty for Lorient prevented Monaco returning to the top of Ligue 1 as they fell to a 1-0 defeat in Brittany on Sunday.

Finnish goalkeeper Lukas Hradecky dived the right way, but Cadiou placed his spot-kick into the corner, to hand Monaco their first league defeat of the season.

Monaco are one of five teams level on points at the top of the table as they were joined by Paris FC, who edged Rennes 4-3 thanks to Lassine Sinayoko’s injury-time penalty. Rennes dropped to fifth, a point behind, despite forward Estéban Lepaul’s hat-trick of penalties in Paris.

Marseille picked up a much-needed win as they thumped Angers 5-2 to pull away from the relegation zone. Le Havre remain rooted to the foot of the table as Cameroon forward Danny Namaso’s double helped Auxerre come away from Normandy with a 3-1 victory.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé blasts home Real Madrid’s third goal. Photograph: Ángel Martínez/Getty Images

Kylian Mbappé scored ⁠twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on ⁠La Liga leaders ⁠Barcelona ​to six points with a 4-1 home win over ⁠Sevilla on Sunday, a week ⁠before the rivals meet in el clásico.

Arda Guler ​opened the ‌scoring in the ‌30th minute, arrowing a shot ‌into the top corner from outside the box, before Mbappé added a second seven minutes later after a brilliant turn. Mbappé ‌then won and converted a penalty in the 63rd minute ​to effectively settle the contest.

Sevilla pulled one back with 10 minutes remaining through the substitute Manu Bueno, ⁠but Yan Diomandé restored Real’s three-goal ​lead ​with a thunderous ​strike two minutes later.

An early penalty from Ante Budimir and a late Asier Osambela goal from earned Osasuna a 2-0 win against Racing Santander while Celta Vigo won 2-1 at home against Alavés.

Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick combined to score two goals as Bayer Leverkusen came from behind to beat in-form Freiburg 2-1 in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

After a shock defeat to promoted Elversberg in the season opener, Leverkusen have now picked up 13 of a possible 18 points and sit fourth, level with third-placed Freiburg – who host Bayern Munich next weekend – on points.

Rock bottom Borussia Mönchengladbach are still searching for a first point of the season after losing 2-1 at home against fellow strugglers Hoffenheim.

Hoffenheim’s Bambasé Conté opened the scoring with his second goal in two games since a surprise call-up to the Germany squad in October. Wael Mohya levelled for the hosts just after the break, but Alexander Prass put Hoffenheim back in front shortly afterwards as the visitors, who host Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday, won just their second game of the season.

View image in fullscreen Patrik Schick scores Bayer Leverkusen’s winner. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

Lazio’s Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen ⁠scored in a 3-0 ⁠win over ​Juventus on Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter at the top of Serie A.

Provstgaard broke the deadlock in the ⁠37th minute, using his height to glance home Mattia Zaccagni’s cross after Lazio worked a short corner on the left.

Fellow Dane Isaksen doubled the lead in ⁠the 66th minute, collecting a pass from Nuno Tavares on the right before shifting the ball onto ​his left foot and bending a low ‌finish into the far ‌corner.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, launching a counterattack from inside his own ‌half and driving into the box before slotting home a low finish as frustrated home supporters jeered their side through to the final whistle.

Cesc Fàbregas’s Como ended their three-game winless streak in Serie A on Sunday with a 3-1 victory at lowly Fiorentina.

First-half goals by Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz put the visitors in charge, before Marin Pongracic halved the deficit shortly before the interval. Anastasios Douvikas netted early in the second period to put to bed any hope of a Fiorentina comeback and keep the hosts locked in the relegation zone on four points.

Milan leapfrogged Como into fourth as they survived a second-half comeback from Atalanta to win 3-2. Goals from Gonçalo Ramos, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila put Milan 3-0 ahead after 58 minutes before Atalanta rallied through Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic.

Earlier, Lecce won 3-0 at Udinese, with Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N’Dri and Jamil Siebert all finding the net.

Sports.title: James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again
Sports.content:
Two goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.

It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.

James’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.

On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”

Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.

View image in fullscreen Lauren James squeezes in Chelsea’s opener from the tightest of angles. Photograph: John Walton/PA

The bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.

If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.

“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: City hold off Brighton to maintain 100% record Show Manchester City held off a spirited fightback from Brighton to close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League. Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles. Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea. London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control. Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left. Manchester United are up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1. Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark. Aston Villa stunned faltering Liverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal. Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half as West Ham defeated Crystal Palace 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“When you’re on top and you concede that second, the way we conceded, from our possession, then that deflates you maybe as a group a little bit. But we have to recover quickly psychologically.”

It was not so much a Spurs collapse as Chelsea putting their foot on the gas, channelling any anger and frustration felt at a less than dominant first-half performance into one full of gut-busting intensity in the second half. Just before the hour Bompastor’s side retook the lead, when Alyssa Thompson surged into the penalty area from the left before sending an angled cutback for the arriving Carpenter to power in.
