Four minutes later James extended their lead, collecting the ball from Lucy Bronze in the centre circle before she powered towards goal, wrongfooted Koga and curled an effort past Lize Kop.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea retake the lead in the second half thanks to Ellie Carpenter’s first goal. Photograph: John Walton/PA

“It’s a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,” Bompastor said of James. “I’m pleased, but I want to highlight the team performance. When the individuals are performing it’s because the team is performing as well and the players around her are doing the job for her to express her quality on the ball.”

Chelsea’s fourth was equally as stylish; Keira Walsh flicked the ball to Nüsken and she blasted a rising strike home six minutes after coming on.

Hamano found herself in acres of space for the fifth, sending a curling shot into the top corner. Walsh was at fault for Spurs’ late second, waiting too long to receive a pass which Gaupset pounced on and then fired a low effort past Hannah Hampton. Unwilling to let the game finish on a down note, Carpenter swapped the ball from her left foot to her right as she turned and fired in her second.

It was a chaotic finish to an end‑to‑end match, as Chelsea continue to assert their status as serious title contenders.

Sports.title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland
Sports.content:
Bournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for a Premier League win is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast.

Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity, Sunderland were sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” the Sunderland manager said. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened.

There was mitigation on offer. With a tight turnaround from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, Wearside resources are stretched and their European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale continues, a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day‑to‑day operations. On the pitch, Sunderland have not had a league win since August, and lost four in succession.

Both teams had made five changes from Thursday and Bournemouth, who had beaten Sturm Graz at home, were visibly fresher. “Fatigue for me is not an issue,” Le Bris said. “We just have to get used to it.”

Granit Xhaka’s early stumble prefaced a jet-lagged, error-strewn performance that followed Sunderland’s first European away game since 1973. After Lewis Cook dabbed the ball forward, Evanilson seized on a collective muddle between Danso and Omar Alderete. The Brazilian’s reputation for unselfishness was deepened by his next choice of action. Instead of shooting, he laid up a diving Marcus Tavernier to head home. “I was waiting for him to shoot but he can see more than you and me,” Rose said.

“Exactly the situation we wanted to avoid,” Le Bris said, and Danso’s exit swiftly made things worse. Evanilson again escaped beyond a dallying defender exposed by Alderete ducking away from the ball. Clumsiness served as no defence. Craig Pawson, the referee, could reach no decision other than sending the Austrian for an early sachet of shower gel.

View image in fullscreen Marcus Tavernier points the way after scoring Bournemouth’s first goal. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

Being a goal and a man up represented a challenge to Bournemouth; they had previously conceded nine points from winning positions. First‑half chances piled up, Robin Roefs repeatedly asked to bail out bungling defenders. “If you have one player more you have to use the momentum,” Rose said.

With pressure piling on, the season lurching, Le Bris can only fight with the players available. Brian Brobbey, on the bench in Portugal following injury on international duty, was missing altogether from the matchday squad. “We decided not to rush the process,” Le Bris said. Timur Tutierov, loaned last season to Exeter, chased autumnal shadows before a merciful substitution on 59 minutes.

On the sidelines Rose, who revealed last week that he had binge‑watched Sunderland ’Til I Die on Netflix, kicked every ball. His need for three points was implicit. With the Vitality Stadium modernising fast, fans sitting in new-build corner stands, relegation battles cannot be countenanced. The second goal was accompanied by a collective sigh of relief, arriving via more Sunderland benevolence. Evanilson, assisted by Alderete’s brain-fog backpass, supplied a hip swivel of which Rudolf Nureyev might have been proud, sitting Roefs down to slot into an empty net. “I am happy that he rewarded himself with a goal,” Rose said of his No 9. “He is always working hard for the team.”

View image in fullscreen Kevin Danso brings down Evanilson before being shown a red card by referee Craig Pawson. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Bournemouth signed off with 29 shots. If thoughts understandably drifted to Thursday and Milan, seven-time European champions, coming to Dorset, Rose would not allow his players to be distracted. Though Sunderland enjoyed a late, brief spell of pressure, Bournemouth calmly collected a win that capped a historic week in club history. “It felt very clear, after [the 5-1 defeat on Friday against] Chelsea we were waiting for this game,” Rose said. “I am settling in well, I love the region. It’s a pleasure to work here. Everyone here stays patient and I really appreciate it.”

For Le Bris, any European success will only be a sticking plaster. “It’s hard to fix without a specific pattern,” he said, lamenting many mistakes. “It wasn’t the best version of Sunderland.”

Two clubs facing similar challenges appear on different trajectories.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Osmand and Nygren at the double as Celtic thrash Hearts 7-1
Sports.content:
Callum Osmand was on target again as Celtic inflicted more misery on Hearts with a 7-1 thrashing at Parkhead.

Osmand netted twice in three first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.

The Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.

Camilo Durán piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear of Rangers.

Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.

They produced 20 shots at goal, one of which found the net from Laurent Mendy, but Celtic were far superior in the final third and benefited from some extremely slack defending.

Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park on Saturday. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.

Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Fink gives Dundee the lead against Rangers from close range. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Motherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”

Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a 1-1 draw at St Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.

The Argentina international was taken to hospital after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during the second half of Saturday’s game at Hill Dickinson Stadium. We’ll be back in a few weeks.” Mike Penders is set to deputise in Martínez’s absence. The 21-year-old made his Premier League debut as a substitute against Everton. 18h ago 07.25 EDT Donald McRae “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” But there’s sadness, too, in the way his life and career were scarred by his refusal to wear the poppy when playing games around Remembrance Sunday in England. “It’s completely changed me as a person,” McClean says. “It’s made me a bit of a recluse because I don’t trust a lot of people now. I’ve been stung bad.” McClean’s autobiography, The Walls, is one of the best sports books of the year. It’s a powerful and sometimes disturbing read elevated by McClean’s willingness to show himself in an unflattering light. 21h ago 04.48 EDT From the archive: Leeds United v Man Utd classics double quotation mark Leeds United 1-0 Manchester United (FA Cup semi-final replay, 31 March 1965); Leeds United 0-1 Manchester United (Division One, 17 April 1965) Here’s where the stags really begin to rut. Don Revie’s side, freshly promoted, were on course for the Double. Only problem was, so were Matt Busby’s men. The pair were drawn in the semi-final of the FA Cup, and spent 90 minutes at Hillsborough kicking seven colours out of each other, Jack Charlton, Billy Bremner, Nobby Stiles, Denis Law and Paddy Crerand enjoying themselves like the proverbial pigs. Good luck if you found yourself in the middle of that. Brouhahas broke out on the terraces as well, and did so again four days later during the replay at the City Ground. The on-field behaviour was much improved, though. According to Big Jack, Manchester United put on a performance as stylish and dangerous as they ever were under Busby, but Leeds somehow held on, wrested the ascendency, and nicked it in the last minute, Bremner twisting in mid-air to steer home an outrageous curling header. Bremner was missing 18 days later when Manchester United came to Elland Road in the league. Had they won, Leeds would have gone five clear at the top with four games left. They went into the game as favourites, Busby’s side having failed to find the net against Leeds in both Cup games and the earlier league match at Old Trafford, which the visitors won 1-0. That particular lean spell ended after 14 minutes – or 284, if you like – when John Connelly drove home. Leeds failed to respond, despite the best efforts of the newly crowned Football Writers’ player of the year, Bobby Collins, and went down again in their next Bremner-less match, a 3-0 hosing at Sheffield Wednesday. Busby’s third great side won their first title; Revie’s team, not quite ready yet, lost the Cup final as well. Even on Tuesday at Anfield, he will not: into his 30th year, the longest presidency in Europe, that is about the only thing that hasn’t changed. More than 1,000 games and still it happens. “I don’t get nervous. It’s worse: I get worried, very anxious,” he says. “I suffer a lot. “It’s emotional to play Liverpool. This will be the fifth time we have faced them, the third at Anfield. The other two were European semi-finals. I’ll watch the morning training session, travel with the team. We’ll go and eat; everywhere we go we get treated very well and we treat them well back. The next day I’ll watch the under-19s in the morning, that I do like. And then the game, which I don’t. 21h ago 04.21 EDT Dominic Booth If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics last season was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell. Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction and relegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted. The problem is the Dansons have been unable to find an ambitious buyer to take the club to the next level. Now the prospect of a first season in the fourth tier since 1996-97 is a distinct possibility, although victory against Reading – the Latics’ second league win of the campaign, sealed by Scott Hogan’s 71st-minute strike – made the picture a little rosier. 22h ago 03.28 EDT Jonathan Wilson The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” This was everything Sunderland fans could have wished for from their first European away game in 53 years and more. They had seen other fans experience these things, and now they could tick off the checklist: complicated travel to a pretty foreign town they would otherwise never visit, a fussy Albanian referee and a great sense of togetherness and community. There was even an injury-time winner from, miracle of miracles, Noah Sadiki. Ask any of the 5,000 or so Wearsiders who made the trip to Portugal if the Europa League was worth it and the answer would be unanimous. Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Brighton fans would surely say something similar: European football, especially for clubs who are unfamiliar with it, is a joy and an adventure. It generates experiences that will be remembered for ever, and if the cost is that the risk of relegation goes up, that’s a price worth paying. Others at those clubs may see things differently. Sports.title: Pierre Sage at risk of becoming first Premier League manager sacked: Crystal Palace chiefs concerned amid strained relationships
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage at risk of becoming first Premier League manager sacked: Crystal Palace chiefs concerned amid strained relationships

Pierre Sage is under growing pressure at Crystal Palace and could become the first Premier League manager sacked this season after an embarrassing 5-0 defeat against rivals Brighton.

Palace chiefs have raised concerns about Sage’s defensive approach for several weeks and considered sacking him in September but a goalless draw against Leeds bought him more time.

However, the backline continues to ring alarm bells at Selhurst Park, leaving Sage’s position at risk.

Palace have the worst defensive record in the league, conceding 17 goals in seven Premier League games.

The French coach is also understood to have a strained relationship with key decision-makers, who doubt his defensive methods.

The Daily Mail previously reported that his decision to bench Jaydee Canvot after a bad game irked chairman Steve Parish.

Pierre Sage said he didn't know how long he would be given to turn things round at Palace

Speaking after Palace’s 5-0 defeat at Brighton, Sage was unsure whether he would be given more time in the job.

‘I don’t know,’ Sage said when asked if he would keep his job. ‘I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face for this club against this other club and we are not at the level we expected.

‘I am really sorry for that because I know how important it is for them. We didn’t show that today. It was really important for us too. We didn’t understand in which context this game was played.

‘I will always give my best. When we lose, I’m really frustrated, but I always take the lesson and try to change things. But it’s the same when I win because I know we can improve.

‘I don’t want to accept the level of the moment if we can do better. Today the work is really important to do and I will do it. It’s my job and I like to change this kind of thing.’

Sports.title: Inside Tottenham's Marbella training camp: Why Roberto De Zerbi chose base after his pre-season preparations were disrupted, his need for secrecy and their Anthony Joshua encounter
Sports.content:
Inside Tottenham's Marbella training camp: Why Roberto De Zerbi chose base after his pre-season preparations were disrupted, his need for secrecy and their Anthony Joshua encounter

Marbella was in the grip of a murder mystery as Tottenham descended for the sunshine training camp they hope will transform their season.

Alexander Aslani, a Ferrari-driving cosmetic surgeon with a reputation as a butt lift expert, had been gunned down amid allegations of a contract killing taken out by a disgruntled patient.

Shockwaves rippled through the gated communities of the Golden Mile and the designer stores, the golf clubs and marina bars.

Roberto De Zerbi, however, was there in search of a different sort of surgery. More of a tactical nip and tuck. Maybe a little something to perk up his team.

Just enough to lift them out of trouble at the bottom of the Premier League.

The Spurs boss wanted the sort of dedicated training operation he felt he had been denied in pre-season, when a tour heavy with commercial obligations in Australia and New Zealand, combined with players filtering back from the World Cup, interfered with his preparations.

Tottenham spent a few days in Marbella last week as part of a training camp after their difficult start to the season

Although it was an intense trip with no distractions, the Spurs squad met with Anthony Joshua

De Zerbi demanded no distractions in Spain. His team, he made it clear, would be going there simply to work and be together at a luxury retreat on the Costa del Sol west of Marbella, towards Estepona.

The Hacienda del Mar is newly refurbished and reopened this summer as part of the Melia Collection, boasting an ‘oasis of calm, authenticity and elegance’, lush sub-tropical gardens and views over the Mediterranean Sea towards Gibraltar and Morocco.

Marbella has become a training camp haven, with its feel-good warmth and elite facilities.

The Marbella Football Center at La Quinta is a regular destination for Europe’s top clubs and national associations with 300 teams per year descending on its 38 pitches, gyms and massage areas.

De Zerbi’s former club Marseille booked in there twice last season, a week after he had departed in February and again in April.

At Spurs, the Italian has been at pains to keep everything tightly under wraps.

No footage has appeared on the club’s own media channels. Nor on the social media accounts of the players who are there, although a group photo did emerge online after the squad’s visit to Anthony Joshua’s gym as he prepares for December’s long-awaited heavyweight fight against Tyson Fury.

Tonight’s game against Coventry City has taken on a vital edge. Only six games into the Premier League campaign yet Spurs are winless and propping up the table.

Coventry have won two in a row and no longer look like the whipping boys they did at the start of the season.

Frank Lampard has his own history with Spurs. He did not lose many against them during his stellar playing career with London rivals Chelsea.

Now, he has the Sky Blues up and running and is sure to prey on the anxieties of Spurs at home, where they have won only two league games in the last 12 months.

If De Zerbi’s team look at any stage as if they might fail to beat Coventry, the mood will quickly sour inside the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

There were positive signs for Spurs at Manchester United, however, with a spirited fightback and a late equaliser — despite finishing the game with ten men because Rodrigo Bentancur failed the ‘No Red Cards ’til Marbs’ challenge.

De Zerbi claimed afterwards it was the first time he had seen his players show they were ‘a team’ and promised to build on this foundation in Marbella. They flew out after training in London on Tuesday.

De Zerbi values conversations and the bonding experience of a communal meal. He does not usually mind if his players want to drink wine or beer.

He referred to alcohol as ‘good medicine’ at the end of last season when Spurs were fighting relegation and he took them out to high-end restaurant Bacchanalia in Mayfair.

The trip gave De Zerbi more time to work with some of his new signings like Sandro Tonali

There will have been down-time and golf in Marbella but he is unlikely to have let his players out on the lash. De Zerbi’s mind is rarely on anything other than football.

For him, the most critical aspect of these days in Spain will have been to have the luxury of undisturbed time with his players, to work tactically on the grass and to reflect together in meetings and analysis sessions.

Twice during his two seasons at Brighton, he took his players away to Dubai.

First during the World Cup in Qatar in 2022 when the focus was on training rather than bonding. They came home and took 14 points from the next seven games. Spurs would happily

Sports.title: The unsustainable trend and underlying deficiency Arsenal have to address if they're to keep winning - and why Eberechi Eze being Mikel Arteta's fall guy is a worrying case of deja-vu, writes ISAAN KHAN
Sports.content:
Pass, pass and pass them to submission.

Arsenal had enjoyed over 70 per cent of possession in the first period but, bar a Kai Havertz effort at Matt Sels’ near post, barely created a chance.

They improved in the second half. Yet for a team of reigning champions, more is expected, particularly against a Nottingham Forest side who were on a two-match losing streak; make it three now.

The comfort of an Arsenal bench worth in excess of £300million helps of course, these riches once again prising a match open.

Bruno Guimaraes did so against Leeds, coming on to score after a poor first hour for the Gunners. The three substitutions of Bukayo Saka, Havertz and Martin Odegaard against Lille cut Arsenal loose midweek in the Champions League, 3-0 the final scoreline.

Here against Forest, Noni Madueke replaced Eberechi Eze at half-time, before Viktor Gyokeres, Mikel Merino and Jurrien Timber entered the fray on 66 minutes.

Arsenal's £300million bench bailed them out again against Nottingham Forest - but the victories are masking an underlying deficiency

Arsenal haven't scored in the first half for six games in a row and are not clinical enough despite their pretty football

The strength of Mikel Arteta’s bench is well documented, their second XI arguably strong enough to compete for a top-four spot.

It’s Arsenal’s recent style of play which results have masked, an underlying deficiency defying the 10 victories of their 11 matches across all competitions.

Madueke’s match-winning strike on 80 minutes was Arsenal’s first — and only — shot on target in the match. The last time Arteta’s side failed to register a shot on target within the first 70 minutes of a fixture dates back to October 2023.

It ties into their goalscoring patterns more generally, unable to score in the first half for a sixth consecutive game. This isn’t sustainable, no matter the talent or depth on offer. Afterwards when asked if he had any concerns over Arsenal’s inability to score earlier in matches, Arteta’s response was telling.

‘We knew today we wouldn't score in the first 20-30 minutes,’ he said.

’We were going to face a different Forest because they're extremely well covered. They put a Christmas tree (3-4-1-2) there. There's no space to play.’We didn't even hit the target, which is the difference. I had the belief that the moment the physical level was going to drop, the spaces would be a little bit bigger. And then we have to suffer.’

A Christmas tree-style defence or not, the Spaniard’s words glossed over Arsenal’s inability to create chances.

Forest, like many teams when facing the Gunners, settled to ceding possession and soaking up the pressure. They played well for large swathes, spearheaded by Liam Delap who charged around and caused both Gabriel and Ezri Konsa plenty of problems.

Nottingham Forest sat off and let Arsenal have most of the ball - and for much of the match, they kept the Gunners at bay

Stronger opposition may punish them before Mikel Arteta has a chance to change the game

His physicality pinned back the centre backs, as he kept looking to make those bulldozing runs straight through the backline.

Going back to Arteta’s words, he banked on Forest getting tired and his players subsequently making the opposition pay. It worked, Madueke’s shot deflecting in on off a Forest player. Still, Arsenal are capable of so much more.

They have the talents to dominate games both in possession — and score more goals.

In fairness, a 1-0 victory is the same value of a wider scoreline. It’s the need to strike earlier in matches, preferably in the first half, which Arteta’s men must address sooner rather than later.

Otherwise, stronger opposition will be less forgiving.

Big weeks ahead for Eze

It’s not the first time Eze has been Arteta’s fall guy.

Rewind back to Aston Villa away in December 2025. The England man had lost Matty Cash in the build-up to Villa’s opening goal.

A lack of tracking back by any frontline player is a cardinal sin under Arteta. Eze didn’t have a great half on that night, mind, though the infringement was enough to send him to the bench.

Eze played the next game against Wolves before having to wait two months for his next league start against Brentford in February.

The attacker has fallen down the pecking order of late, to Madueke and Christos Tzolis, making Forest away so crucial for him.

With Tzolis injured, Eze started on the left wing for his first league start of the season — before being substituted at half-time, mirroring the forward’s exit at Villa.

The next few weeks could prove crucial to Eberechi Eze - and Arteta needs to manage him well

One of his last actions before being hooked off this time saw Eze pass the ball out near the corner flag. Before that, he just couldn’t get going, losing the ball a few times to Arteta’s clear frustration on the touchline.

A lack of confidence in general could be sensed as he tried to work the ball forward. It shouldn’t be a surprise owing to his circumstances.

This was Eze’s first league start of the season, a chance presented from Tzolis’ injury and Madueke sitting on the bench after an indifferent start to the campaign.

The pressure of needing to perform, knowing another league start maybe otherwise be far away, is psychologically challenging to say the least.

The burden is real for a player who will likely feel aggrieved at being the only Arsenal player to come off at the break, in arguably a telling statement by Arteta.

How the Spaniard manages him in these coming weeks will be crucial for the prospects of a man who possesses much talent but is in dire need of an arm around the shoulder.

The opposite could well be detrimental.

Sports.title: Match Of The Day star Kelly Cates can't wipe the smile off her face as she and boyfriend Mark Chapman are seen together for the first time since their romance was confirmed

Kelly Cates couldn't wipe the smile off her face as she walked alongside her beaming boyfriend Mark Chapman on Sunday.

It was confirmed earlier this month that the Match Of The Day pundits were dating after finding love together on the BBC show last year.

And this weekend the pair were seen together for the first time since their romance was confirmed as they arrived at work for MOTD.

Kelly, 51, looked in great spirits as she kept it stylish in a pale pink loose-fitted shirt and dark grey tailored trousers.

Meanwhile Mark, 53, wrapped up in a cream zip up fleece and dark navy jacket.

The couple were seen smiling and laughing together as Kelly pushed her suitcase along the street.

Sports.title: After nearly seven years of being Man United's main man is the time drawing near when Bruno Fernandes will have to pass on that mantle? His display vs Leeds was a microcosm of his season, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
After nearly seven years of being Man United's main man is the time drawing near when Bruno Fernandes will have to pass on that mantle? His display vs Leeds was a microcosm of his season, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Even by the usual level of animosity directed towards Bruno Fernandes at away grounds around the country, this was brutal in the extreme.

‘Bruno is a ****,’ echoed the chant around Elland Road as the Leeds fans spewed their bile towards the Manchester United captain, enraged by an ugly lunging tackle on Tarik Muharemovic that earned Fernandes an early yellow card and had the natives baying for red.

It is to his credit that he led from the front for the remaining 73 minutes without giving them any more opportunities to implore referee Darren England to send him off in a full-blooded fixture that doesn’t allow players to hold anything back.

Fernandes is used to it by now. He rarely takes the bait from rival supporters, preferring to answer his critics by hitting their team where it hurts.

You would have bet on the Bruno of old having the final word at Elland Road. But he didn’t, just as he has failed to have a meaningful impact in most of United’s 10 games so far this season.

His four goals and one assist have come in his team’s only two wins, against Ipswich Town and Sabah at Old Trafford, two of the easier fixtures it has to be said.

Bruno Fernandes' superpowers have largely deserted him - his days of being Manchester United's main man look numbered

In past seasons he may have had the final word in this sort of match at Elland Road - not now

Otherwise the superpowers that earned the Portugal star the PFA and FWA Player of the Year awards with nine goals and a Premier League record 21 assists have largely deserted him.

It was a familiar story on Sunday as Fernandes reached into his box of tricks and came up empty-handed yet again.

He is not good at hiding his emotions at the best of times, and we were treated to the full repertoire of arm-throwing and grumbling (mainly at Diogo Dalot) as he searched in vain for inspiration.

Afterwards, it was put to Michael Carrick that Fernandes’ body language wasn’t the best. ‘No, he was absolutely fine today, don't worry,’ smiled United’s head coach, accustomed by now to answering questions specifically about his captain in most press conferences.

Fernandes might be fine, but the fact that Carrick has felt the need to move him out of the No.10 position he has made his own tells its own story.

Against Atletico Madrid in midweek, he played wide on the right, allowing Youri Tielemans to push forward from midfield and play No.10. The Belgian performed well enough to stay there against Leeds, and set up the opening goal for Bryan Mbeumo while Fernandes started side left and inter-changed with Mbeumo at centre-forward.

‘Today, he pretty much played where he has been playing for the most part, through the middle of the pitch, so there wasn't really too much change,’ added Carrick.

‘He played a slightly different position in midweek, but apart from that it's pretty much as usual, you know. And he's an important part of our team, Bruno. He has been for us for some time, and that's not changing.’

Youri Tielemans deserves to start against Como in the Champions League on Wednesday

Michael Carrick has been asked if Fernandes is undroppable - he may soon feel pressured to bench him

Maybe not but, on this evidence, Tielemans deserves to continue against Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. Matheus Cunha is another who can play at No.10 but has had to work around Fernandes.

Until now, that has been beyond question. His stats spoke for themselves. But Carrick was asked in Madrid if Fernandes is undroppable and the noise around him is only going to grow louder.

After nearly seven years of being United’s main man is the time drawing near when he will have to pass on that mantle?

The Old Trafford hierarchy were certainly open to that idea when Al-Hilal came calling last year with the offer of a £100million transfer fee and untold riches for Fernandes himself.

The player decided to stay despite admitting that he was ‘hurt’ by the club’s willingness to let him go, and it paid off with an incredible season leading into last summer’s World Cup.

This year, Galatasaray tried their luck and were prepared to double Fernandes’ wages. Again, he stayed, showing admirable loyalty to a club who are no nearer winning the Premier League than when he walked through the door from Sporing Lisbon in January 2020.

It would be a shame if Fernandes’ time at Old Trafford yielded only a FA Cup and Carabao Cup, but that might well be as good as it gets.

The 32-year-old will be out of contract at the end of June, although United have the option to extend it by another 12 months. Talks over a new deal have started, but there is no sign of a breakthrough anytime soon. On current form, would United want to renew?

In a summer that saw United offload Casemiro but fail to find a buyer for Marcus Rashford, would it have been better to have moved their other big earner off the books, particularly with Tielemans coming in?

Time will tell. Fernandes’ track record tells you that the loss of form is only temporary and it won’t be long before he proves the doubters wrong. That Tielemans’ ownership of the No.10 spot is shortlived and Fernandes will soon be back pulling the strings like he always does.

The longer this goes on, though, the louder the questions will grow – and the more people will wonder if one of the few great United careers in the post-Ferguson era is drawing to a close.

Sports.title: Journey to Wembley: Halifax reach first round in a beloved stadium they may soon lose - as ambitious South Shields' FA Cup dreams fizzle out for another year
Sports.content:
Journey to Wembley: Halifax reach first round in a beloved stadium they may soon lose - as ambitious South Shields' FA Cup dreams fizzle out for another year

FA Cup Fourth Qualifying Round: FC Halifax 3-2 South Shields

There is not even a sign carrying the club’s name on the exterior walls of FC Halifax’s famous old stadium, which the council wants to sell, but memories of knocking a star-studded Manchester City side out of the FA Cup in 1980 are providing sustenance in tough times, an hour before kick-off on Saturday afternoon.

One of the Halifax Town directors back then, Andrew Hodgson, is remembering being part of the small group, including City manager Malcolm Allison, who gathered with the referee for an inspection of the half-frozen, half-boggy pitch on which the then-Fourth Division side triumphed 1-0.

‘The game should never have been played,’ Hodgson relates, over his beer in the supporters’ bar. ‘But Mal Allison wanted it to be played. Insisted it should be played. City were that cocky. So convinced that they didn’t even need a good pitch to beat us on. We thought all our birthdays had come at once. Great days.’

We are here in Halifax, west Yorkshire, with South Shields, on the sixth instalment of our journey to Wembley told through all 13 rounds, following a club as far as they go and then picking up with the team who knock them out, all the way to the final. And though the team from the Tyneside coast are 20 places and one league lower than their hosts, they are the ones with all the ambition now.

With their directors as they draw up here is American investment banker Gordon McBean, who is helping Shields access US capital markets. ‘There is a huge appetite in the US for the Cinderella stories of clubs from working class places,’ McBean says. ‘But it takes money and capital to grow.’

Shields have just spent another week in the maelstrom of activity that is accompanying the arrival of their new Chinese/American ownership consortium.

Halifax knocked South Shields out in a 3-2 thriller to reach the FA Cup first round - a boon amid fears that the council will sell off their stadium

Supporters raise funds for the club to buy equipment by selling merchandise

When we drop into the club, a few days out from this fourth qualifying round FA Cup tie, a Chinese executive currently providing commercial expertise is hot desking with other staff in a small meeting room overlooking the pitch. A lunchtime in the company of Shields manager Mike Williamson takes place against the din of builders creating a new reception area at the training ground.

The discussion with Williamson centres on Shields’ ambitions to develop players who have not made it at nearby Newcastle United, Sunderland and Middlesbrough’s academies, and the former Magpies defender certainly brings nuance to how that might happen. ‘Some lads are so full of fear that it stops them working hard. It looks like they don’t care when they do — but that’s just a self-protection mechanism,’ he says.

‘They’re so scared of failing that if they invest their whole life and fail, they feel far more vulnerable. They don’t realise that if you don’t give your everything you will always have an excuse. That’s the toughest part — the lads who never really fulfil it. It’s not always a question of lads not being good enough.’

He speaks from the perspective of a football career which saw him play at every level from Shields’ current tier to the Premier League and face rejection and criticism along the way.

This all feels a million miles away from the reality of FC Halifax, the club formed in 2008 just a month after Halifax Town were wound up. There was an acceleration up through the non-leagues, but the Shay looks a careworn place now, and it is the fans who are keeping the spirit alive.

This is the first stadium on our journey which has lacked its own official club shop but the Supporters’ Club have been providing a ‘pop up’ one for the past few years, selling everything from darts shirts, school satchels and ‘Spirit of the Shay’ gin, produced by a local distillery, from a storage space beneath the main stand. The proceeds go towards buying equipment for the team, from winter coats to training ground covers.

‘We ask the coaching staff what they need and settle the invoice,’ says Phil Merrifield, Supporters’ Club vice-chairman whose wife, Lesley, is among a group of five people helping him out. ‘It’s good to have this space,’ he adds. ‘For a long time, we had to load it in and out of our car. We live out in Doncaster so it’s a long way to bring it.’

The evidence of how much this means to the playing staff is self-evident. Manager John McGrath, kit man Mark Bett and goalkeeping coach Jon Stewart all call in to express their gratitude as they arrive for this game. McGrath’s players wave as they walk past.

Halifax fans are proud of their club, who are regulars in the National League play-offs

South Shields have big ambitions under an arriving Chinese/American ownership consortium, but their FA Cup journey has come to an end

Managers Mike Williamson (left, South Shields) and John McGrath (right, Halifax) shake hands

In the club bar, there are groans as it emerges that a match programme will not be published for the game, though the far greater concern is the jeopardy surrounding the club’s future at this iconic old ground, where Paul Hendrie’s 78th-minute goal in the mud sank City.

Calderdale Council wanted to sell it to the owner of the Huddersfield Giants rugby league team and though campaigners staved that off, there are now two other private bidders. The club’s owner, Leeds-based businessman David Bosomworth, whose investment on the playing side has kept the club competitive in the fifth tier, is not among them.

A tantalising reminder of how precious a big Cup run looks like was dangled in front of South Shields just a week ago when they arrived for their league match at Macclesfield. Home supporters were still wearing their half-and-half scarves from last winter’s third-round giant-killing against Crystal Palace. But Shields surrendered a 3-1 lead to lose 4-3 that afternoon and were outmuscled.

They carry their town’s motto — ‘Always Ready’ — wherever they go, but their technical game, prioritising passing through the lines above physicality, is by no means flawless. Aerially, they are vulnerable.

For all that strategic direction and focus, it is little less than a thumping for the first 45 minutes against Halifax. Conor Carty, the 24-year-old Irish striker signed this summer, heads the home side ahead from Connor Douglas’ cross. That Shields aerial weakness again.

Max Bardell poaches a second from close range and barely 20 minutes in, Carty has contributed a third. It might have been five at the interval, by which time Ben Tollitt has crashed a shot against a post.

Shields’ former Leicester City academy player Toby Onanaye adds such spirit when arriving from the bench that you wonder why he did not start. He scores spectacularly, after team-mate Cedwyn Scott’s goal has brought Shields back into it.

But it is an emphatic win for a side whose player budget has been in the bottom quartile of the National League these past few years. So much lies up ahead for South Shields, who we leave behind after a month on this journey.

A good FA Cup run can boost the finances of a lower-league club for seasons to come

Non-league players often balance the demands of football with other jobs, though the fifth tier is mostly professionalised

Home supporters enjoying a chat during the half-time break as Halifax beat South Shields 3-2

The ribbon was cut only last week on a cafe, called The Coal Face, which their charitable community foundation has opened at the Harton and Westoe Miners Welfare building, site of an old colliery pithead, which co-owner Geoff Thompson has saved from redevelopment.

The miners’ sanctuary is alive and thriving once more and the foundation has generated £45million in revenue for the community in the past five years.

A promotional film about the club has been developed to stimulate creative interest as the Shields’ owners look to put its story before audiences in China or the US.

Tyneside musician Jade Thirlwall, the former Little Mix singer and successful solo artist, wants to help and will look to do so as she arrives home to the North East for the 2026 Mercury Prize event in Newcastle this week. She and her family are confirmed Shields fans. This club’s journey will be fascinating to follow.

Halifax are the ones who feel in greater need of the FA Cup’s restorative powers, though, and they will head into the first round proper — a holy grail for lower-league sides — with the folk memory of clobbering that ultra-confident Manchester City side.

Back then, Halifax manager George Kirby recruited the help of a hypnotherapist who claimed he had previously placed a curse on Allison for an unpaid debt — though people generally feel the state of the pitch made most difference.

Nearly 50 years on, Halifax need all the help they can get.

Sports.title: US Air Force service member dies from injuries suffered in horrific 150ft fall at college football game
Sports.content:
An Air Force service member has died from injuries suffered when he fell more than 150 feet from the rafters of the Alamodome in a horrifying pregame accident on Saturday night, Air Force officials have confirmed.

The victim has yet to be identified publicly. Per official Air Force policy, deceased service members are not named publicly until 24 hours after the family has been notified.

The Airman was one of four service members rappelling from the rafters ahead of the Navy-University of Texas at San Antonio (UTSA) football game when he slipped down the rope and slammed into the turf at tremendous speed. He was rushed to the hospital, where he later died, according to a statement from Nellis Air Force Base Public Affairs. The incident is under investigation.

News of the individual's death was first reported by Task and Purpose, an online publication that focuses on military affairs. The deceased Airman was assigned to the 6th Combat Training Squadron, a unit that conducts advanced skills training for special warfare Airmen.

Clips filmed from multiple angles showed the Airman hitting the ground as thousands of onlookers were left stunned in San Antonio. Alamodome medics quickly rushed to the fallen Airman's aid.

He was carted off the field and taken to a local hospital.

Video captured by San Antonio resident James Larken Smith showed the officer hit the turf

A military member rappels from the stadium rafters in a previous demonstration

'Everybody was quiet, the band stopped performing. Everybody was dead silent,' witness Adrian Corey told KSAT.

Adrian's mother, Siomara, described the unsettling confusion after the accident.

'There was no updates after that other than asking for prayers, but it did not look good,' she told KSAT.

A similar stunt was performed without incident before a 2025 game at the Alamodome between Army and UTSA.

Despite the pre-game incident, officials proceeded with kickoff after a 10-minute delay. UTSA went on to beat Navy, 38-34, and afterwards many players took part in a group prayer for the injured Airman.

'I know we said a prayer postgame, but they'll continue being our thoughts and prayers, and really thinking about them,' Roadrunners quarterback Owen McCown told reporters.

The American Conference, which includes both Navy and UTSA, decided to proceed with the game before it was revealed that the Airman had died, according to a Sunday statement.

The ceiling at the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas is 180ft above the field

'During the game, representatives of both participating member institutions, Alamodome management and local authorities met with American Conference Commissioner Tim Pernetti and a working group to review the information available and discuss next steps,' read the conference statement. 'At the time of those discussions, Nellis Air Force Base Public Affairs had not publicly confirmed the service member’s condition.

'Air Force casualty notification and information-release procedures establish safeguards for notifying families and publicly releasing casualty information. In accordance with conference bylaws and with the support of both participating member institutions, the conference made the decision to continue the game. Respect for the family’s privacy and adherence to the military’s notification process guided the decision to mitigate speculation about the service member’s medical status and avoid additional distress for his family.

'Later, at 11:40pm Eastern time, Nellis Air Force Base Public Affairs confirmed that the service member had been injured during the pregame demonstration and transported to a local hospital, where he later died. We are grateful to the first responders and emergency personnel who provided immediate care on the field. Our hearts and prayers are with everyone impacted by this tragedy.'

UTSA has offered counseling services to students in need of assistance following the tragedy.

The viral X user known as Freddy was at the game and later shared a post about the incident before news of the Airman's death had been publicized.

'Another college game done,' the semi-anonymous social media influencer and minor World Cup celebrity wrote on X amid his prolonged tour of the United States. 'UTSA got the win against Navy! Thank you to all the nice people that we met today.

'Unfortunately,' he continued, 'there was a serious accident before the game, which is why I stopped updating on here. Our thoughts are with the service member and his family.'

After the game, UTSA coach Jeff Traylor described the situation he faced in the locker room as his anxious team looked to take the field.

'The only information I had was there had been an incident, and the game was going to be delayed, and we didn't expand upon it any further than that,' Traylor said, as quoted by the Express-News. 'I didn't know if I did the right thing or not. I didn't know anything. I didn't know what to tell them, so that's how I handled it.

'What I heard that happened is heartbreaking, but I want to give the family time,' Traylor added. 'They're in our prayers. It's tragic.'

Sports.title: Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson is ejected from game after spitting at opponent in shameful NFL moment
Sports.content:
Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson is ejected from game after spitting at opponent in shameful NFL moment

Buffalo Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson has been ejected from their game against the Las Vegas Raiders after spitting at an opponent on the field.

During the second quarter, the Bills safety approached Raiders tight end Brock Bowers for a heated exchange of words - before spitting in his rival's direction.

The disgusting incident occurred right in front of an official, who quickly flagged the action. Gardner-Johnson was ejected from the game soon after.

Bizarrely, the Bills safety was seen with a big grin on his face as he made his way back to the locker room following the ruling by the officials.

The incident quickly went viral on social media, with fans calling for the Bills to part ways with the former Philadelphia Eagles star.

'If you can't play Professionally, you don't belong in the NFL or Bills Team', one furious fan wrote on X.

Bills star CJ Gardner-Johnson was seen grinning after being ejected on Sunday afternoon

The Bills safety was seen spitting at a Las Vegas Raiders rival during their Week 6 clash

C.J. Gardner-Johnson spits in the direction of Brock Bowers, leading to disqualification pic.twitter.com/8zW4OYIP7o — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) October 18, 2026

'Just stupid, disrespectful and selfish. Idiot never learns,' another fan said online.

Meanwhile, one fan wrote: 'Just replace him with someone from the practice squad'.

The shocking ordeal comes just two weeks after Gardner-Johnson sparked a feud with Mike Vrabel after the Bills star derided the Patriots' Efton Chism over his incredible game-winning touchdown in Buffalo.

Chism, an undrafted free agent, made a stunning one-handed catch as New England secured a 29-26 victory earlier this month.

It was just his seventh reception since joining the Patriots in 2025 but it condemned the Bills to a first loss of the season and afterwards Gardner-Johnson dismissed Chism as only a 'practice squad player.'

The Bills safety said: 'An elevated guy made a hell of a catch - [we] probably won't hear from him again.... a practice squad player made a hell of a play.

'That's all I'm going to tell you. You do it again, and he probably won't make it again.'

Gardner-Johnson's comments quickly went viral and when they were put to Vrabel, the Patriots coach did not turn down the chance to poke holes in the safety's own resume.

Some fans called for the Bills to cut Gardner-Johnson after the disgusting on-field act

The incident comes just two weeks after Gardner-Johnson drew the ire of New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel, having taken aim at New England star Efton Chism

'For a guy that's been on eight teams in four years? I mean, I guess he knows the drill,' he told The Greg Hill Show.

Gardner-Johnson was drafted by the New Orleans Saints in 2019 and before joining the Bills, he spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles (twice), the Detroit Lions, the Houston Texans, the Baltimore Ravens and the Chicago Bears.

The Bills are his fifth team since 2024. Chism, meanwhile, has played in 11 regular-season games and has never spent time on the Patriots practice squad.

'Nobody works harder [than Chism]. You love to see players take advantage of opportunities, to help the team win,' Vrabel added.

'He is very well respected, he practices, he is on show team, he takes a million reps, nobody logs more miles or yards or whatever we track than Chis.'

Sports.title: Kai Rooney shares update as he bounces back from Man Utd heartbreak in perfect way
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney shares update as he bounces back from Man Utd heartbreak in perfect way

The 16-year-old son of Manchester United legend Wayne made his Premier League 2 debut on Friday as part of a busy weekend

View 2 Images Kai Rooney had a busy weekend playing for Manchester United (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Kai Rooney, the son of Manchester United legend Wayne, has posted a message after responding to his Under-21s debut in the perfect way. The 16-year-old made his bow in Premier League 2 on Friday.

‌



‌



After making his way through the youth teams at United, he was part of the squad for the match against Nottingham Forest at Loughborough University. He was given a chance to make an impression when he was brought on with 12 minutes left to play.

‌



At that time, the scoreline was 2-2, with United hoping that Rooney could help them to push for a winner. But, the game went the opposite way as Forest scored late to record a 3-2 win as he suffered late heartbreak.

‌



The loss was the United development squad's first of the campaign in Premier League 2, having clinched victories in their opening three fixtures against Ipswich Town, Leicester City and Brentford. However, Rooney, had little time to think about the setback.

Despite featuring for the U21s on Friday, he was straight back into the starting line-up for the club's U18s the following day as they too faced Nottingham Forest. Rooney got himself on the scoresheet to hand United the advantage in the first half.

‌



He was substituted in the 66th minute, but United were unable to hold on for all three points. Forest drew level in the 78th minute, with the match finishing 1-1.

Following the double header, Rooney took to social media to respond to his goal, sharing a picture of his celebration alongside a caption reading: "back on the scoresheet.'. It's been a busy few weeks for Rooney as he made his U19s debut just last week.

‌



He came on as a second-half substitute in the UEFA Youth League clash against Atletico Madrid, a game which United lost 3-0.

He signed a two-year scholarship with the club back in July. The deal can turn into a three-year professional deal worth around £50,000 per year, plus an annual signing-on fee.

View 2 Images Kai Rooney has come up through the Manchester United youth ranks (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



As Rooney was starting to make his own way in football, it had previously been revealed by his mum, Coleen, that he had to ban his dad from attending matches.

As Rooney began carving out his own path in football, his mum, Coleen, had previously revealed that he was forced to ban his father from watching him play. "Kai told Wayne to stop coming to football games, when he played grassroots tournaments and stuff because he used to get swarmed and he couldn't even watch the game," she said on I'm a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here in 2024.

"How do you say to all of these kids, 'Go away, I'm watching my son?' Adults, it's different, you could speak to them. So he (Kai) just said, 'Oh, dad there's no point you coming because you don't even watch me play anyway.' Which is sad, but it can't be helped anyway. At the same time, the fans help you along the way and get you where you are."

Article continues below

Wayne has, however, since been spotted at matches, suggesting that the ban has now been lifted.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta masterstroke sees Arsenal earn gritty win against Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Arsenal ensured they kept pace with Manchester City in the early Premier League title race after squeezing past by Nottingham Forest.

The Gunners struggled to break down their hosts throughout the majority of the game, albeit Declan Rice was guilty of passing up a golden opportunity.

Their opener eventually came late on through Noni Madueke, whose deflected effort was enough to seal victory for the champions.

The win leaves Mikel Arteta's side sitting second and three points behind City. Forest in the meantime remain in the drop zone despite their resolute performance going unrewarded.

‌

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Madueke makes an impact

Following a less-than inspiring first-half in the East-Midlands, Arsenal boss Arteta opted for a change at the break, with Eberechi Eze being replaced by Noni Madeueke. While substitutions have proven so fruitful for the Arsenal boss over recent seasons, it looked as though the opposite might be true at the City Ground.

Madueke endured a nightmare start to his outing after picking up a booking. He also had very little impact from an attacking standpoint.

‌



That was until the final ten minutes of the game. Madueke picked up the ball on the left flank, cut inside and let fly, with his effort flying past Mats Sels via a deflection.

It was a bold move from Arteta, but one that was absolutely the correct one.

Delap Forest's biggest outlet

After scoring his first Forest in the win against Villa last month, striker Liam Delap was once again his side's biggest threat against Arsenal. And while he didn't quite manage to get on the scoresheet, it was still an impressive performance from the forward.

His tireless running gave Forest a real focal point, while Delap's strength and physicality allowed Forest to move up the pitch once he had successfully managed to hold the ball up.

‌



Of course, goals need to come more regularly for Delap now, having scored just two Premier League goals over the past 18 months. But more performances like this are really encouraging.

View 2 Images Liam Delap was Forest's biggest threat (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal's City Ground hoodoo comes to an end

Arteta's side have not had the best of luck at the City Ground over the past few years. They had only won on one of their last five visits to Forest - a record that includes a rotten FA Cup defeat, as well as consecutive 0-0 draws.

In fact, their only win at the City Ground since Forest's promotion back to the top fight came back in January 2024.

‌



So it was no surprise to see Arsenal struggle for fluency. They failed to produce a single shot on target throughout the first 75 minutes and never really looked like taking the lead.

That was until, of course, Madueke converted. And it was just about enough to see Arsenal seal a hard-fought three points. It's an old cliche but champions find a way to win and that's exactly what they did.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest demand fans stop 'misogynistic' chant and reveal sanctions if caught
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest demand fans stop 'misogynistic' chant and reveal sanctions if caught

Nottingham Forest take on Arsenal at the City Ground on Sunday afternoon and the Midlands side have sent a strong message to supporters about their behaviour ahead of the game

View 2 Images Forest have asked supporters to stop signing a 'mysoginistic' chant (Image: Getty Images)

Nottingham Forest have urged fans to stop a historic ‘misogynistic’ chant ahead of their clash with Arsenal. The Midlands side welcome the reigning Premier League champions to the City Ground on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



And before that game, Forest released a statement requesting that supporters leave their ‘Nottingham is full of fun’ chant that referenced ‘t*** and f****’ in the past - or face sanctions.

‌



A statement read: “Nottingham Forest is proud of the inclusive environment it has worked hard to create, and remains committed to ensuring everybody feels welcome, respected, and valued.

‌



“We recognise that a particular chant has a long history among small sections of our support. While it is only sung by a minority of supporters, the potential impact of this chant and its misogynistic nature cannot be overlooked.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



“This issue has also been raised by Nottinghamshire Police and Kick It Out, and after discussing further with our Fan Advisory Board, we are committed to delivering a united message: any form of discrimination, including misogynistic chanting, will not be tolerated.

“Any supporters identified to be engaging in discriminatory chanting may face education sessions or further action, including club bans and being placed on acceptable behaviour contracts. The Club may also face sanctions if such chanting continues.

“We want all supporters, including the women and girls who are an integral part of our Forest family, to feel safe and respected at the City Ground and when following the team away from home.

‌



View 2 Images Forest issued a strong warning to supporters (Image: Getty Images)

“We ask all fans to consider the impact of their words and help ensure Nottingham Forest remains an inclusive environment where everyone belongs.”

The decision did not go down particularly well with some supporters, with one replying on social media: “Pretty sure that chant started because of the massive population of females compared to males in the 60-70s? Older fans could well correct me on that though. The majority of female fans around us sing it as well.”

Article continues below

Forest had endured a difficult start to the season under new boss Oliver Glasner ahead of their clash with Arsenal. After winning just one of their opening six games, they were left in the relegation zone.

Their showdown with Arsenal was also their last game on home soil for a little while, with away games against Ipswich and Brentford to come ahead of taking on Manchester City at the City Ground on November 7.

Sports.title: Leeds miss golden chance to pile misery on Man Utd - but match didn't deserve a winner
Sports.content:
Leeds miss golden chance to pile misery on Man Utd - but match didn't deserve a winner

LEEDS 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: Bryan Mbeumo fired the Red Devils ahead before the break but Dominic Calvert-Lewin struck in the second half to earn a point for the hosts

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin scores the equaliser for Leeds (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Dominic Calvert-Lewin denied Manchester United their first win in six games - to pile more pressure on Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



Calvert-Lewin's second half equaliser cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's 35th minute strike, to make it honours even at a white hot Elland Road.

‌



But if Carrick returned across the Pennines feeling satisfied, he shouldn't have done. The United boss insists he has the best job possible and is still 'loving it'.

‌



But no manager in their right mind should be loving the fact their side has not won a single game for more than five weeks.

Or kept a clean sheet in the league all season. At this rate, United will be airing the club's dirty laundry in public again, by sacking another manager.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Carrick had needed this trip to Elland Road like a hole in the head. The cauldron of hate is bad enough in normal circumstances, let alone when United had not won in five games in all competitions.

Leeds never need an excuse to pile pain on their bitter rivals, but on this occasion the hosts must have been relishing the visit of Carrick's men more than ever.

‌



Leeds went into this clash above United in the table. The last time this happened was back in 2002, which was also the last time Leeds beat United at home. But this time round United appeared vulnerable and there for the taking.

Not least because United started with a right back at left back, and a centre back at right back. While Lisandro Martinez owed his manager a big performance, considering his outburst in the wake of the defeat at Atletico Madrid.

Most of the first half was high on toxicity and low on quality. Ethan Ampadu made three crunching tackles on Andrey Santos, Kobbie Mainoo and Mbeumo.

‌



View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo opened the scoring (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

While Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson were booked for two crude challenges of their own. This was no place for shrinking violets. But a football match broke out just before the half hour mark.

Nico Elvedi saw a header well saved by Senne Lammens. While at the opposite end Youri Tielemans put a chance on a plate for Mbeumo, who made a complete meal of it by heading wide with just James Trafford to beat.

‌



Trafford then had to charge from goal to stop Amad Diallo. It was fast, furious and frantic in equal measure. But 10 minutes before the break Mbeumo made amends to give United the lead.

He brushed aside a feeble challenge from James Justin to meet another Tielemans cross and beat Trafford with a cool finish. Ao Tanaka shot straight at Lammens before Calvert-Lewin headed just wide, as Leeds looked to hit back.

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

‌



Which they eventually did six minutes into the second half, when Calvert-Lewin lashed home from close range after United had failed to deal with a corner.

Leeds had their tails up, and Tanaka smashed a volley over the top. Harry Maguire was fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty after pulling Ampadu to the ground inside the box.

Tensions continued to simmer, with Ampadu and Fernandes involved in a spiteful exchange of words, while Tanaka left Diallo writhing in pain following a brutal - but legal - tackle.

Article continues below

Fernandes dragged a shot wide and Anton Stach blazed over as both sides went in search of winner. But in truth, the game didn't deserve one.

Sports.title: Brighton star scores from HALFWAY LINE as Seagulls run riot against rivals Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Brighton star scores from HALFWAY LINE as Seagulls run riot against rivals Crystal Palace

Brighton blew rivals Crystal Palace away with a sensational opening ten minutes on Sunday afternoon with Paraguayan midfielder Diego Gomez stealing the show with a stunning goal

View 2 Images Diego Gomez's first goal of the season was one to remember (Image: Getty Images)

Brighton star Diego Gomez has been compared to David Beckham following his wondergoal from the halfway line. The Seagulls enjoyed a scintillating opening half against their rivals Crystal Palace on Sunday afternoon.

‌



‌



They took the lead as Jaydee Canvot put through his own net, with Gomez then doubling the lead just moments later with a stunning strike.

‌



Gomez, 23, picked the ball up in the centre circle and fired a brilliant effort over Palace keeper Walter Benitez and into the back of the net.

‌



Speaking about the striker, former Premier League stopper Shay Given said: “It's an amazing goal. Reminiscent of David Beckham [vs Wimbledon].

“I don't even blame Benitez the goalkeeper. We're always talking about sweeper goalkeepers and you've got to be high up for the through ball and the defence playing a high line.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“I think his position was fine. You've just got to take your hat off to Gomez. That is just a brilliant, brilliant goal.”

Fellow pundit Efan Ekoku added: “What a strike. Wharton gets dispossessed and Gomez only has one thought.

‌



“He absolutely drills out, superbly struck and right over the head of the keeper from the centre-circle. That's the goal of the season so far - what a hit.”

Gomez has been a star performer for Brighton this season, the Seagulls having enjoyed a brilliant start to the campaign under Fabian Hurzeler. He now has a goal and two assists to his name.

View 2 Images Gomez's teammates were left stunned by his goal (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Gomez was signed from MLS side Inter Miami in January 2025. Away from his goal, Brighton’s afternoon continued to get even better.

Just moments after Gomez’s strike, Yasin Ayari got on the scoresheet to round off a sensational opening 10 minutes. Charalampos Kostoulas then extended their advantage even further in the second half. Jack Hinselwood rounded off the scoring late on.

Their win leaves them second in the Premier League table after five wins from their opening seven games. Following their thumping of Palace, Brighton will now turn their attention to their European commitments, with a clash with Czech side Jablonec to come in midweek ahead of a clash with Liverpool.

Article continues below

Palace in the meantime have been left to lick their wounds ahead of a clash with Turkish giants Besiktas. Their next Premier League assignment will see them tangle with Newcastle.
