Sports.title: F1 could make call to move finale to Imola as late as ‘mid-November’ – report | Briefs
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

It comes after missile strikes hit an airport in nearby Saudi Arabia, whose world championship round was cancelled earlier this year. F1 is due to return to the country in March next year.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Still Has Plenty Of Paydays Available
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley can still bag massive paydays below elite title level. Calls for him to hang up the gloves after getting stopped by Daniel Dubois completely miss that reality. Falling short against Dubois does not strip him of his ability to top domestic bills.

Derek Chisora wrote the playbook here. Chisora never had to conquer top-tier heavyweights to fill arenas or generate huge paychecks. British fans recognize him, know the entertainment they are paying for, and show up. Wardley can mirror that blueprint without wasting years fruitlessly chasing a rematch with Dubois.

Domestic dust-ups against Dave Allen, Johnny Fisher, or Chisora himself offer immediate box-office appeal. Efe Ajagba or Tony Yoka provide solid international flavor. None of those are walkovers, but none require beating a pound-for-pound monster to pack out a venue.

The draw remains unchanged. Fans know Wardley hits like a truck, and they know he can get hurt in return. Put Wardley in the ring with Fisher, and nobody cares if a world belt is on the line; they are tuning in because someone is going to sleep.

That leaves Queensberry holding plenty of cards. A routine bounce-back victory followed by a massive domestic main event puts him right back in the money without pretending he solved the Dubois riddle.

Down the line, reaching the end of his Queensberry deal might even open up a fresh bidding war. Zuffa could easily see value in an action-heavy British brawler. While nothing is on the table right now, it highlights how many avenues exist beyond this single loss.

Wardley’s physical condition must always come first. From a purely business perspective, the path is clear. Chisora proved you can remain a massive ticket seller without beating the division’s champions.

Wardley does not need another belt around his waist to get paid. Pick the right matchups, and he can laugh all the way to the bank for years to come.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Seeks Stamina Help From Team Usyk
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is working alongside Oleksandr Usyk’s conditioning team ahead of his October 31 bout against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh. The meeting will thoroughly test his gas tank across twelve rounds.

Base camp is Gandia, Spain, where Canelo brought in outside fitness specialists while Eddy Reynoso directs the boxing work. Against Mbilli, the payoff must show when fatigue sets in, especially since the younger contender never stops pressing forward.

“In strength and conditioning, I am learning new things,” Canelo told The Ring. “I appreciate them because they put all of their energy into me and are doing everything based on what [my head coach] Eddy Reynoso needs for boxing.”

Mbilli’s relentless tempo explains the sudden shift in preparation. Canelo punishes opponents who march directly into his range, yet he needs steady volume to win rounds. Landing occasional sharp counters leaves far too much clock open for an aggressive challenger throwing nonstop leather.

The main question is whether Canelo can sustain his offense once the fight pushes past the midway mark. Now 36, Canelo returns following his defeat against Terence Crawford and subsequent surgery on his left elbow, with over a year of inactivity behind him. He expects peak execution from a heavily taxed body.

A fresh training philosophy provides something new, yet genuine output down the stretch remains unproven. Cardiovascular endurance does not magically appear in the twilight of a twenty-year career. You cannot rebuild an engine with that much mileage, especially after serious elbow surgery and more than a year out of the ring.

Usyk’s training methods work for Usyk because he has spent a lifetime developing an engine built for movement, bounce, and non-stop output. Transplanting those drills onto a flat-footed counterpuncher who relies on heavy torso rotations and planted feet makes zero sense mechanically.

Mbilli is a nightmare style for an aging fighter who needs scheduled rest breaks. He throws upwards of 80 punches a round, does not care about taking shots to give three back, and smothers distance

The mental comfort of working with Usyk’s crew might give him a temporary psychological lift in camp, but once round seven arrives, and Mbilli is still in his chest, those new drills will not buy him the oxygen his legs and lungs can no longer produce.

Training in Spain softens the time shift into Saudi Arabia. Canelo described feeling “really weird” during his early morning bout with William Scull and stated he has requested that Turki Alalshikh schedule a ring walk no later than midnight or 1 a.m.

Better timing can sharpen his entrance. Once the bell rings, though, Mbilli brings intense pressure that travel logistics cannot solve. Canelo needs the work with Usyk’s camp to translate into steady output when fatigue threatens to stall him.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Drops Canelo Chase Three Years Late
Sports.content:
David Benavidez has finally conceded that a fight with Canelo Alvarez will never happen, admitting that reality years after his climb up the divisions settled the question.

Benavidez currently fights at cruiserweight, two full divisions above super middleweight, while openly discussing a future heavyweight jump against Oleksandr Usyk. He has not made 168 pounds since 2023. Any realistic window to face Canelo closed several weight classes ago.

“I think honestly I could say with confidence that that fight is never going to happen,” Benavidez told Brian Custer.

When Brian asked if he had permanently moved on, Benavidez praised Canelo, yet still claimed the Mexican star simply refused to face him.

“I don’t want to keep disrespecting somebody … not even disrespecting, but just calling somebody out that doesn’t want to fight,” he said.

That rationale ignores the massive physical gap separating them today. Critics can reasonably argue Canelo should have met Benavidez when both shared the 168-pound division. That complaint loses all weight with Benavidez now preparing for Michal Cieslak at 200 pounds.

His prospective roadmap includes Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, and eventual heavyweight tests. None of those plans lead anywhere near Canelo.

A logical alternative after Canelo fell to Terence Crawford would have been targeting Crawford directly. Crawford had talked of entering boxing’s Mount Rushmore. The public intrigue around him was at an all-time peak, and Turki Alalshikh held the purse strings to fund virtually any blockbuster Crawford wanted next.

If Benavidez truly wanted to settle the score on the belts Canelo kept out of reach, Crawford was the obvious lever to pull. Instead of shifting his crosshairs to the newly crowned undisputed champion, Benavidez let the moment disappear.

“He’s a great fighter. He’s a legend,” Benavidez said. “I would like to be a great Mexican legend like him one day.”

Calling yourself a future Mexican legend sounds nice in an interview, but looking at the actual resume tells a different story. Canelo earned that status by taking on the toughest challenges available from junior middleweight all the way to light heavyweight, facing elite operators like Floyd Mayweather Jr., Gennadiy Golovkin, Miguel Cotto, and Dmitry Bivol.

Benavidez is nowhere near that neighborhood. Instead of securing defining legacy bouts, he is lining up voluntary defenses against Michal Cieslak at 200 pounds. While Cieslak is a capable European contender, nobody outside of hard-core circles is paying to see that fight. It does nothing to elevate Benavidez to the pantheon of Mexican greats.

If Benavidez genuinely wanted to close the gap on Canelo, he needed to make real waves. Taking out Gilberto Ramirez was a solid win, but sitting on belts and scheduling low-demand opponents like Cieslak keeps him in neutral. Fighting fringe contenders at cruiserweight only proves that while he talks about chasing history, his matchmaking still trails far behind the standard Canelo set.

Sports.title: Frank Martin Wants Shakur Stevenson Or Tank Rematch
Sports.content:
Frank Martin is calling for bouts with Shakur Stevenson, Gervonta Davis, or Isaac Pitbull Cruz. Still, his recent ring activity shows he has serious ground to cover before getting those marquee fights.

The 31-year-old light welterweight contender welcomed every major challenge, targeting Davis in particular.

“Man, I love that rematch,” Martin said to Fight Hub TV. He also acknowledged that facing Cruz or Lamont Roach could build momentum toward a second Davis meeting.

Martin pointed to weight issues during his initial loss to Davis without detailing what went wrong. Vague explanations will not convince the public to buy a sequel. He must deliver clear proof inside the ropes that a second meeting would end differently.

The inactivity is killing whatever marketability he had left from the Tank pay-per-view. Since the lucrative 2024 bout with Davis, Martin has made only two ring appearances. His sole win since 2023 was a decision over veteran Rances Barthelemy, followed by a ten-round draw against Nahir Albright earlier this year.

Albright was supposed to be a routine showcase to get him winning, and instead, Martin escaped with a gift draw in a fight that many observers thought he dropped. When you look shaky against Albright, you have zero leverage to demand dates with elite champions.

Martin steps into the ring against Tarik Zaina on October 24 for a rebuilding fight. Winning is essential, yet vanishing into inactivity afterward would erase any progress.

“We ain’t chasing nobody,” Martin stated. “I just want to put on a dominant performance,” noting he is ready for whatever comes next.

Waiting for top fighters to call him rarely works. Neither Stevenson nor Davis has an incentive to pick him when Martin carries minimal buzz. Cruz offers the most practical path forward. The aggressive style Cruz brings could create an explosive contest, giving Martin a platform to secure a defining victory.

Joining Zuffa could also solve his scheduling problems if the promotion delivers active fight dates. Constant ring time will do far more for his career than calling out superstars he cannot book.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Reveals Three Fight Roadmap: Opetaia, Beterbiev, And Usyk
Sports.content:
David Benavidez is mapping out an ambitious three-fight wishlist once he handles Michal Cieslak on December 5. Benavidez laid out three massive targets: Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, plus Oleksandr Usyk.

That roadmap keeps him focused on cruiserweight, along with an eventual leap to heavyweight for Usyk. It also leaves Dmitry Bivol completely on the sidelines for the foreseeable future.

“We’re talking about Opetaia. We’re talking about Beterbiev. And then we’re maybe talking about Usyk,” Benavidez said to Brian Custer’s channel.

Opetaia sits at the top of the queue. If Benavidez gets past Cieslak, he wants the Australian champion on Cinco de Mayo weekend in May 2027.

“The fight that I got to honor first is the fight with Opetaia because I told him I’d fight him Cinco de Mayo next year,” he explained.

Beterbiev comes next in the plan, specifically at cruiserweight. Benavidez figures the Russian puncher would benefit from skipping the brutal drain down to 175 pounds. That choice sets up a fresher, more dangerous rival to conquer.

“I think it’s a better fight for both of us at cruiserweight,” Benavidez said. “It’d be a bigger challenge for me.”

Trading shots in the pocket against Beterbiev without weight drain presents a massive test. If Benavidez stays inside to let his punches fly, he must survive lethal return fire right back.

A meeting with Usyk remains the most ambitious idea on the board. Benavidez mentioned taking that bout at cruiserweight or heavyweight, saying he would take the chance immediately.

Keep in mind, these names represent Benavidez’s personal target list rather than finalized contracts. He plans on staying with PBC while working across promotional boundaries to secure them.

A bout with Bivol could happen down the line, but it will not happen anytime soon.

“In the next three fights, probably not,” Benavidez said regarding Bivol.

Gold fever completely clouds judgment, and Benavidez sounds like an old prospector who spotted a glitter in the stream and started spending millions in his head before he even picked up a shovel.

Counting Opetaia as an automatic win to reach massive paydays against an aging Artur Beterbiev and Oleksandr Usyk shows how disconnected Benavidez has become from reality. If Opetaia clips him, that entire fantasy sequence turns to smoke. The Usyk dream evaporates, the cruiserweight belts vanish, and the massive Saudi checks dry up overnight.

Benavidez is so fixated on cashing in on three giant events that he forgets the brutal toll the very first hurdle demands.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Questions Unequal Protection On Canelo Alvarez Card
Sports.content:
Robert Garcia wants assurances about his camp’s safety before Lindolfo Delgado’s October 31 vacant IBF light welterweight title fight in Riyadh. He expects Canelo Alvarez to receive royal treatment ahead of his fight with Christian Mbilli, but fears his own team will be left traveling without the same protection.

The veteran trainer sounded uneasy rather than defiant when speaking on his team’s travel logistics. His issue is not whether the bout takes place, but the wide gulf between how the headliner travels and how the undercard talent gets moved into Saudi Arabia.

Canelo operates in an entirely different financial stratosphere. Garcia expects him to arrive by private plane with security handling his trip to the arena. His fear is that Delgado and his corner will have to fly commercial and pass through a public airport without comparable protection.

“They’ll f***ing fly private. They’ll go into a private airport where nobody knows where they’re at. They’ll have security driving them to the arena,” Garcia told Elie Seckbach.

Garcia wants similar protection for his group, but his tone sounded more resigned than demanding. He knows how big-money boxing operates. Promoters spare no expense for the box-office anchor, while supporting fighters are left to fend for themselves on standard itineraries.

“Canelo’s fight might happen because, like I told you, he’s secured. Not us. We’re not secured,” Garcia admitted.

The idea of Delgado’s camp joining Canelo on a private charter is wishful thinking, and Garcia practically acknowledged it in the same breath.

“If they tell us, ‘You guys are all traveling together,’ then we’re fine, but I don’t think that’s the case.”

Garcia doesn’t sound hopeful. Delgado is fighting Artur Biyarslanov for the vacant IBF light welterweight title, but that doesn’t buy him Canelo’s treatment. Canelo headlines the event. Delgado fills a spot underneath him, even with a world championship at stake.

Robert can vent to reporters, but walking away could cost his fighter the opportunity he’s been working toward. If Garcia refuses to travel without better security, organizers could look for a replacement. Delgado would then be watching somebody else fight for the belt.

That’s what makes Garcia’s position so uncomfortable. He has every reason to ask how his team will be protected, yet Delgado could be the one paying for it if they refuse to go. A world title shot is a powerful incentive to board the plane, even when your trainer has serious doubts about the trip.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley’s Defeats Overshadow His Finest Boxing Year
Sports.content:
A back-and-forth heavyweight fight captures the public’s collective imagination like few other sporting events. Countless expressions originating or popularized in heavyweight boxing describe competitive sporting events. “A knockdown drag-out contest”, “teams throwing haymakers”, “a slugfest”, “a heavyweight fight”, and many other such phrases regularly feature on football, baseball and basketball broadcasts.

The first fight between Daniel Dubois (24-3, 23 KO) and Fabio Wardley (20-2-1, 19 KO) in May illustrated the fantasy of what many envision in a heavyweight clash. Knockdowns, temerity, mettle, blood, violence. In the end, Daniel Dubois prevailed via technical knockout in the eleventh round. Fabio Wardley lost his championship, but gained the respect of anyone watching. It instantly entered the “fight of the year” conversation and was hailed as a heavyweight classic.

…

This past Saturday, just over five months later, Dubois and Wardley met again. The rematch was anticlimactic by comparison. The fight featured an early knockdown like the first encounter, though this time Daniel Dubois delivered it. Though Wardley tried to resist Dubois’ onslaught, it proved to be futile. Dubois nearly ended the bout inside the first round. But Wardley survived long enough to hear the bell to conclude round one. Ultimately, Wardley’s doggedness just lengthened his suffering.

Sixty seconds later, as round two began, Dubois was patient, waiting to find openings to pound away at Wardley. Dubois did it in short order. In the final minute of round two, Dubois peppered a winded and wounded Wardley with clean, powerful punches. The fight got stopped 2:21 into the second round; it was undoubtedly a fair stoppage. Referee Steve Gray stopped the contest just as Wardley’s trainer Ben Davidson threw in the towel from the corner.

Dubois obliterated Fabio Wardley and extinguished any doubt from fans and media, at least for now.

…

Fabio Wardley was a latecomer to boxing, turning professional at 22 years old with no amateur fights on his resume. Both his age and lack of amateur experience are considered rarities. Four fights into his pro career, Wardley agreed to be managed by Dillian Whyte, a fellow British heavyweight and former sparring partner. Wardley was born in Ipswich, England, and naturally is a lifelong supporter of Ipswich Town Football Club. He attained a dream by fighting at Ipswich Town’s stadium, Portman Road, in June 2025. His knockout win there over Justis Huni helped propel Wardley to recognition as 2025’s British Boxer of the Year, according to multiple outlets. An upset victory over former world champion Joseph Parker earned Wardley the WBO’s interim heavyweight championship. Wardley’s banner year of 2025 set him up to challenge Daniel Dubois in May for the vacant WBO heavyweight title.

…

On Saturday, Fabio Wardley was walloped. This year, Wardley has zero wins and two losses, both by technical knockout. But boxing fans will always remember the slugfest Wardley and Dubois had in May. While 2025 was Wardley’s most successful year in boxing, he will inevitably be associated with Daniel Dubois and their classic fight five months ago. In a career in which he has beaten former world champions and scored devastating knockouts, boxing fans will most fondly remember Fabio Wardley for a fight he lost.

It might not be fair, but it is reality. In a way, it is endearing, though. Even if Fabio Wardley never competes for a heavyweight championship again, the Ipswichian has forever earned a place in heavyweight boxing lore for his performance on May 9, 2026.

…

Sports and society at large are infatuated with analytics and data. Decades from now, when a young boxing fan asks their personalized robot about Fabio Wardley, they will be unimpressed by consecutive knockout losses. But if that young fan finds an old head and mentions Fabio Wardley, they will hear about his toughness, how he could have won a title in a different era, who Wardley reminds them of, and whatever else. Wardley and Dubois have earned remembrance in highlight reels and recollections, the greatest accolade of all.

Sports.title: Dalton Smith Wants Shakur Stevenson After Alberto Puello
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith is already eyeing a massive unification bout with Shakur Stevenson, even with his first WBC light welterweight title defense against Alberto Puello just days away.

Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) meets Puello on October 24 at Utilita Arena Sheffield. The unbeaten titleholder wants this victory to catapult him toward marquee names. Shakur sits near the top of his target list, but Puello can ruin everything.

“I’m boxing to be a part of the biggest fights possible. Of course the Shakur fight would be up there as one of the biggest. I’d love to be a part of that,” Smith told the Boxing World YouTube channel. “But of course, I have to get through Puello first.”

Smith grabbed the WBC belt back in January by stopping Subriel Matias inside five rounds during his US debut. Blowing through Matias earned him huge momentum, though it guarantees nothing against Puello.

Puello brings an awkward southpaw style. Smith will not get the same gifts he received from Matias, who walked straight in until he got caught by heavy counters. Puello is far more than a tune-up on the way to a Shakur payday. This matchup tests whether Dalton can defend his crown against a completely different kind of opponent.

“I don’t overlook what’s in front of me, but once I get the job done against Puello, I want to be chasing the biggest fights possible,” Smith said.

Puello (25-1, 11 KOs) has his own motives to spoil the party and steal that massive future date for himself. Calling out Shakur is the easy part for Smith. He still has to leave the ring with the belt.

Even if he gets past Puello, Dalton is overlooking the obstacles that will prevent him from fighting Shakur next. The network and promotional divide makes the Shakur-Smith fight virtually impossible to assemble right now. Shakur is signed with Zuffa and locked into Paramount+, while Smith is a Matchroom flagship fighter tied to DAZN.

Dual-network broadcasts only happen when the revenue numbers are astronomical, like Gervonta Davis against Ryan Garcia or massive undisputed heavyweight cards funded by deep foreign pockets. Dalton Smith versus Shakur Stevenson is nowhere near that category.

Neither guy moves US pay-per-view buys on that scale, and Zuffa has zero incentive to share production, split domestic rights, or loan out Shakur to DAZN for an ordinary regular-subscription card.

Dalton is known almost exclusively in the UK, and Shakur has struggled to build an audience that translates into commercial event revenue.

Zuffa Boxing did not bring Shakur to Paramount+ just to farm him out to DAZN or hand Matchroom control of an international production. If Zuffa wants Shakur in a unification or a meaningful fight at 140 pounds, they have zero business justification to share the pie with an outside streaming rival on an event with minimal domestic pay-per-view appetite.

Ghana News.title: 2026 Beach Soccer AFCON: Ghana qualifies after thrilling win over Nigeria

BS1

Ghana's national Beach Soccer team, the Black Sharks, have booked their ticket to the 2026 CAF Beach Soccer Africa Cup of Nations in Senegal after securing a 7-4 victory over arch-rivals Nigeria in the final round of qualifiers.

Ghana News.title: Black Maidens fall to Norway in U-17 Women’s World Cup opener
Ghana News.content:
Black Maidens

Ghana's Black Maidens began their FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup campaign with a 3-0 defeat to Norway in their Group C opener at the Mohammed VI Football Complex on Sunday.

Norway broke the deadlock in spectacular fashion when Isabella Lepore rifled home a thunderous effort from 30 yards, her strike smashing the underside of the crossbar before nestling in the back of the net.

The Europeans doubled their lead with another superb finish. Hanne Nesse collected the ball on the edge of the box and laid it off to Maia Melgard, who shifted onto her left foot and curled home a sumptuous second.

Coach Joe Nana Adarkwa's side responded well after the break and came close to pulling one back when substitute Cynthia Obinsrewuo was sent clean through on goal, but Norwegian goalkeeper Erla Braathen stood tall to deny her.

Norway sealed their maiden U-17 Women's World Cup victory midway through the second half when Melgard played a neat one-two from a corner, cut inside and unleashed another jaw-dropping effort that left goalkeeper Belinda Manu Aklie with no chance.

The result leaves Ghana with work to do in Group C, with heavyweights Brazil and Canada still to come.

The Maidens will now shift focus to their second group fixture as they aim to bounce back and keep their hopes of reaching the knockout stage alive.

Ghana News.title: Interest rates development continues to reflect more expansionary monetary policy environment – BoG
Ghana News.content:
BoG Governor, Dr Johnson Asiama

Interest rate developments in August 2026 continued to reflect the more expansionary monetary policy environment in the second half of 2025.

Relative to August 2025, policy and market interest rates declined, consistent with the easing of inflationary pressures and improved macroeconomic conditions.

According to the Bank of Ghana, real interest rates, however, remained positive during the period under review.

The Monetary Policy Rate declined to 14.0% from 25.0% in August 2025. The reduction in the policy rate by 11 percentage points reflected the cumulative monetary easing undertaken by the Bank of Ghana in response to the moderation in inflation during the review period, as well as improvements in macroeconomic fundamentals.

The corresponding downward adjustment in the Interbank Weighted Average Rate (IWAR) reinforced the easing of the monetary policy stance. The IWAR declined to 10.2% in August 2026 from 23.3% a year earlier.

Similarly, the average lending rate of banks eased to 15.9% from 24.2% in August 2025, reflecting a pass-through effect of the reduction in the policy rate to market rates.

Meanwhile, real interest rates remained broadly positive during the review period, reflecting the faster pace of disinflation relative to the decline in nominal interest rates.

Developments in the Treasury bill market were consistent with the general decline in interest rates.

The 91-day, 182-day, and 364-day Treasury bill rates declined sharply to 5.4%, 7.3% and 12.2%, respectively, compared with 10.3%, 12.3% and 13.1 percent, a year earlier.

According to the Central Bank, this decline reflected sustained investor demand at the short end of the curve, improved inflation expectations, and ongoing efforts by the government to reduce domestic financing costs.

Rates on medium- to long-term government securities, such as the 2-year, 3-year, 5-year, 6-year, 7-year, 10-year, 15-year and 20-year bonds, however, remained broadly unchanged, given limited activity in that segment of the market.

Ghana News.title: A remarkable journey of Steve Kyerematen: Insurance, reinsurance, diplomacy and leadership
Ghana News.content:
With 50 years of distinguished experience in Africa's insurance and reinsurance sector, Steve Kyerematen’s career blends technical expertise, corporate leadership, and national service.

From 1997 to 2007, he served as Regional Manager and Member of Operational Management for the Munich Reinsurance Group and Munich Mauritius Re, based in Accra, 1997, with territorial responsibility for West and Central African insurance markets.

Diplomat and Statesman

Between his careers with the Munich Re Group and the Activa Group, Mr. Kyerematen was called to serve his nation, Ghana, as High Commissioner to Malaysia, with concurrent accreditation to five South-East Asian countries including Thailand and the Philippines. In this role, he deepened Ghana’s diplomatic and economic ties across Asia.

Industry Leader

Until 2014, he served as a member of the Board of Directors of the Ghana Insurers Association. He also served for four years as Chairman of the Ghana National Bureau of the ECOWAS Brown Card Insurance Scheme, promoting motor insurance integration and free movement in West Africa.

Corporate CEO

He served for seven years with the Activa Insurance Group as founding CEO of Activa International Insurance Company, Ghana, and concurrently as Managing Director of Activa Finances that is Activa Groupe's Holding Company, from 2014 to 2017 in Mauritius.

Current Pan-African Board Leadership

He continues to provide strategic oversight across the continent:

- Former Chairman, Board of Directors, MiLife Insurance Company, Ghana

- Former Chairman, Board of Directors, Activa International Insurance Company, Liberia

- Former Chairman, Board of Directors, Activa International Insurance Company, Sierra Leone

- Vice Chairman, Board of Directors, Activa International Insurance Company, Ghana

- Member, Board of Directors, Activa Finances, Mauritius

- Former Member, Board of Directors, UGAR Activa, Guinea

- Former Member, Board of Directors, Activa Assurance Vie, Guinea

- Former Member, Board of Directors, *Activa Group Foundation (from inception)

- Currently Founding Promoter and Board Member of FBS REINSURANCE COMPANY, Lagos, Nigeria.

- Currently Chairman of VISAL Reinsurance Brokers Company, Ghana

- Former Secretary- General of the West African Insurance

- Companies Association (WAICA) from 1984 to 1988

A Legacy that Built a Continent’s Capacity

From underwriting rooms in Accra to diplomatic halls in Kuala Lumpur, Mr. Kyerematen’s life work embodies the very spirit of the AIO – African solutions for Africa’s growth.

His foundational contributions as a pioneer of the Forum in 1995 continue to underpin the Forum’s mission to strengthen continental reinsurance capability.

This recognition in Mauritius is a fitting tribute to a man who has served insurance, served his country, and served Africa.

The AIO African Reinsurance Forum salutes Steve Kyerematen – Pioneer, Diplomat, Industry Icon.

Ghana News.title: La Community vows to challenge La Pleasure Beach Redevelopment in court
Ghana News.content:
The La Community has declared its intention to challenge any plans to redevelop the La Pleasure Beach Resort without its approval, maintaining that the disputed property belongs to the people of La.

The position comes after the demolition of structures at La Beach in Accra, affecting facilities including La Pleasure Beach and the Polo Beach Club, situated close to the Labadi Beach Hotel.

The demolition was carried out under the supervision of personnel from the Ghana Armed Forces’ 48 Engineer Regiment, with assistance from the Ghana Police Service.

During the operation, traders and operators of businesses in the area were instructed to leave the premises. The exercise has heightened tensions over ownership of the land and raised concerns about the future of businesses operating along the beachfront.

Addressing a press conference, the community’s lawyer, Nsiah Akuetteh, disclosed that legal action had already been initiated over what he described as an unauthorised occupation of the land.

He accused the resort’s management of proceeding with the demolition without first consulting the community and warned that investors who attempt to develop the property without resolving the dispute could also be taken to court. According to him, the use of money or security personnel cannot substitute for legitimate ownership of land.

Mr Akuetteh emphasised that the community remained open to development proposals but insisted that any plans must begin with dialogue and an agreement with the people claiming ownership of the property.

He urged the resort’s management to engage the community and address the concerns of traders and other affected persons to prevent further conflict.

He added that the community would carefully assess any investment proposals and would not allow development to proceed in a manner that undermines its land ownership claims or the livelihoods of residents.

Ghana News.title: GSE’s Abena Amoah and Japan Motors’ Salem Kalmouni win CIMG Marketing Woman and Man for 2025
Ghana News.content:
The Managing Director of the Ghana Stock Exchange (GSE), Abena Amoah, and the Group CEO of Japan Motors, Salem Kalmouni, were named Marketing Woman and Marketing Man of the Year at the 37th Annual National Marketing Performance Awards organised by the Chartered Institute of Marketing, Ghana (CIMG).

The awards, which celebrate achievements for 2025, were presented at a ceremony held at Labadi Beach Hotel in Accra on Saturday, October 17, 2026.

Ms Amoah was recognised for her contribution to marketing and leadership in Ghana’s financial sector. Mr Kalmouni, who was the Managing Director of Japan Motors up until June 2026, received the Marketing Man of the Year award for his contribution to marketing and business leadership.

Other individual winners were Mavis Frempong, Head of Corporate Communications, Marketing and Brands at Consolidated Bank Ghana Limited, who was named Marketing Practitioner of the Year, and Thomasina Tettey, who received the Marketing Student of the Year award.

Ecobank and Multimedia Group were among the corporate winners.

Ecobank Ghana Plc was named Overall Marketing-Oriented Organisation, and Multimedia Group Limited was recognised as Media Organisation of the Year.

Many other organisations were recognised in sectors such as banking, telecommunications, retail, manufacturing, hospitality, insurance, and more.

Melcom Ghana won in both the Retail Outlet and E-Commerce Company categories. Japan Motors was also recognised in the Motor Firm category, alongside Mr Kalmouni’s individual award.

GOIL Plc was recognised in the petroleum categories, and Labadi Beach Hotel won in the hotel category. Adansi Travels was honoured in the Hospitality Facility (Allied and Support Services) category.

MTN Ghana was recognised in telecommunications, Enterprise Trustees in Corporate Pensions Trust, DHL Ghana Limited in international postal and courier services, and Myjoyonline in the Online News Portal category.

For the media awards, the Ginny Rice Campaign won in the Above-the-Line category, the CBG Electroland Promo took the Below-the-Line award, and Multimedia Group’s Galamsey Fight campaign (#Notogalamsey) was named the winner in the New Media Campaign category.

Joy FM’s Drive Time programme won the Radio Programme category, and the National Science and Maths Quiz, produced by Primetime, received the award for TV Programme.

Wilmar Africa Limited was named Manufacturing Company of the Year and also won the Product Manufacturing category with Frytol.

Other winners were Hollard Life for Insurance Company (Life), Star Assurance Company Limited for Insurance Company (General), Lakeside Estate Limited for Real Estate, New Crystal Health Services Ltd for Private Health Facility, and Amenfiman Rural Bank Plc for Rural Bank.

The awards also recognised Opportunity International Savings and Loans Company Ltd, Maroon Capital Micro-Finance, Forms Capital Limited, Smart Infraco Limited, Dynamic Data Solutions Ltd, Passion Air, Yom Yom Services Limited, Newage Agric Solutions Ltd, World Vision Ghana, Zesuza Catering Services, and Kivo Hot Shito in their categories.

Ghana News.title: Ridge Hospital opens medical oxygen plant to external buyers
Ghana News.content:
The Greater Accra Regional Hospital, popularly known as Ridge Hospital, has begun supplying medical oxygen to customers outside the facility as part of efforts to improve access to the essential healthcare resource.

The service is available to other health facilities and individuals who require medical oxygen, expanding the hospital’s operations beyond meeting the needs of its own patients.

The initiative is intended to help address challenges associated with the availability of medical oxygen and ensure a more dependable supply for healthcare delivery.

Previously, the hospital’s oxygen production was largely reserved for patients receiving treatment at the facility, but the decision to sell to external buyers has created an additional source of supply for eligible consumers.

The hospital’s oxygen production system involves compressing atmospheric air before passing it through a series of filters designed to remove moisture and other unwanted particles, including bacteria.

The processed oxygen is subsequently channelled through a pipeline network to hospital wards, where it reaches patients through designated outlets. Staff also monitor pressure levels within the system to ensure oxygen is supplied at the appropriate pressure.

Speaking to Citi FM, the hospital’s Head of Public Relations, Juliana Haruna, disclosed that commercial sales of medical oxygen commenced around February 2026.

She explained that the initiative was introduced by management to enhance healthcare delivery by ensuring the consistent availability of oxygen for both internal use and external supply.

Ghana News.title: Yusif Sulemana donates GH¢10,000 to Bole Nursing College TEIN, urges students to prioritise academics
Ghana News.content:
The Deputy Minister of Lands and Natural Resources and Member of Parliament for Bole-Bamboi, Yusif Sulemana, has urged members of the Tertiary Education Institutions Network (TEIN) of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) at the Bole Nurses and Midwifery Training College to prioritise their academic work while remaining committed to the party.

In a Facebook post on Sunday, the MP shared his nostalgic experience of joining the TEIN family at the college for the swearing-in of new executives and a welcoming ceremony for fresh students.

Mr Sulemana said the gathering provided an opportunity to interact with student activists and encourage them to take their studies seriously.

He stressed that academic excellence should remain a priority for students, adding that the NDC had a track record of rewarding TEIN comrades who demonstrate academic competence and loyalty to the party. He urged students to combine their political involvement with a strong commitment to their education.

To inspire the students, the Deputy Minister pointed to several former TEIN members and leaders who now occupy various positions in the current government.

He cited their progress as evidence that dedication to both academic work and party activities can create opportunities, encouraging students to stay focused on their ambitions while contributing meaningfully to the NDC.

As part of his support for the newly inaugurated executives, Mr Sulemana donated GH¢10,000 to assist the leadership in carrying out its activities.

He also pledged his continued and unwavering support for the group as it begins its work. The gesture, he indicated, was intended to strengthen the new leadership and encourage its members to remain active and committed to their responsibilities within the TEIN fraternity.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Mbappe scores two, Guler one, as Real Madrid find form before El Clasico
World.content:
Real Madrid beat Sevilla 4-1 a day after Barcelona thrashed Real Betis 5-2, as the Spanish giants prepare for El Clasico.

Share Mbappe scores two, Guler one, as Real Madrid find form before El Clasico on social media

Kylian Mbappe scored twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on La Liga leaders Barcelona to six points with ⁠⁠a 4-1 win over Sevilla at the Santiago Bernabeu, a week before the rivals meet.

Despite the absence of suspended Vinicius Jr, Real produced the fluid attacking football the team had been lacking of late, with Arda Guler again orchestrating their best work on Sunday.

After a stale opening, the Turkish international sparked the match into life.

Sevilla appealed for a red card following an incident involving Guler and Peque Fernandez, but Guler responded minutes later by collecting Yan Diomande’s pass and arrowing a shot into ⁠⁠the top corner.

Mbappe scored an equally impressive second in the 37th ⁠⁠minute, turning brilliantly to burst through on goal before calmly beating Odysseas Vlachodimos.

Fede Valverde, restored to right back by coach Jose Mourinho, made a crucial block to deny Felix Correia just before the hour as Sevilla threatened to work ⁠⁠their way back into the contest.

Diomande then exploited the space created by Sevilla’s more adventurous approach, evading his marker before sending Mbappe in ⁠⁠behind the defence. Andres Castrin brought down the French forward, ⁠⁠who got to his feet to convert the resulting penalty and effectively settle the contest.

Substitute Manu Bueno reduced Sevilla’s arrears with a composed finish 10 minutes from time after Mbappe cheaply surrendered possession deep inside his own half.



Diomande restored Real’s ‌‌three-goal advantage two minutes later, capping a fine display with a thunderous strike.

Eder Militao received a warm ovation when he came on in the 85th minute for his first appearance since undergoing ‌‌hamstring ‌‌surgery in April.

Mourinho will take encouragement from one of the most complete performances of his second spell at Real as they prepare for next Sunday’s pivotal meeting with Barcelona.

Real, who have won three straight games in all competitions following the international break, climbed ⁠⁠to third on 21 points, one behind Atletico Madrid, while Sevilla are sixth on 14.

Earlier on Saturday, Barcelona beat Real Betis 5-2 to make it nine wins from nine and ⁠⁠stretch their blistering league tally to 39 goals.

Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric Garcia and substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentin Gomez and Ez Abde replied for Betis, who played much of the ⁠⁠second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for head-butting Lamine.

Barca moved to 27 points, five above Atletico, who won 1-0 at Espanyol, while third-placed Betis have 19 and Real Madrid sit fourth on 18 before welcoming Sevilla on Sunday.

Elsewhere, Osasuna withstood second-half pressure from Racing Santander to win 2-0 in Jagoba Arrasate’s first game back as manager.

Two flying saves from Ionut Radu denied Alaves a point in a 2-1 defeat to Celta Vigo, while ‌‌Real Sociedad won 5-2 at Malaga.

World.title: The kingmakers who could determine Israel’s election
World.content:
Israel’s Arab-led and ultra-Orthodox parties face attacks but could hold the balance of power after October 27 vote.

In the run-up to Israel’s high-stakes election, few parties have featured more often in Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s attacks on rivals than Ra’am and the Joint List.

Together, the two parties representing the Palestinian citizens of Israel, who make up about 20 percent of the population, are projected to win 13 seats. If this is confirmed at the October 27 polls, the Arab-led lists could be critical to any post-election coalition, regardless of its political stripe.

They have been here before.

In 2021, Ra’am made history by becoming the first Arab party to enter an Israeli government after joining a broad coalition that briefly removed Netanyahu from power. Netanyahu had previously shown himself ready to negotiate terms for a potential government with Mansour Abbas, the leader of Ra’am, or the United Arab List. But instead, Abbas joined forces with the coalition of Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid to try to drive through some of the measures he had campaigned for.

This time, both the Netanyahu camp and most leaders of the self-styled Zionist opposition bloc have ruled out forming a government with the parties representing Palestinian citizens. Still, Netanyahu and his allies have sought to portray their political opponents as beholden to the Arab-led lists, while the opposition has been attacking them for their reliance on the minority ultra-Orthodox parties to maintain their own power base.

Opinion polls have consistently indicated that Netanyahu’s Likud party and the far-right coalition it leads are running neck-and-neck with the Zionist opposition bloc, with neither side on track to win an outright majority in the 120-strong Knesset.



“Netanyahu would work with Ra’am in a heartbeat, if it meant staying in power,” said Yossi Mekelberg, a Middle East analyst at Chatham House.

“The opposition, too, don’t seem to understand the consequences of their actions,” he said of repeated attempts across the opposition bloc to undermine the credibility of what may be a future plank in any government.

“If it came down to it, of course they’d accept the support of the party they’d previously vilified without thinking of how that will undermine their government, and undermine the votes of the large numbers of Arab Israelis who support them,” added Mekelberg.

In the lead-up to the polls, Likud has repeatedly used hard-hitting attack adverts to warn that if Netanyahu is voted out, it will be the Arab parties that would emerge as kingmakers in a new government potentially led by former army chief Gadi Eisenkot, the leader of the Yashar party.

“There is no Gadi without [Ahmad] Tibi,” said a Likud campaign slogan in reference to the leader of Ta’al, one of three parties comprising the Joint List.

The alliance, which also includes the Hadash and Balad factions, has said it could provide a so-called safety net to the anti-Netanyahu coalition by agreeing not to stand against it in a confidence vote, even if the alliance does not join the government. In return, it has said it would demand certain conditions, including a path to Palestinian statehood and fighting organised crime.

Combatting the wave of violent crime that has been allowed to engulf Palestinian communities, as well as addressing discriminatory government policies, including on housing, have also been the focus of Ra’am ahead of the election.

Established in 1996, the party has already distanced itself from its religiously conservative foundations. In December 2025, Abbas said the party’s political decision-making body would separate from its religious council. Eight months later, it selected its electoral list independently for the first time and placed the Jewish Zionist Yoav Segalovitz, a former senior police commander and deputy public security minister in the Bennett-Lapid government, second on its slate.

Describing Ra’am as “one of the most interesting parties” of this year’s election, Mekelberg said: “Through Mansour Abbas, they are continually reinventing themselves without appearing opportunist.”

The upcoming election is the first since the Hamas-led attack in southern Israel of October 7, 2023 that led to the killing of an estimated 1,200 people, and triggered Israel’s genocidal war on Gaza.



The war has also sped up a political shift to the right, with Arab-led parties increasingly targeted by right-wing figures seeking to cast them as complicit in the October 7 assault.

In May, Bennett apologised for going into government with Ra’am, while in September, Netanyahu’s Likud and the Otzma Yehudi party of National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir petitioned to bar Ra’am and the Joint List from the election.

On September 23, the Central Elections Committee, whose members are drawn from the Knesset’s parties, voted to disqualify both lists, as well as two individual candidates.

Balad leader Sami Abu Shehadeh was to be barred over an article he wrote on October 8, 2023 describing the Hamas-led attack of the previous day as an “important historic event”. Ofer Cassif, a Jewish politician with Hadash, was targeted in a petition filed by Likud that cited legal prohibitions on candidates who support “an armed struggle by an enemy state or terrorist organisation against the State of Israel”.

On October 2, the Supreme Court unanimously overturned the disqualifications of the Joint List and Ra’am, as well as Cassif’s, by a 7-2 majority. Abu Shehadeh had withdrawn his candidacy a day earlier, after it became clear the court was likely to uphold his disqualification.

Speaking to Al Jazeera, Cassif later called it “a political decision far more than a judicial one”, driven by “fear that they’re going to need us”.

Orly Noy, a Balad candidate and the first Jewish politician to be voted onto the party list’s top five, said it was “safe to say” that the alliance is not going to be part of the next ruling coalition.

“It depends if the other parties want to prioritise the wishes of their voters or their own racism. However, even if we’re excluded, we can still gain concessions from any coalition in return for our support,” she added. “That might not mean ending the occupation, which of course would be ideal, but there’s a lot we can still do that will make people’s lives better.”

Fallout

The taint of October 7 has not only extended to Arab parties unconnected to the events of that day, but also to ultra-Orthodox Jewish parties.

As routine partners in Likud’s governing coalitions, they have faced accusations by many leading opponents of draft-dodging, while drawing heavily on what many regard as a generous state welfare package.

Israel’s ultra-Orthodox community is largely represented by two parties: Shas, which draws on Jews of Spanish, North African and Middle Eastern descent; and United Torah Judaism (UTJ), comprising Jews of central and eastern European descent. Each is polling at about seven or eight seats.

Rather than focusing on foreign policy and taxation, their core aims tend to be shielding ultra-Orthodox students from military service, securing welfare support for the large families common in the community, where many men study rather than work, and protecting state funding for their schools and institutions.



Long seen as Netanyahu’s most dependable allies, they broke with Likud last year over its failure to legislate an exemption to the draft. The UTJ left the coalition altogether, while Shas quit the government but did not pull its 11 politicians out of the parliamentary coalition. Shas later gave up its coalition committee roles, and both parties boycotted coalition bills.

Nevertheless, the support of the ultra-Orthodox has come with a political price tag. In January, opposition leader Yair Lapid accused the government of sending billions “to the corrupt and [the] draft dodgers” while another possible contender for the premiership, the right-wing Avigdor Lieberman, who heads the Yisrael Beytenu list, likened Shas and UTJ to the Taliban over their lack of female representation.

World.title: China’s economy grows 4.5 percent in Q3, beating forecasts
World.content:
China’s economy has grown faster than expected in the most recent quarter amid booming exports underpinned by artificial intelligence, according to official figures.

China’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded 4.5 percent in the July-September period from the same quarter a year earlier, picking up from 4.3 percent growth in the second quarter and beating most analysts’ forecasts, figures released on Monday by the National Bureau of Statistics showed.

During the first nine months of the year, GDP grew 4.6 percent year-on-year, according to the preliminary figures.

While China’s technology-related exports have surged during the AI boom, growth in the world’s second-largest economy has been dampened by weak domestic demand and a sagging property market.

China’s ruling Communist Party has set a GDP growth target of 4.5 to 5 percent for 2026, which would be among the slowest expansions in decades, excluding during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Chinese exports surged more than 16 percent in the first three quarters of the year to reach 23.19 billion yuan ($3.47bn), according to the official data, largely due to strong demand for semiconductors and other tech-related goods.

Retail sales, a key measure of domestic consumption, increased 1.1 percent year-on-year in September and 2.6 percent during the first nine months of 2026.

Industrial production, which measures output in sectors such as manufacturing and mining, rose 5.5 percent in September, taking growth in the first three quarters to 5.3 percent.



Investment in fixed assets, which covers spending on real estate, factories and machinery, edged up 0.7 percent last month but contracted 7.2 percent during the January-September period.

Zhiguo He, a finance professor at Stanford University’s Graduate School of Business who studies the Chinese economy, said that while China’s economy is on track to hit official targets, Beijing will be wary of the continuing reliance on export-driven growth.

“I expect Beijing is getting 4.5 percent as wanted,” He told Al Jazeera.

“A managed slow slowdown is the best Beijing can hope for,” he said.

“Real estate is still shrinking. This is what Beijing wanted and a good thing, and China’s households have been adapting their expectations based on this.”

World.title: Pope greeted by crowds in first major appearance since lung cancer surgery
World.content:
Pope Leo pledges a gradual return to duties in an address to the Catholic faithful in St Peter’s Square at the Vatican.

Share Pope greeted by crowds in first major appearance since lung cancer surgery on social media

Pope Leo XIV has thanked some 15,000 Catholic faithful gathered in St Peter’s Square during his Sunday address, his first major public appearance since lung cancer surgery.

“Now that this delicate phase is behind me, I will gradually resume my activities, always with God’s help and your prayers,” Leo said.

The 71-year-old pontiff addressed the crowd from a window overlooking the square at the Vatican, where a week ago on the same occasion of the traditional Angelus blessing, he revealed that a nodule had been found in his lung and would be surgically removed.

The operation confirmed he had adenocarcinoma, the most common type of lung cancer.

Test results to determine whether the cancer has spread are still pending.

Leo said the experience of the past week “has made me feel especially close to those facing illness and infirmity”.

He told the crowd that he had “truly felt your support” and expressed “particular gratitude to the doctors, nurses and all the staff at Gemelli Hospital” in Rome, where he was treated.

The pope paused for a moment and waved before retreating into his apartment in the Apostolic Palace.

A delegation from Africa, in Rome for a Catholic meeting, danced and ululated after the pope’s blessing.

“He was always in our prayers when he was sick, and we are happy to see him today,″ Alain Kalembu of the Democratic Republic of the Congo said. “This is an expression of our joy.”



Meanwhile, Claire Holland from Jacksonville, Florida, United States, said she felt “very blessed” to be present for the pope’s return to his flock.

There had been doubts that a planned papal voyage to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru in November would go ahead.

The Vatican’s secretary of state, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told journalists on Friday that the pope may need to adjust the pace of his schedule “according to the condition of his health”.

But Leo’s surgeon, Stefano Margaritora, told Vatican News he believed there were “no clinical reasons why the trip should not go ahead”.

Latin Americans in the crowd in St Peter’s Square welcomed the news.

“We are all hoping for his recovery, and that he has gotten through the situation well. We know that he is OK, and we’re pleased,” Soledad Espinosa from Ecuador said.

World.title: Lula and Bolsonaro spar in Brazil’s fiery first presidential run-off debate
World.content:
Brazil’s president and his opponent lob a barrage of attacks on each other in debate a week before the October 25 vote.

Share Lula and Bolsonaro spar in Brazil’s fiery first presidential run-off debate on social media

Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro fired off a barrage of personal attacks during their first debate a week before a tight presidential run-off.

In a chaotic exchange on Sunday, the two men called each other “liar” multiple times, accused each other of corruption, dragged up various scandals, and clashed on issues from public security to healthcare.

Lula said Bolsonaro was “a habitual liar” and a “thug”, and physically distanced himself on stage from the candidate he called a “militiaman”, alluding to his alleged ties to Rio de Janeiro’s paramilitary groups.

Bolsonaro, who led the first-round election with 47 percent to Lula’s 45 percent, said it was better to keep Lula at a distance “because my wallet could be stolen”.

Throughout the debate, Bolsonaro, 45, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, paced behind Lula, shaking his head, smirking and scoffing as his adversary spoke.

The 80-year-old Lula, who is seeking a fourth term, demanded an explanation regarding a corruption investigation involving the older Bolsonaro, a question his opponent dodged.

The younger Bolsonaro responded by calling Lula a “clown”, and then parried by bringing up a potential corruption case involving one of the president’s sons.

Jair Bolsonaro has been under house arrest while serving a 27-year sentence connected to efforts to overturn the 2022 election, which he lost to Lula.



Cost of living, public spending in focus

Flavio Bolsonaro hammered away at the top concerns of Brazilians, such as the cost of living and crime, and accused Lula of “reckless spending” to get re-elected, referring to various social measures the president has announced during the campaign.

Lula countered by asking Bolsonaro about his plans to emulate the drastic public spending cuts implemented by Argentina’s right-wing president, Javier Milei.

Bolsonaro dodged the question throughout the debate and pivoted to different topics.

When his father’s handling of the COVID-19 pandemic came up, Bolsonaro admitted that this “wasn’t an area where we saw the best results during Bolsonaro’s presidency. I’ll offer a mea culpa here.”

Lula also sought to portray his opponent as out of touch with poor Brazilians, saying Bolsonaro had never used the country’s public healthcare system or taken a bus.

“My opponent only knows about buses from books. He has never even stepped foot on one. He has no idea what the world of work is like,” Lula said.

Voters show their colours

Ahead of Sunday’s debate, supporters of each candidate gathered en masse in public to show their allegiance.

Pro-Bolsonaro crowds wearing Brazil’s national colours of yellow, green and blue packed Paulista Avenue in Sao Paulo’s financial centre, where the candidate addressed the crowd.

Lula supporters wearing red, symbolic of his Workers’ Party, filled Brasilia’s plaza of government buildings, while students backing the president protested against Bolsonaro in Rio de Janeiro.

“We need the current government to remain in power. If another government comes in, we’re, excuse my language, screwed,” said Lula supporter Sonia Maria at the Brasilia rally.

“I don’t like bandits. Out with Lula!” said Bolsonaro backer Vera de Sousa in Sao Paulo.

Also on Sunday, Brazil’s federal police asked the country’s Supreme Court to open an investigation into Bolsonaro over a money laundering accusation involving a lawyer close to him.

The presidential candidate is already under investigation for his links to Daniel Vorcaro, a disgraced former banker who financed a movie about Jair Bolsonaro’s life.

Lula spent 580 days in prison in ⁠2018 and 2019 on a corruption conviction that was later annulled over flaws in the investigation and legal proceedings.



Polls suggest a close race for the October 25 run-off, with Flavio Bolsonaro holding a slight advantage after finishing nearly 2 percentage points ahead of Lula in the first round on October 4.

Both candidates hope to engage the 33 million voters who stayed home in the first ⁠round, equal to about one in five eligible voters.

Sunday’s debate was the first between Lula and Bolsonaro after the candidates both ⁠declined previous opportunities. A second debate is scheduled for October 23, just ahead of the run-off.
