Shell expects first oil from the asset by end of the decade. Bonga North development holds estimated recoverable resource volumes of more than 300 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe).

The project is one of the mega deepwater projects on which the federal government and the industry are banking on to lift Nigeria’s oil production to 3 million barrels per day by 2030.

Kellagher said the successful coating in Onne means PCNL now possessed a world-class five-layer system able to compete for future deepwater projects globally, with partners working seamlessly to address technical, health, safety, environment and logistics challenges.

He said the development demonstrated that Nigeria had both the people and industrial capability to execute highest quality deepwater projects without exporting jobs and expenditure.

Managing Director of Tenaris Nigeria, Rosario Osobase, described the day as three milestones telling a single story of commitment, capability, and partnership.

Osobase said Tenaris was celebrating 25 years of growth, partnership, innovation, and shared success in Nigeria, moving from a service provider to a deepwater coating and insulation hub at Onne.

She said the inauguration of the thermal insulation plant reflected Tenaris’ confidence in Nigeria, while the Bonga North coating campaign demonstrated what world-class technology and local expertise could achieve when combined.

She stated that every milestone was made possible by employees past and present and by institutions championing local capability, adding that the new facility is an investment in people and long-term partnerships for the next generation of deepwater projects.

Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Oil), Senator Heineken Lokpobiri, who inaugurated the plant, said government had changed the narrative from investment decline to recovery, with Engineering Procurement and Construction (EPC) companies returning and several projects coming on stream between 2023 and 2026.

Lokpobiri said priority will now be given to companies with proven in-country capacity and equipment, stressing that retention of petroleum expenditure, skilled jobs and technology transfer must drive project execution.

Executive Commissioner for Production and Development, Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Enorense Armadasu, representing Commission Chief Executive, Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, said Bonga North answered the question of whether Nigeria could deliver complex deepwater projects to global standards.

Armadasu said the project showcaseed partnership where SNEPCo and joint venture partners worked shoulder to shoulder with indigenous capacity, a model he said the commission was institutionalising under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) 2021 with over 15 high impact regulations.

He said several offshore projects, including Bonga SouthWest, Zabazaba, Bosi and Preowei, were expected to draw tens of billions of dollars by 2030, all requiring subsea infrastructure and facilities, like the Onne plant.

“The pipelines that will carry Bonga North production have been coated and qualified to international standards right here in Onne,” Armadasu said.

He added, “That is not merely a project milestone, it is a declaration of industrial capability.”

Armadasu stated, “This plant is not built for one campaign; it is built for a generation of them. Its presence tells every operator that world-class deepwater coating no longer requires a voyage abroad.

“To Tenaris, you have positioned yourself at the front of a decade-long queue of opportunity that will define Nigeria’s next deepwater chapter.”

World.title: 2027: Kwara is No Go Area for PDP, Says AbdulRazaq, Yari’s Campaign Train Visits
World.content:
*DG meets Emir of Ilorin, Ooni

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin and Adedayo Akinwale in Abuja

Kwara State Governor and Chairman of Nigeria’s Governors’ Forum (NGF), Alhaji AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, yesterday, said Kwara remained the stronghold of the All Progressives Congress (APC) since 2019, adding that the party’s unmatched popularity and consistent victory have made the state a no-go area for the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

The governor said the inauguration of the PDP National leader and FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, as member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council would widen the margin of APC’s victory in Kwara.

The governor spoke in Ilorin while receiving the delegation of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) led by Director General, Senator AbdulAziz Abubakar Yari, at the Ahmadu Bello Government, yesterday.

The team also paid homage to the Emir of Ilorin and Chairman Kwara State Council of Chiefs, Dr. Ibrahim Sulu-Gambari, CFR.

At least, 10 former governors, former members of the National Assembly, and former party executives were part of the delegation, including Alhaji Aminu Bello Masari (Katsina), Senator Rochas Okorocha (Imo) and Ali Modu Sheriff (Borno).

Others were Kebbi Adamu Aleiro (Kebbi), Abubakar Badaru (Jigawa), Danjuma Goje (Gombe), Ibrahim Shema (Katsina), Sani Yerima (Zamfara), Abdullahi Ganduje (Kano), Olusegun Mimiko (Ondo), Hon. Dimeji Bankole, and Hon. Olubunmi Ette.

AbdulRazaq commended the PCC’s composition and their preparedness for the task ahead, attesting to their capacity and contributions to nation building.

The governor also appreciated them for their engagement that featured the Speaker of Kwara House of Assembly and APC gubernatorial candidate, Hon Salihu Yakubu Danladi, his running mate, Hon Seun Oguniyi Adato, other top government officials and the state APC Chairman, Sunday Fagbemi.

He said, “We know that you’ve been going around the country, hitting the ground running. Even before inauguration, you were out doing your work. That shows the seriousness which you’ve attached to the job.



“I congratulate you for being nominated into PCC, the highest organ of our campaign. It’s because the party recognises your capacities, your contribution to nation building and what you can achieve.

“Now, we appreciate this courtesy visit. It’s important to know, to hit the ground running, you’re going to campaign, and to know that Kwara is solidly on the APC’s side of defence.

“The leader of PDP made our job much easier. The balance of the equation here is 70-30. 70% APC and 30% PDP. And that’s consistent from 2019 until the election. Nothing has changed except that PDP has continued to weaken.



“With the national leader of PDP being a member of our (APC) campaign council and declaring that his party, the PDP, will vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it means that the PDP 30% versus our 70% is now adding up to 100 per cent.

“So, this will be one of the easiest states for our party, because the two main parties in the state are voting for President Tinubu.”

Yari, on his part, said the visit was to appreciate the governor for his roles and to seek his continued support to make the APC succeed nationwide.

He thanked him for giving his team “a great reception” right from the General Tunde Idiagbon International Airport, Ilorin, saying that was their first time to earn such an executive honour since they started the tour.

“Your Excellency, we are here to pay homage. We know, particularly I personally know what you are doing to ensure that APC succeeds not only in Kwara but also in Nigeria.

“We know the role you are playing in terms of advice to Mr President and to the Council. Your concern is how this journey will be successful. I really appreciate all this, and we are going to continue working together,” Yari said.

At the Emir’s Palace, Yari reiterated the purpose of their visit to the state, saying the homage was to seek his blessing and prayers for the victory of APC candidates, particularly President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

“Your son, Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu, has done a lot for this country, and your son, the Governor of Kwara State, has done a lot for this state, from where he took the responsibility from 2019 to where we are today.

“Your Royal Highness, we not only came here to seek your support but also your prayers and blessings for Asiwaju’s re-election in 2027.”

The Emir, Dr. Sulu-Gambari, appreciated the team for the visit and prayed for the success of Tinubu and all APC candidates in the 2027 general election.

“The leader of the team, Senator Abdul-Aziz Yari, is a great man and all of you are great men in Nigerian politics. You are all going to be victorious and I wish you success in your future endeavours In Sha Allaah,” the Emir prayed.

In another development, Yari, also led chieftains of the party on consultative visits to the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi (Ojaja II).

Yari, in a statement by his media office clarified that the visits were not to seek political endorsement or mobilisation support from the royal fathers.

Yari noted that the visits were part of strategic engagements with traditional institutions ahead of the 2027 general election.

The director-general stressed that the visits were designed to strengthen engagement with traditional institutions, foster mutual understanding, and seek the support, blessings and counsel of revered traditional leaders as part of the Council’s nationwide consultations.

The visits, he added, were aimed at seeking prayers and blessings of the royal fathers, underscoring the moral and spiritual anchorage traditional rulers provide in the nation’s political process.

World.title: Presidency, Oyo Gov Bicker Over Allegations of Withholding N250bn NLNG Dividend Due Each State
World.content:
.FG says report is false and should be disregarded



.Describes as basically illogical and lacking economic reality the claim that a supposed single payout exceeds company’s entire 25 years lifetime distribution to govt purse



.Makinde stands by his claim, says presidency’s response side stepped central issue



.Wants breakdown of how the $3bn NLNG revenue gotten under Tinubu’s govt was shared



.Says findings show a N9trn shortfall due to states and local governments which federal govt acknowledged

Deji Elumoye in Abuja and Kemi Olaitan in Ibadan

The Presidency and Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State on Sunday disagree over the reported withholding of NLNG dividends of N250 billion due to each state by the federal government.

While the Presidency punctured the claim by Oyo governor as being false and should be disregarded, Makinde in another response saud he stood by his claims while asking for a breakdown of how $3 billion that accrued under the Tinubu’s government were shared among the three tiers of government.



The Presidency had submitted that report that the federal government was withholding N250 billion dividends accruing to each of the 36 states from the Nigerian Liquified and Natural Gas (NLNG) was false and should be disregarded forthwith.

Makinde had on Friday at the 2027 Budget Stakeholders’ Consultative Engagement held at the Olola Ogunlana Hall, International Conference Centre, University of Ibadan claimed the funds would not be released until after the 2027 elections adding that the Federal Government had spent the money.

“Each state was supposed to get ₦250 billion. We had already identified projects that would expand Oyo State’s economy. But they have now said the money will not be paid until after the election. Is the election more important than the people of Nigeria?” the governor said.

Reacting to the claim, The Presidency in a release issued by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga stated that

Makinde’s latest claim that the Federal Government is withholding the NLNG dividend windfall is false and should be disregarded.

He explained how the Federation Account is managed and how money is shared among the three tiers of government.

According to him: “Even as a one-off distribution, ₦250 billion to each of the 36 states amounts to ₦9.0 trillion, excluding the Federal Government, the FCT, and the 774 local councils.

“Under the Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) formula, states receive 26.72% of the distributable Federation Account revenue. For the states’ share alone to reach ₦9 trillion, total NLNG dividends paid into the Federation Account would have to exceed ₦33.68 trillion (about $25 billion) in a single declaration.”

The Presidency added that NLNG has never paid $25 billion in dividends to the Federation Account in a single payout.

It further delved into NLNG and its Historical Dividend Context saying

NLNG has paid approximately $21.5 billion in dividends to the Federation over the last 25 years, with less than $3 billion realised since President Bola Tinubu assumed office.

The Presidency also posited that any claim that a single payout exceeds the company’s entire lifetime distribution to the Federation—and is being withheld—defies basic logic and economic reality.

“We expect Governor Makinde to be more measured in his public conduct and utterances. Since he embarked on his presidential bid, he has chosen to play politics by making misleading claims rather than presenting verifiable facts. Indeed, he has turned false, unguarded statements and claims into an art form.

“He once described the huge financial flow from the federation account to states, including Oyo, as ‘voodoo’.

“Under Nigerian law, Governor Makinde is free to pursue his presidential ambition. He should desist from making falsehoods and disinformation the hallmarks of his campaign.

“We urge the public to disregard these unfounded claims, which serve only to mislead citizens and stoke needless disaffection against the Federal authorities,” the Presidency further said.

In a swift reaction on Sunday, Governor Makinde said he stood by his submission saying Presidency’s response side stepped the central issue at hand.

In a release issued by his Special Adviser on Media, Dr Sulaimon Olanrewaju, Oyo State Governor called for a breakdown of the $3 billion received under Tinubu’s government were shared among the three tiers of government.

Makinde added that earlier findings by a consultant had showed N9 trillion to states and local governments saying the federal government accepted the findings.

Oyo state governor in the release issued by his media adviser, Dr Sulaimon Olanrewaju, entitled “NLNG Dividends: Governor Makinde stands by his claim”, stated, inter alia: “We have read the Presidency’s response to Governor Seyi Makinde’s statement on the Federal Government’s withholding of NLNG dividends due to states and local governments.

“The response sidestepped the central issue: the Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF), with the Federal Government’s support, engaged a consultant to reconcile NLNG dividend payments. The exercise identified a shortfall of about ₦9 trillion due to states and local governments. The Federal Government accepted the findings.

“The report remains in the custody of both the Federal Government and the NGF. We trust the Presidency will not deny its existence.

“Governor Makinde is the NGF’s incumbent Vice-Chairman.

“The Presidency stated that NLNG had paid $21.5 billion in dividends into the Federation Account since inception, including $3 billion received under the current administration. But it did not explain how these funds were disbursed.

“Have states and local governments received their shares? How much did they receive, and how were those amounts calculated? What happened to the $3 billion received under this administration?

“Governor Makinde conducts public discourse with decorum and does not make unfounded claims or quote figures without a basis.

“We remain ready to provide further clarification while we urge the presidency to address the substance of the matter.”

World.title: 2027: Opposition Coalition Came Too Late, Tinubu Will Win Re-election, Plang Boasts
World.content:
Yemi Kosoko in Jos

Senator Diket Plang, representing Plateau Central Senatorial District, has dismissed concerns over the emerging opposition coalition ahead of the 2027 general election, insisting that it posed no threat to President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Speaking during an interactive session with journalists in Jos, the Plateau State capital, Plang argued that opposition’s efforts came too late, maintaining that the APC had already consolidated its political structures, expanded its reach and strengthened its alliances across the country.

According to him, developments within the ruling party, including the composition of its presidential campaign machinery and what he described as broad-based acceptance of President Tinubu across party lines, indicated that the APC remained firmly positioned ahead of the next electoral cycle.

“The coalition came deeply late because opinions, positions, strategies, inclusiveness and APC’s ability to dominate have already been consolidated,” he said.

Plang expressed confidence that the APC would secure victories not only in the presidential election but also in governorship, National Assembly and state assembly contests.

“I am very sure that APC will get the majority support of this nation. Other parties may win some positions, but they will not win the presidency,” he stated.

The lawmaker further declared that President Tinubu’s return in 2027 was not in doubt, adding that many political stakeholders within the APC were equally optimistic about the return of Vice President Kashim Shettima and key leaders of the National Assembly.

On the debate over whether President Tinubu should personally traverse the country to campaign, Plang said such arguments misunderstood the realities of political mobilisation in a democracy as large as Nigeria.

He maintained that no presidential candidate could physically visit every polling unit in the federation and that campaigns were traditionally conducted through layers of political representation extending from national and zonal structures down to states, local governments, wards and polling units.

“You cannot expect a presidential candidate to visit every polling unit in Nigeria. Campaigns are built on representation. What matters is that the message reaches the people through established structures,” he said.

World.title: Kwankwaso Rules Out Withdrawal from  Presidential Election, Rejects ADC Alliance
World.content:
*Dismisses speculation over last-minute deal with opposition party

*Says neither APC nor ADC offers Nigerians the alternative his ticket represents

*You can’t distract us, your response exposes alleged alliance with Tinubu, says ADC-PCC

Chuks Okocha and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Vice-Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, has ruled out withdrawing from the 2027 presidential race in favour of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) or any other political party, insisting that his joint ticket with Mr. Peter Obi, remained committed to contesting the election.

Kwankwaso, who is running alongside a former Anambra State governor, Peter Obi, said the NDC would not surrender its candidacy to another party, dismissing speculation about a possible last-minute arrangement with the ADC as unfounded.

In a statement expressing concern over the recent exchanges between the two opposition camps, the former Kano State governor criticised what he described as unnecessary attacks by the ADC Presidential Campaign Council on him, Obi and the NDC.

He argued that opposition parties should concentrate on presenting their candidates’ credentials and policy alternatives to Nigerians rather than engaging in exchanges that could undermine cooperation among parties challenging the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

“The attacks directed at me, our presidential candidate, His Excellency Peter Obi, and our party, the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), are unnecessary and unhelpful,” Kwankwaso said.

He accused the ADC campaign council of diverting attention from its candidate’s qualifications by raising questions about NDC’s intentions and suggesting that the party might eventually step aside for the ADC presidential candidate.

“Rather than focusing on presenting the competence, credibility and capacity of their own candidate, as we have consistently done by placing our credentials and record of achievements before Nigerians, the ADC Presidential Campaign Council appears intent on creating mischief against our party and ticket,” he said.

Kwankwaso maintained that the NDC would neither work for the APC nor enter into an arrangement to withdraw its presidential ticket for the ADC.

He said, “Let me state clearly and unequivocally: we will not withdraw our candidature for the ADC or any other party. We remain confident in our capacity, competence and readiness to lead Nigeria.”

The NDC candidate also cautioned his supporters against being misled by any suggestion that the party intended to abandon the contest as election day approached.

“We are aware that the ADC-PCC may try to mislead our supporters on the eve of the election by claiming that we intend to withdraw in their favour.

“The OK ticket is neither working for nor acting on behalf of the APC or any of its candidates. We see no possibility or reason to withdraw from the presidential race in favour of the ADC candidate or any other. These claims are unfounded and should be treated as such,” he added.

The NDC candidate sought to establish a clear distinction between his party’s proposed agenda and the records of both the APC-led federal government and the ADC.

He argued that neither party offered the kind of alternative the NDC claimed to represent, insisting that his joint ticket with Obi had the experience and national reach required to address Nigeria’s challenges.

“The APC-led government has failed Nigerians. The ADC offers no better alternative. We believe the OK ticket presents a credible and viable option, backed by proven capacity, a strong track record, credibility and broad support across both Northern and Southern Nigeria.

“We believe the OK ticket is a healing ticket committed to uniting our country and tackling critical challenges in security, education, agriculture, infrastructure, healthcare, the economy and other key sectors,” he said.

World.title: ADC-PCC: Kwankwaso Can’t Distract Us, His Response Exposes Alleged Deal With Tinubu
World.content:
But the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has dismissed Kwankwaso’s response to its earlier statement as diversionary, insisting that his reaction has further raised questions about his political alignment with the All Progressives Congress (APC) and President Bola Tinubu.

The ADC-PCC had earlier advised Kwankwaso to stop attacking the ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, and redirect his energy towards holding the ruling APC accountable for its failures.

The Council maintained that, as an opposition figure, Kwankwaso should be challenging the Tinubu administration over the worsening economic hardship, insecurity and declining living standards confronting Nigerians, rather than repeatedly targeting Atiku and the ADC.

In a statement, yesterday, the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, said Kwankwaso’s response had failed to address the substance of the Council’s concerns.

According to the ADC-PCC, Kwankwaso casually mentioned the APC in his defence but devoted much of his response to attacking the ADC, a development it said raised questions about his priorities as an opposition leader.

“Why is Senator Kwankwaso making our candidate the issue instead of confronting the ruling APC, whose policies have made life increasingly difficult for millions of Nigerians?” the Council asked.

It argued that Nigerians were more concerned about hunger, insecurity, high fuel prices, the depreciation of the naira and the crushing economic hardship under the APC-led government than political exchanges among opposition figures.

The Council insisted that these national challenges should be the priority of any politician genuinely committed to providing an alternative to the Tinubu administration.

World.title: Coach hospitalised after alleged punch by Sundowns’ Komphela
World.content:
Steve Komphela travels with Mamelodi Sundowns to Angola in the CAF Champions League. Image: Sundowns media

The alleged incident occurred after Sundowns played out a goalless draw against the Angolan side in a CAF Champions League qualifier. Reports from African football journalists claim tensions boiled over between the two technical teams after the final whistle.

According to unverified reports, an alleged racial insult directed at Komphela triggered the confrontation, with the former Kaizer Chiefs coach accused of punching Bianchi.

MAMELODI SUNDOWNS’ STEVE KOMPHELA ALLEGEDLY INVOLVED IN ALTERCATION

Reports claim Bianchi sustained injuries during the alleged altercation and was taken to a local hospital for medical attention. The Wiliete SC coach subsequently missed the mandatory post-match press conference, where his assistant coach addressed the media and confirmed his hospitalisation.



However, the circumstances surrounding the alleged confrontation remain unverified, and the claims against Komphela have not been officially confirmed.

CLUB AND CAF AND YET TO RESPOND

Neither Mamelodi Sundowns nor Wiliete SC has issued an official statement regarding the reported incident. CAF has also yet to announce any formal disciplinary investigation.

Further clarity is expected as more information emerges from Angola. For now, the allegations remain unconfirmed, with no official account establishing exactly what happened after the final whistle.

World.title: Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show: Kylie Jenner and Mzansi’s angel shine [video]
World.content:
Kylie Jenner made a surprise debut in the Fantasy Bra at the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show in Los Angeles on 18 October. Image: Instagram @victoriassecret

The Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show saved its biggest surprise for last.

It wasn’t one of the famous Angels who wore the Fantasy Bra.

It was a reality star and beauty mogul making her runway debut.



And the bra she wore is the most valuable ever made.

The 2026 show took place at Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, Los Angeles, on Sunday, 18 October.

In South Africa, it streamed live on YouTube in the early hours of Monday, 19 October.

KYLIE JENNER’S SURPRISE DEBUT

The night’s biggest moment came at the end of the show, when Kylie Jenner, 29, stepped onto the runway in the Fantasy Bra.

The diamond-covered piece is valued at $50 million (about R823 million), making it the most valuable Fantasy Bra ever made.

According to reports, Jenner is the first model outside the official Victoria’s Secret line-up to wear it.



She paired it with white angel wings, while boyfriend Timothée Chalamet and mom Kris Jenner watched from the audience.

THE RETURN OF THE FANTASY BRA

It’s the first time a Fantasy Bra has appeared on the runway since 2018, when Swedish model Elsa Hosk wore it.

The tradition dates back to 1996, when supermodel Claudia Schiffer wore the first one.

This year’s bra was created with a luxury jewellery house, and features diamonds in a range of shapes and sizes.

Its centrepiece is a yellow diamond, reportedly worth around $22 million (about R362 million).

Not everyone was impressed.

Some fans took to social media to question why the honour went to Jenner, rather than one of the show’s long-time models.

MZANSI’S ANGEL SHINES

South Africa had its own star on the runway.

Candice Swanepoel, who grew up in Mooi River, KwaZulu-Natal, wore several looks during the show, including a gleaming gold number.

She walked alongside fellow Victoria’s Secret favourites, including Adriana Lima, Alessandra Ambrosio and Joan Smalls.

Other big names on the runway included Gigi Hadid, Ashley Graham, Paloma Elsesser, Anok Yai, Liu Wen and Alex Consani.

WHO PERFORMED AT THE VICTORIA’S SECRET FASHION SHOW?

The music was just as star-studded as the runway.

Megan Thee Stallion performed her hit Body as models walked alongside her.

performed her hit Body as models walked alongside her. Tate McRae performed Sports Car, and sang her new single Housewife live for the first time, as Gigi Hadid returned to the runway.

performed Sports Car, and sang her new single Housewife live for the first time, as Gigi Hadid returned to the runway. KATSEYE brought the pop-star energy.

brought the pop-star energy. Megan Moroney also performed.

WHO WAS IN THE AUDIENCE?

Besides Chalamet and Kris Jenner, the crowd included actress Nicole Kidman and singer Tinashe.

One notable absence was Kylie’s sister, Kendall Jenner, who has walked for Victoria’s Secret in the past.

A RETURN TO LOS ANGELES

This year’s show marked the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show’s return to Los Angeles for the first time in 19 years.

It’s the third show since the brand relaunched its runway event in 2024, after a break of several years.

I’ll admit, I didn’t see the Kylie Jenner moment coming.

But my favourite part of the night? Seeing Candice Swanepoel on that runway, still flying the flag for Mzansi.

From Mooi River to Los Angeles, she’s proof that South African talent can shine on any stage.

World.title: WHAT to expect from MTBPS 2026 ‘reality check’ this week
World.content:
Here's what analysts from the SAIT and PSG predict we'll hear in the MTBPS 2026 coming this week. Image: File

Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana tables the MTBPS 2026 this week, and analysts say it’s going to be a tough one. Because February’s Budget speech was written before the US-Iran war, and that economic world more or less no longer exists.

Oh, what a difference eight months can make. Fuel costs have skyrocketed to record levels and previous growth forecasts look positively absurd in the current economy. As such, here’s the ‘reality check’ analysts predict we’ll face this week …

MTBPS 2026

Growth: Treasury forecast 1.6% for 2026 in February. The IMF cut its 2026 forecast to just 1% last week. And 1.3% projected for 2027. South Africa’s GDP contracted 0.2% year-on-year in the second quarter.

Treasury forecast for 2026 in February. The IMF cut its 2026 forecast to just last week. And projected for 2027. South Africa’s GDP contracted year-on-year in the second quarter. Fuel and inflation: Brent crude is above $100 a barrel, and diesel has jumped from about R17 to R33 a litre . As such, Stanlib’s Kevin Lings expects inflation to top 5% .

Brent crude is above a barrel, and diesel has jumped from about . As such, Stanlib’s Kevin Lings expects inflation to top . Interest rates: Reserve Bank has hiked them twice, taking the repo rate to 7.25% in September. This is instead of the cuts expected in February’s Budget.

TWO CAMPS ON BUDGET DEFICIT

The trajectory of SASSA grants has an enormous bearing on national finances. Image: File

Moreover, the SA Institute for Taxation (SAIT) expects a delay to Treasury’s debt-stabilisation forecast. Higher interest rates and a weaker rand lift debt costs and slow growth. Meanwhile, PSG expects a revenue overrun of R50 billion or more, with the deficit narrowing to about 3.5% of GDP. This is against a government deficit target of 3.7%.



A separate analysis puts the windfall higher at R70 billion, driven by corporate tax from gold and precious metals. Furthermore, PSG expects a fiscally conservative MTBPS 2026 that could set up ratings upgrades from Moody’s or S&P. As far as taxes go, SAIT calls it a resilience test, noting the minister kept his promise not to raise taxes in 2026. Therefore, it doesn’t expect any rate changes to be announced this Wednesday.

THE BIG GRANT QUESTION

Minister Godongwana said back in February that the details of the ‘expanded’ SASSA SRD grant would be revealed in the MTBPS 2026. Now is as good a time as any to finally put up or shut up. The R370 grant is funded until 31 March 2027, and the case on its regulations is before the courts. Estimates on expanding the grant to Basic Income Support could cost the National Treasury roughly R90 billion a year. Core SASSA grant beneficiaries will also be watching for any indication of movement on grants after October payments passed without zero top-up.

In conclusion, here’s what to watch for in MTBPS 2026 this Wednesday 21 October 2026:

Treasury’s revised growth forecast, versus IMF’s predicted 1.0%.

The deficit and primary surplus, versus the original 3.5%.

Whether debt stabilisation is pushed out to 2027.

Any signal on tax increases for 2027.

Core and SRD SASSA grant future plans and costs.

But what do you think? Is there anything you’d like to see addressed directly in MTBPS 2026? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Man missing after rescuing friend caught in rip currents – NSRI
World.content:
A 27-year-old man is missing after reportedly being caught in rip currents while attempting to help his friend at Alkanstrand Main Beach in Richards Bay. Image: Wikimedia Commons

A 27-year-old man is missing after reportedly being caught in rip currents while attempting to help his friend at Alkantstrand Main Beach in Richards Bay.

The National Sea Rescue Institute (NSRI) said its Richards Bay duty crew was activated at 17:33 on Sunday following eyewitness reports of a drowning in progress.

FEEL GOOD | Boy and his dog rescued at Yzerfontein Harbour – NSRI



Initial reports indicated that two people were in distress in the surf zone and appeared to have been caught in rip currents.

However, further emergency calls received while rescuers were responding indicated that one man had managed to reach the shore, while the other had disappeared in the surf.

On arrival, rescue teams confirmed that a 26-year-old man was safely ashore, but his 27-year-old friend was missing.

Friend reportedly caught in rip currents

According to NSRI Richards Bay station commander Norman Rautenbach, it appears that the 26-year-old man may have been caught in rip currents while swimming.

His friend reportedly tried to assist him but was then caught in the dangerous currents himself.

NSRI rescue swimmers and a rescue vehicle responded alongside the South African Police Service (SAPS), Police Search and Rescue, uMhlathuze Fire and Rescue Services, and Mounties Emergency Medical Services.



An extensive search was conducted, but no signs of the missing man were found.

The 26-year-old survivor was assessed by paramedics at the scene and did not require further medical treatment.

Search for missing swimmer continues

Police Search and Rescue teams are continuing their efforts to locate the missing man.

Police have also opened an investigation into the incident.

The NSRI expressed its thoughts and care for the missing man’s family and friends as the search continues.

Rip currents can quickly carry swimmers away from the shore, making it dangerous for even strong swimmers to attempt a rescue without assistance.

Beachgoers are urged to exercise caution in the surf and seek help from lifeguards or emergency services when someone is in distress.

World.title: URC: Kick off times for South African teams this weekend
World.content:
The Bulls, Stormers, and Sharks got their Champions Cup and Challenge Cup campaigns off to encouraging starts over the weekend as European competitions came briefly into the spotlight during a break in the URC.

Of course, it was a round of action that was heavily overshadowed by the tragic passing of Lions lock Hyron Andrews in an emotional weekend all around.

The Lions, who opted to play their Champions Cup match against Stade Rochelais in Andrews’ honour despite Friday’s tragic news of their teammate’s untimely death, were always going to be up against it with their emotions in tatters, and went down 31-14 in their clash against the former champions in France.

World.title: Julius Malema takes swipe at Helen Zille over ‘Gusheshe’ spinning
World.content:
EFF leader Julius Malema has taken a swipe at DA mayoral candidate Helen Zille after she arrived at a Johannesburg election rally in a “Gusheshe”. Image: X @EFFSouthAfrica

EFF leader Julius Malema has taken a swipe at Democratic Alliance (DA) mayoral candidate Helen Zille after she arrived at a Johannesburg election rally in a BMW known as a “Gusheshe”.

Zille made the entrance at the DA’s “Joburg Now or Never Rally” at the Nasrec Expo Centre on Saturday, ahead of South Africa’s local government elections on Wednesday, 4 November.

Popular nickname

Julius Malema criticised the celebration of activities such as spinning a Gusheshe, arguing that they do little to improve the lives of ordinary South Africans.



A Gusheshe is a popular South African nickname for the BMW 325iS, a car associated with spinning and car culture.

“You are celebrating a person who spins Gusheshe and you think that thing has to do with improving the lives of our people. How does spinning Gusheshe improve our lives?” Malema said.

He questioned whether arriving at a political rally in the car should be celebrated when communities continue to face challenges around food security and healthy living.



“How does entering a rally in a Gusheshe improve our lives compared to how to plant vegetables, sustain ourselves and protect food security and ensure that we live a healthy lifestyle? We have got our priorities mixed up,” he said.

Julius Malema’s remarks came as the EFF promotes its own mayoral candidate for the City of Johannesburg, Dr Tlaleng Mofokeng, who is competing with Zille for the city’s top political position.

The EFF leader praised Mofokeng’s education and experience, saying she had worked with many people.



Malema also declared that his candidate was superior to Zille, describing Mofokeng as “head and shoulders above” the DA candidate.

The exchange highlights the contest between the EFF and DA as parties seek to win over voters in Johannesburg, South Africa’s largest city and a key battleground ahead of the 4 November local government elections.

With the campaign gathering pace, candidates and party leaders are increasingly using rallies and public appearances to promote their visions for the city.



For Malema, however, Zille’s Gusheshe entrance became an opportunity to question the priorities of political leaders, arguing that food security, sustainable living and the wellbeing of residents should take precedence over rally spectacle.

World.title: Former Kaizer Chiefs stars Musona and Billiat shine in CAF Champions League
World.content:
Knowledge Musona and Khama Billiat scored as Scottland FC beat Petro de Luanda 2-0 in the CAF Champions League.

Zimbabwean stars Knowledge Musona and Khama Billiat scored as Scottland FC secured a 2-0 victory over Angola’s Petro de Luanda in the first leg of their CAF Champions League second preliminary round tie.

The Zimbabwean champions claimed the advantage at the National Sports Stadium in Harare on Sunday, 18 October, with the experienced forwards finding the net in the second half.

According to CAF, the victory puts Scottland in a strong position ahead of the return fixture, with a place in the group stage at stake.



Billiat and Musona deliver for Scottland

Scottland struggled to break down their opponents in the first half despite enjoying a numerical advantage for almost the entire match.

Petro de Luanda goalkeeper Hugo Marques was sent off within the opening minute after fouling Panashe Mutimbanyoka outside the penalty area, leaving the Angolan side with 10 men.

However, the visitors remained organised defensively, frustrating Scottland as the teams went into the break without a goal.



The breakthrough eventually arrived in the 67th minute when Billiat finished a cross from substitute Walter Musona, who had come on for Emmanuel Jalai.

Billiat then helped create the second goal, drawing defenders towards him before setting up his long-time friend Knowledge Musona to score in the 80th minute.

The two goals gave Scottland a valuable cushion before Friday’s return leg in Angola, according to The Herald.



Former Kaizer Chiefs stars make their mark

South African football supporters are familiar with the Zimbabwean duo’s time at Kaizer Chiefs.

Billiat established himself as an influential attacking player during his spell at Amakhosi, while Musona previously captained the Soweto club.

Their contributions against Petro de Luanda underline the value of their experience as Scottland pursue a place among Africa’s leading club sides.



Scottland coach Norman Mapeza praised the pair’s contribution, describing their experience as priceless as the club targets qualification for the group stage.

The result is particularly significant for Scottland, who are competing in Africa’s premier club competition after winning Zimbabwe’s domestic league.

Scottland face decisive test in Angola

Despite the two-goal advantage, Scottland must complete the job in the second leg to secure progression.



Petro de Luanda will have home advantage in the return fixture and will need to overturn the deficit to keep their Champions League campaign alive.

Scottland, meanwhile, will look to protect their lead and take another step towards a historic group-stage appearance.

World.title: Hawks rescue three Peruvian women in Gqeberha trafficking probe
World.content:
The Hawks rescued three Peruvian women from a Gqeberha lodge during an investigation into suspected human trafficking and cybercrime. Image: Sowetan

The Hawks have rescued three Peruvian women from a Gqeberha lodge after uncovering a suspected human trafficking and cybercrime operation linked to fraudulent job offers.

The Hawks and Home Affairs immigration officials raided the property in Bluewater Bay on Friday, 16 October, after the Peruvian government raised concerns about an 18-year-old woman who had allegedly travelled to South Africa for a call centre job.

Instead, she reportedly found herself at a lodge where people allegedly carried out online scams targeting victims in Peru.



Eastern Cape Hawks spokesperson Warrant Officer Ndiphiwe Mhlakuvana said the woman’s father played a crucial role in helping authorities track down the property.

FAKE JOB OFFER LEADS WOMAN TO GQEBERHA

According to Mhlakuvana, the 18-year-old arrived at OR Tambo International Airport on 2 October before travelling to Gqeberha the following day.

Recruiters had allegedly promised her employment at an online call centre.

However, when she arrived at the Bluewater Bay lodge, she discovered that the operation differed significantly from the job she had expected.

Investigators believe those running the operation used the premises to conduct online scams targeting people in Peru. Participants allegedly had to communicate in Spanish.

The young woman contacted her father in Peru and shared information about her location.



Her father alerted authorities, prompting the Peruvian government to raise the alarm through the National Human Trafficking Hotline.

“The information was relayed through the appropriate channels, leading to the law enforcement intervention,” Mhlakuvana said.

HAWKS FIND 26 PEOPLE DURING RAID

Hawks investigators and Home Affairs officials arrived at the lodge at approximately 17:00 on Friday.

They found 26 people, including 14 Peruvian women and 12 men.

The men included two South Africans allegedly working as drivers, two Chinese nationals identified as tenants linked to the online business and eight Peruvian nationals.

Investigators are still trying to establish each person’s role in the suspected operation.

Officers removed the 18-year-old and two other Peruvian women who had reportedly arrived in South Africa on the same date.

Authorities took the three women to a place of safety, where they will receive further assistance and support.

POLICE SEIZE COMPUTERS AND CELLPHONES

During the operation, investigators seized laptops, desktop computers and cellphones as they pursued allegations of human trafficking, fraudulent recruitment and cybercrime.

Police also took the remaining 23 people to various police stations to verify their immigration status and investigate their possible involvement in criminal activities.

Mhlakuvana confirmed that the Hawks had not arrested anyone by Sunday, 18 October.

The investigation remains ongoing.

Eastern Cape Hawks acting provincial head Brigadier Romeo Petrus praised the National Human Trafficking Hotline and the joint operation that led to the women’s rescue.

Investigators will now examine the seized electronic devices and establish whether those involved committed any criminal offences.

World.title: The Voting Booth | 18 October 2026
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Voting Booth, eNCA’s special elections programme, unpacks the findings of the eNCA–MarkData survey, conducted across six of South Africa’s metropolitan municipalities, offering a snapshot of voter sentiment ahead of the Local Government Elections on Wednesday, 4 November.

But there’s more to these findings than voting intentions.

World.title: BMA tech puts brakes on cross-border vehicle smuggling
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Syndicates smuggling stolen vehicles across South Africa’s borders could soon find it harder to evade the law, as the Border Management Authority (BMA) turns to technology to strengthen its crackdown.

The BMA has introduced a digital system that uses intelligence to flag suspicious vehicles and help officers intercept them at ports of entry.

The system marks a shift from random checks to targeted inspections, aimed at disrupting vehicle smuggling and other cross-border crime.

At least 85 vehicles are stolen in South Africa every day, with organised criminal syndicates exploiting porous borders to move stolen vehicles into criminal networks.

But authorities are increasingly relying on technology to put the brakes on these operations.

The new Vehicle Targeting System, launched in April, is now operational at six ports of entry. Over the past six months, approximately 83 vehicles valued at R46.6-million have been recovered.

These include stolen vehicles, eight cloned vehicles, 37 cases involving fraudulent documentation and 33 financed vehicles recovered and returned to financial institutions.

A further 1,817 vehicles were stopped because their drivers could not provide proof of financing.

Strategically placed cameras scan vehicle number plates, allowing the system to flag suspicious vehicles for inspection before they reach the border.

The BMA demonstrated the system at the Lebombo border post in Komatipoort on Sunday, highlighting how intelligence-led checks are helping officers identify vehicles requiring further investigation.

BMA Commissioner Mike Masiapato said the technology was already delivering results, improving both traffic flow and the authority’s ability to intercept suspicious vehicles.

“We have seen very tangible results since we started operating the system,” he said.

“From a queue-management perspective, we have seen improvements in the movement of vehicles, because law-abiding travellers who have nothing to declare or nothing suspicious about their vehicles no longer have to undergo unnecessary checks.”

Masiapato said the system runs checks against several databases in the background, allowing officers to focus on vehicles flagged for further investigation.

“When a vehicle is flagged for interception or further investigation, officers on the ground are alerted and can pull it aside for inspection,” he said.

“We have seen improvements in traffic flow, but also in our ability to intercept vehicles.”

World.title: Women await justice for police killings in Brazil
World.content:
SALVADOR - The sea, facing a favela in Brazil's northeastern city of Salvador, serves as a backdrop for the last photograph Vilma Alves de Oliveira has with her son, who she claims was killed by police three years ago.

Joao Vitor, who worked as a pizza maker, was 20 years old when he went out for a beer with a friend in 2023. Witnesses told Oliveira that police showed up and opened fire.

"No mother is prepared to lose a child, much less in this way. My son's life was taken by the police, the armed wing of the state," said Oliveira, 49, who is Black and lives in the Nordeste de Amaralina complex.

The neighbourhood, with its steep streets and the lingering scent of dende -- the palm oil central to cooking in Bahia -- is one of the epicentres of police violence in the state.

According to the Brazilian Public Security Yearbook, there were 1,570 deaths resulting from law enforcement operations in the state in 2025, the highest figure in the country.

Virtually none of the cases have resulted in legal proceedings.

World.title: Rubio seeks to strengthen US foothold in Central Asia
World.content:
SAMARKAND - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio launches into talks on Monday with key Central Asian states before heading to India on a tour to a region with vast natural resources and China as a key competitor.

Rubio arrived in Uzbekistan's Silk Road city of Samarkand late Sunday to prepare for talks with top officials from Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Uzbek hosts.

The leaders of the five former Soviet republics held talks with US President Donald Trump at the White House in November last year.

At the head of a delegation that includes 200 business executives, Rubio will visit the Samarkand's old city, a historic staging post between China and the West, before starting talks aimed at the modern-day rivalry with China.

With the United States stuck in a war with Iran and unable to halt the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Rubio has stepped up his foreign travel with recent trips to Europe and Latin America while leaving Trump to handle the conflicts and the US mid-term elections.

But Rubio insisted this week's tour is of strategic importance.

"This is an important relationship," he said shortly before his departure. "There's countries you'd like to get to because we want to build our relationships with them."

A senior State Department official told reporters on Friday that Rubio was demonstrating US goodwill towards the "deepening partnership across Central Asia", especially in the energy sector.

- India deal 'very close' -

After Uzbekistan, Rubio will go to India where the US ambassador is Sergio Gor, who was born in Uzbekistan and is also the US special envoy for Central Asia.

The central Asian states remain linked to Russia by energy pipelines and security and migratory networks, but Russian influence has eroded since the start of its invasion of Ukraine.

And China has reaped the benefits. It is now the main trade partner of all five nations.

Chinese companies have signed a number of energy-related deals, seeking to buy natural gas in Turkmenistan, uranium in Kazakhstan and rare earths in Tajikistan.

On his second visit to India this year, Rubio will have stops in Mumbai and Jamnagar in Gujarat state. Both are major port cities.

"We're very close" to a trade deal with India, a second senior US official said of negotiations with the Asian giant that have dragged on for months.

The two sides reached a provisional agreement in February aimed at reducing US tariffs on Indian products.

But legal battles in US courts over Trump's tariffs have fuelled uncertainty about when a bilateral trade deal could take effect.

India-US relations were also rattled when Trump imposed 25 percent tariffs on Indian goods in retaliation for Delhi's purchases of Russian oil, but those duties have since been lifted.

World.title: 'Street Fighter' wins North America box office, buzzy doc stuns in 2nd
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Paramount's action film "Street Fighter" karate-chopped the competition this weekend with a $31 million debut at the North American box office, industry estimates showed.

However, a buzzy three-hour documentary on tech fraudster Elizabeth Holmes was the talk of Tinseltown, after a stunning $15 million debut on less than 1,000 screens in the United States and Canada.

"Street Fighter," based on the beloved Capcom video game, follows super-powered martial artists competing in a global tournament who uncover and battle a sinister conspiracy.

Andrew Koji, Noah Centineo and Callina Liang star in the film -- the third feature-length adaptation of the video game and the first since production company Legendary acquired the movie rights in 2023.

Jason Momoa and Curtis Jackson -- better known as rapper "50 Cent" -- also make appearances.

Analyst David A. Gross of Franchise Entertainment Research called the $31 million debut a "good opening" but noted "critics' reviews are weak and the audience score is soft."

"The film should recover its costs after playing in ancillary markets, in addition to adding value back to the franchise in all its forms -- in film, TV and games," he added.

In second place was A24's hotly anticipated documentary "You Can See Everything," co-directed by comedian Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim.

The film, which follows Holmes at her home in 2023 during the month before she began an 11-year prison sentence, took in $15 million on just 855 screens, according to Exhibitor Relations.

Holmes was convicted of defrauding investors in her medical testing company Theranos after touting lofty promises she couldn't deliver.

The scandal fueled a media circus and was chronicled in a book, multiple podcasts, and the biographical mini-series "The Dropout," starring Amanda Seyfried.

In "You Can See Everything," comedian Fielder places himself inside the action, like in his previous projects that blur the lines of documentary, social experiment and prank show.

The film has garnered much interest since its trailer -- showing Holmes unblinkingly asking Fielder "Why would I deceive you?" -- sparked a deluge of online memes, and a surprise debut at the Telluride Film Festival garnered rave reviews.

Deadline called the $15 million debut "easily the second best opening ever for a documentary at the box office after 2004s 'Fahrenheit 9/11.'"

Third place went to Universal and Blumhouse's "Other Mommy," which gained another $8.4 million after topping the box office last weekend with a $27.8 million debut.

The horror flick stars Oscar-winner Jessica Chastain in a dual role as a sinister entity terrorising a child -- made even worse by the fact that the demon resembles the girl's mother.

In fourth place was 20th Century's "Whalefall," a survival-thriller film that debuted to only $8 million.

The movie follows a scuba diver who is swallowed by a whale and has an hour of oxygen to escape.

"At a cost of $60 million, the film won't break even, even with relatively good business overseas," said Gross.

Fifth place went to Focus Features' new adaptation of the Jane Austen novel "Sense and Sensibility," directed by Georgia Oakley.

The film, starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and George MacKay, took in an estimated $7.5 million.

World.title: Boland strikes twice for Australia in rain-hit South Africa Test
World.content:
GQEBERHA - Australia's Scott Boland took two wickets in two balls on a severely rain-shortened first day of the second Test against South Africa at St George's Park on Sunday.

South Africa, sent in to bat, were 20 for two when play was called off after two short periods of play during which only 12.2 overs were bowled.

But it was enough for Boland to strike two crucial blows. He dismissed Aiden Markram and David Bedingham – South Africa's most successful batsmen in their defeat in the first Test in Durban.

Coming on as first change, Boland bowled Markram for 11 with his tenth delivery, a ball which nipped in off the pitch to crash into Markram's middle stump off an inside edge. Then he produced a ball which seamed away to have Bedingham caught behind first ball.

Boland was making only his 20th appearance in Australia's 50th Test since making a sensational debut when he took six for seven against England in Melbourne in December 2021.

He has had to wait his turn behind Australia's world-class pace trio of skipper Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood. He got his chance on Sunday, replacing off-spinner Nathan Lyon when Australia decided to field an all-seam attack on a green-tinged pitch in heavily overcast conditions.

"Scotty Boland has been incredible whenever he's played Test cricket," Cummins said after winning the toss. "When there's anything in the wicket, he gets a lot of seam movement, super accurate, and then even if it does flatten out, he brings control, experience. He's the whole package."

Rain started falling ten minutes after the toss and delayed the start by two hours. Markram hit two boundaries off Starc before play was halted with South Africa on 11 for no wicket after 5.3 overs.

Boland was brought into the attack after the players returned in the afternoon and immediately struck a challenging length.

New cap Marques Ackerman was unbeaten on five and captain Temba Bavuma was on four when rain brought what proved to be the final stoppage of the day.

Boland for Lyon was the only change from the Australian team that won the first Test by 214 runs.

South Africa made three changes, with fast bowler Kagiso Rabada returning after recovering from a hamstring injury. He replaced left-arm spin bowler Keshav Maharaj.

Ackerman and fellow batsman Matthew Breetzke replaced Tristan Stubbs and Kyle Verreynne with Ryan Rickelton taking over from Verreynne as wicketkeeper.

World.title: Carrim returns to court as bail hearing resumes
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - North West businessman Suliman Carrim is expected to return to the Pretoria Magistrate’s Court on Monday as his bail hearing resumes.

Carrim spent the weekend in custody at Kgosi Mampuru Correctional Centre following his arrest at OR Tambo International Airport on Thursday night.

The 49-year-old was arrested shortly before he was due to board an international flight to the United Arab Emirates.

His legal team is seeking his release on bail.

During his court appearance, Carrim told the court that he was travelling abroad for spiritual purposes and intended to return to South Africa.

The court is expected to hear further arguments on his bail application on Monday.

World.title: ANC faces court bid to recover R40m owed to Eltel
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The African National Congress (ANC) is facing a legal challenge over an alleged R40-million debt owed to digital services company Eltel for services provided during the 2019 elections.

Eltel founder Asif Casoojee says repeated attempts to recover the outstanding amount have been unsuccessful.

Court documents show Eltel is seeking to recover the original R24-million debt, along with R13-million in interest and R2.9-million in legal fees.

Casoojee has approached the South Gauteng High Court, seeking an order directing the Independent Electoral Commission (IEC) to redirect funds allocated to the ANC towards settling the outstanding debt.

The matter is set to be heard on 27 October.

World.title: Ruto-Moi fallout: State's daring occupation as armed GSU storm Moi's family property
World.content:
Gideon Moi’s family’s disputed property near Eldoret State Lodge. [Peter Ochieng, Standard]

For nearly a year, private security guards had watched over the five-acre property near the Eldoret State Lodge, going about their daily routine without incident.

But on Friday morning, that routine was abruptly interrupted when armed General Service Unit (GSU) officers arrived and ordered them to leave by 4 pm.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
