World.title: Liberia Conducts First National Honeybee Survey to Boost Beekeeping
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Ministry of Agriculture(MOA), in collaboration with the Society for the Conservation of Nature Liberia (SCNL) and other partners, has convened a national workshop to validate findings from Liberia’s first national honeybee survey, aimed at establishing baseline data to guide the development of the country’s beekeeping industry.

By Francis G. Boayue

The validation workshop held over the weekend brought together stakeholders in agriculture, beekeeping and conservation to review the survey findings, identify challenges facing honey producers, and recommend measures to strengthen production, improve market access, and promote sustainable beekeeping practices.



The survey covers Liberia’s 15 counties and seeks to establish baseline information on the number and distribution of beekeepers, honey production trends, harvesting methods, and the marketing of honey products.

Austin G. Yeanay, Director of Extension at the Ministry of Agriculture, welcomed participants and expressed optimism that the findings would provide useful information to advance the sector.

Yeanay acknowledged that the survey process had faced delays but said the information gathered from the field would provide a basis for discussions and further action. He encouraged participants to carefully review the findings and contribute to deliberations that would help move the beekeeping sector forward.

Cecil S. Wilson, Country Director of Universal Outreach, said the survey presented an opportunity to understand the current state of beekeeping in Liberia, particularly in areas where organizations have supported the activity for several years.

Wilson, who said he had spent 14 years working in Liberia, noted that the initiative would help stakeholders assess developments in the sector and identify barriers to its growth.

He urged participants to pay close attention to the findings and provide meaningful contributions to ensure the final report accurately reflects the realities of beekeeping across the country.

Michael E. Taire, Program Manager of SCNL, described the survey as significant, noting that Liberia had not previously conducted a national assessment of honey production.

According to Taire, the findings will establish a baseline against which future changes in the number of beekeepers, production levels, and market participation can be measured.

He explained that the survey examines the number of farmers engaged in honeybee production, their geographic distribution, harvesting practices and the plant species that attract bees.

The assessment also considers how beekeepers process, package and market their products, including whether they sell locally or supply supermarkets and other larger markets.

Taire said the information would help stakeholders determine whether honey production is increasing or declining and identify opportunities to improve the competitiveness of Liberian honey.

He added that the findings could inform strategies to expand market access and explore opportunities for exporting Liberian honey to other countries.

The initiative is supported by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) through the Apimondia program, with the Ministry of Agriculture taking the lead in collaboration with SCNL and other organizations involved in beekeeping development.

Other partners identified during the workshop included the Wild Chimpanzee Foundation, Samaritan’s Purse, Universal Outreach, and the Association of Beekeepers of Liberia. The names and roles of participating organizations will need confirmation before publication.

Beyond agricultural production, Taire said beekeeping also contributes to environmental conservation because honeybees depend on flowering plants, including those found in forests and agricultural areas.

He encouraged communities, particularly those living near forest areas, to embrace beekeeping while protecting forests and planting trees that provide suitable habitats and food sources for bees.

According to him, maintaining healthy forest ecosystems can support honey production while advancing broader conservation efforts. The validated report is expected to provide the Ministry of Agriculture and its partners with information to guide interventions, address challenges confronting beekeepers, and strengthen the development of Liberia’s honey production industry.

World.title: ACC arrests Chama education chief over K2.5 million maize and beans payments
World.content:
The Anti-Corruption Commission has arrested and charged Chama District Education Board Secretary Titus Mbewe, 56, over payments of nearly K2.5 million made while he headed education in Mkushi District. Mr Mbewe faces two counts of abuse of authority of office contrary to Section 21(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act, Chapter 91 of the Laws of Zambia. He also faces one count of wilful failure to follow applicable procedure contrary to Section 34(2)(b) of the same Act. He has been released on bond and is expected to appear in court soon. ACC head of corporate communications Joseph Mwenya announced the arrest in a statement.

The ACC alleges that between January and December 2025, while serving as Mkushi District Education Board Secretary in Central Province, Mr Mbewe facilitated payments of K1,424,115 to Frelun Commodities Limited for the supply of white maize. He is also alleged to have facilitated payments of K1,073,000 to Ichikwanka Multi-Purpose Cooperative for the supply of dried beans. According to the Commission, both payments were made before the Mkushi council secretary approved the contracts. Together the two payments come to K2,497,115. The supplies were linked to the school feeding programme.

“Further, he allegedly authorised full payment to the suppliers before the goods were delivered,” Mr Mwenya said.

On the third count, the ACC alleges that during the same period Mr Mbewe, acting with persons unknown, facilitated the abrogation of procedure. He is alleged to have claimed that the Evaluation Committee and the Procurement Committee had evaluated the tenders when they had not. Those committees exist to test whether a supplier can deliver at a fair price before public money is committed. Bypassing them removes the main safeguard in public procurement. Mr Mbewe was transferred to Chama after the period in question and was serving there at the time of his arrest.

School feeding programmes give learners a daily meal and are one of the most effective tools for keeping children, especially in rural areas, in class. Maize and beans are staples of the programme because they are locally produced and nutritious. Any loss of funds meant for such supplies falls directly on pupils. That explains the strength of public reaction to the case. Mr Mbewe is presumed innocent until proven guilty, and the allegations are yet to be tested in court.

Members of the public reacting to the arrest called for wider action. Some urged audits of all District Education Board Secretaries and head teachers, particularly over school grants, while others asked investigators to look at other districts, including Mkushi and Chipili. One reader proposed that corruption involving public money should be non-bailable and carry a life sentence on conviction. Another asked how the Grow Zambia Agenda could succeed with such conduct in the public service.

The arrest comes days after Minister of Health Roma Chilengi made public audit findings showing reported procurement irregularities involving contracts worth K1.4 billion at the Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency (ZAMMSA). Southern African Network Against Corruption (SANAC) president Kasenzi Kalenga urged other ministries to follow that example. He said ministers should ask difficult questions about procurement, spending, inventory and contract management in their portfolios. Dr Kalenga said permanent secretaries, boards and chief executives must act on warning signs early rather than wait for scandals to surface.

“For SANAC, this is the kind of institutional resolve that other ministries should emulate,” Dr Kalenga said.

He said accountability should be an ongoing institutional duty, not a reaction to exposed irregularities. Public funds, he said, must be used for their intended purposes and deliver tangible benefits to citizens. Effective internal controls, transparent procurement and consistent leadership were essential to restoring public confidence. The ACC has not said whether further arrests are expected in the Mkushi matter.

World.title: Jay Jay Banda case: rights advocate asks Amnesty to weigh the allegations as well as the arrest
World.content:
A Zambian human rights advocate has asked Amnesty International to look at the full record of allegations against former Petauke Central Member of Parliament Emmanuel “Jay Jay” Banda before it reaches conclusions about his return to Zambia. Sikaile Sikaile, who says he has worked with Amnesty International for more than a decade, said the organisation should hear from people who say Banda harmed them. He also asked it to separate legitimate political dissent from conduct that may amount to criminal offences. His appeal follows Amnesty International’s public interest in how Banda was apprehended and returned. Zambia Police confirmed on October 16, 2026 that Banda was back in the country and would be formally charged.

The case goes back more than two years. In August 2024, Banda was in custody at Chipata General Hospital, receiving treatment while he awaited trial on charges that included attempted murder and aggravated robbery. He escaped from that custody. In July 2025, while he was still at large, his case was committed to the High Court for trial. In mid-October 2026, the Zimbabwe Republic Police announced that it was working with Zambian authorities to trace him and several other wanted suspects. He now faces charges of attempted murder, aggravated robbery and escape from lawful custody.

Mr Sikaile listed several incidents he said Amnesty International should examine. They include the assault of journalist Peter Sukwa during voter registration in Eastern Province before the 2016 general election. Mr Sikaile said Mr Sukwa was beaten, urinated on and doused with petrol. He also cited broadcasts in which Banda allegedly called for President Hakainde Hichilema to be killed and for members of the Tonga community to be eliminated. Mr Sikaile said these remarks, if authenticated and read in their proper context, went beyond ordinary political criticism.

“Calls for the assassination of a political leader cannot simply be dismissed as political criticism, just as statements targeting an ethnic community deserve serious scrutiny,” Mr Sikaile said.

He also pointed to broadcasts during the 2026 general election in which Banda discussed the political situation with people linked to opposition leader Brian Mundubile. Mr Sikaile alleged that early declarations of victory before the official results, together with calls for supporters to take to the streets, came before billboards bearing President Hichilema’s image were destroyed. He asked Amnesty International to apply the same human rights standards whatever the political identity of the accused or of those allegedly targeted. None of these allegations has been tested in court. Banda has not been convicted of any offence.

State House chief communications specialist Clayson Hamasaka questioned why some human rights organisations were quick to condemn Banda’s apprehension but silent when the threats against the President were allegedly made. He went further and described Amnesty International as hypocritical for seeking clarity on how Banda was apprehended and transferred to Zambia. His remarks have set the tone for a sharp exchange between the Government and rights groups over the case. Choma South UPND Member of Parliament Trevor Mwiinde said the arrest gave Banda a chance to answer the charges and to substantiate the claims he had made against others.

“Emmanuel Jay Banda is an escapee who needs to answer to a lot of charges. As a country, and the Government in place, we believe in the rule of law and justice. So, we leave it in the hands of the police and the judicial system,” Mr Mwiinde said.

Governance and Development Advocates Zambia executive director Elias Mulenga commended Zambian and Zimbabwean law enforcement agencies for tracking Banda down. Acton Institute for Policy Analysis Centre executive director Solomon Ngoma also welcomed the joint operation. Mr Ngoma said freedom of expression must be exercised responsibly and within the law. He said democratic rights do not justify conduct that undermines state institutions or incites unrest.

The opposition has taken the opposite view. In a joint communique with the Forum for Democracy and Development (FDD), Tonse Alliance deputy spokesperson Anthony Chibuye demanded fairness and due process in the handling of Banda. He accused the ruling UPND of selective justice, alleging that its cadres had issued death threats against opposition figures, including Mr Mundubile, without being arrested. Mr Chibuye said the alliance does not glorify hate or threats but wants the law applied equally. He described Banda as a brother, husband, father and uncle who is entitled to humane treatment.

“The police should be professional in the prosecution of this matter,” Mr Chibuye said.

In an opinion piece, State House chief communications strategist Whitney Mulobela said the Government accepts several of Amnesty International’s points. He said Banda is entitled to medical care, confidential access to a lawyer, contact with his family and prompt appearance before a court. However, he rejected Amnesty’s description of Banda as a government critic in need of protection, as well as its reference to the principle of non-refoulement. Mr Mulobela said there was no record that Banda had ever applied for asylum in Zimbabwe, Mozambique or elsewhere. He added that Article 1F of the Refugee Convention excludes people suspected of serious non-political crimes, and that any challenge to the circumstances of Banda’s return belongs before the High Court.

World.title: Ask not what Jesus can do for you, but what you can do for Him
World.content:
By Edward Chisanga

Why do we always ask Jesus to give us bread?

All along, my prayers have been loaded with requests for Jesus to look after me, to find food and water for me, to look after my family, to watch over me when driving, walking, sleeping and eating. I ask Him to help me become rich, wise, intelligent and professional. I have asked Jesus to guard me and my family against enemies, jealousy, hate, malice, wild animals and insects and others that threaten my life. In short, I ask Him to give me bread (Bread here, meaning all nice things). I’ve asked Him to heel me when sick; to give my family many blessings and to provide for many other wishes.

In the foregoing paragraph, I have just described a loop-sided relationship between Zambians and Jesus. We engage in a relationship that’s not mutually beneficial with Jesus. It’s called a parasitic relationship, in which simply want to receive from someone else. We simply stretch our hands towards them to give us and give nothing in return. That’s what 90% of Zambians do. We draw milk from a fat cow until it dries. We don’t know how to give back or reciprocate. Now, we’ve extended it to the partnership with our Lord Jesus from whom we only ask and not give. When we pray, we always ask Jesus to give us favors. Now, I reflect back to see the mountain of sins that my parents and I committed and continue to, and ask for their forgiveness. In this article, I share with the reader that I have altered how to pray. I wish to focus on addressing past and current sins and asking Jesus to forgive me. I have completely dropped asking Him for bread.

What are sins?

What I read in the Bible and other literature is that the genesis of sin is Adam and Eve’s choice to defy God’s advice, “You’re free to eat from any tree in the garden, but you must not eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, for when you eat from it, you’ll certainly die.” I also read that the Old Testament ‘narrates humanity’s early rebellion against God and also shows us what’s forbidden in the famous Ten Commandments, including: ‘worshipping other gods; Making or worshipping idols; misusing God’s name; Failing to remember the Sabbath; Dishonoring parents; Murder; Adultery; Stealing; Bearing testimony and Coveting.’ The New Testament also highlights sins, including, sexuality, impurity, debauchery, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, discord, jealousy, fits of rage, drunkenness, orgies and others too numerous to mention.

A few years ago, I read an extraordinary religious book, “The way of Divine Love” by Sister Josefa Menendez, a Spanish nun that altered my life. In it are some extraordinary religious encounters, wonderful prayers and revelations between she and Jesus, including man’s sins against Jesus. In many and different forms, Jesus reveals how He’s grousing about man’s sins. In Gethsemane, He complains, “I live in the midst of sinners that I may be their life, their physician, and the remedy of the diseases bred by corrupt nature. And in return they forsake, insult and despise Me.” He grouses about lack of affection and gratitude.

He continues, “After having preached to greater crowds, healed the sick, given sight to the blind, raised the dead….after having lived three years with My apostles to train them and teach My doctrine to them…..I finally willed to teach them by example how to love one another, to put up with Myself one another, and how mutually to serve each other; and this I did by washing their feet and making their food.” Continues the Master, “But cannot you spare a few minutes in which to come and prove your affection and your gratitude? Learn also from Him that all important actions should be preceded by and vivified by, for only in prayer can a soul obtain the strength needed in life’s difficulties.” Jesus complains about the sleeping disciples that He found when they should have been awake, waiting for Him. He complains about His scourging and crowning of thorns on His Head and reads in His hand, the thirst, the Cross. He said, “All these suffering thronged before My eyes and pressed upon My Heart, while at one and the same time I saw all the offences, sins and crimes that were to be committed throughout the ages. O sinners who torture Me. Will this Blood bring salvation and life, or will it be shed in vain for you?”

Then He says, “My soul, already shattered and a prey to sadness, had to ensure still more deadly grief, for crushed by the weight of the sins of men, and in return for so much suffering and love, I saw only outrages and ingratitude. The blood now pouring from My body and which I was soon to shed from countless wounds would be in vain for so many souls, many would be lost, a still greater number would sin against Me, and myriads would not so much as hear My name. Alas, at this moment, I see how many will turn away from Me, some will not listen to My call, others will hear but will not follow Me, others will respond for a time with a certain amount of generosity to the call of My Heart, but then will gradually grow drowsy and one day will say to Me by their deeds, ‘I have worked enough, I have been faithful to every detail of my duty, I have overcome nature, I’m no longer a child, so many privations, so much vigilance are no longer necessary, I need no longer endure this restraint.”

Referring to His disciples, He goes on, “I had chosen them that they might share My agony, pray with Me and by their company afford Me some consolation What were My feelings to find them asleep? O the pang of loneliness, and to have none to share in My sorrow. How often My Heart suffers this same grief, how often, hoping to solace among the souls It loves, It finds them slumbering. Another episode of Christ reminds us when He says, “Bring to me the souls who do not believe in God and who do not know Me, and those who have separated themselves from My Church.” He grouses about lack of affection and gratitude saying, “After having preached to greater crowds, healed the sick, given sight to the blind, raised the dead….after having lived three years with My apostles to train them and teach My doctrine to them…..I finally willed to teach them by example how to love one another, to put up with one another, and how mutually to serve each other; and this I did by washing their feet and making Myself their food.”

Finally, but non-exhaustive, Jesus complains about what we know as five wounds on His Body: The nailing of his two feet and hands and piecing on His right side. “They have pierced My hands and My feet; they have numbered all My bones.” I also recently discovered the wound on His shoulder caused by the carrying of the heavy Cross. He complains, “I had on My Shoulder while I bore My Cross on the Way of Sorrows, a grievous Wound which was more painful than the others, and which is not recorded by men.” Indeed, the Bible further reminds us of more painful sins of man. Isaiah reminds us, “But he was pierced for our transgressions, he was crushed for our iniquities; the punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed. Your shoulder wound reminds me that You carried more than I can imagine. He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross… by his wounds you have been healed.” Jesus is also greatly sorrowed by blasphemy and by the profanation of Sunday by our work and failure to go to Mass. Of course, these are only a few of the millions of sins of man.

Addressing sins

I cannot explain where it came from. But I just decided recently that I will radically alter the way I pray. I will no longer ask Jesus to give me. Instead, I will give Him. I have decided that I will pray Him vigorously, unashamedly, fearlessly, respectfully, and unquenchably giver Him means, I know exactly what constitutes sin that my parents and I committed and continue to because, either He himself has clearly, comprehensively and unequivocally listed these sins.

So, if what I have shared in the foregoing paragraphs constitute approximate sins or excesses that estrange us from Jesus, then my single most important task is to ensure I pray that they’re understood and forgiven by Jesus. For example, for the last sin I have listed, “Shoulder wound that we caused on Jesus,” I offer this prayer I found somewhere, “Most loving Jesus, meek Lamb of God, I, a miserable sinner, salute and worship the most Sacred Wound of Your Shoulder on which You bore Your heavy Cross which so tore Your flesh and laid bare Your bones as to inflict on You an anguish greater than any other wound of Your Most Blessed Body. I adore You, O Jesus most sorrowful; I praise and glorify You, and give You thanks for this most sacred and painful Wound, beseeching You by that exceeding pain, and by the crushing burden of Your heavy Cross, to be merciful to me, a sinner, to forgive me all my mortal and venial sins, and to lead me on towards Heaven along the Way of Your Cross.” Jesus, I ask that I accompany You on Your Stations of the Cross to pray for sinners who brought this anguish on You. I’m sorry for having offended You. I pray for souls in purgatory as well as the lukewarm souls. Help me not to go back to these sins. My Lord Jesus, you have made this journey to die for me with infinite love. So many times I have sinned, but I repent sincerely because I love You. Pardon me, my God. I will love you all my life.

I don’t ask Jesus to give me bread. I pray that he forgives me for causing grievous wounds on his body. So, when He says, “Truly I say to you, ask and you will receive, seek and you will find, knock and it will be opened to you,” you obviously have your own understanding and perhaps you’re right. But for me, it means I will ask Him, I will seek and knock so that I tell Him how sorry I’m for mistreating and causing Him death on the Cross. Never will ask Him for bread. I have changed my life. I want 90% of my prayers to devote to giving Jesus instead of asking Him. I pray that I will listen and do exactly what Jesus instructs such as obeying that I will not eat from the forbidden tree and ask Him to help me live by the ten commandments and other instructions because it’s sin not to. It’s undeniable that man disrespects the ten commandments. Most sin such as adultery, murder, stealing, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, misusing God’s name; failing to remember the Sabbath; dishonoring parents and coveting and many others listed earlier come out of them. We selfishly continue to commit them at the same time ask Jesus for favors before we address them. We murder in the evening and ask Jesus to give us breakfast, lunch and dinner the following day.

Jesus wants to live with us in order to help us address sins, to be our life, our doctor and curer of all diseases bred by corrupt nature. We don’t take advantage and pray that He lives with us. Instead, we forsake, insult and despise Him and ask Him to protect us from the people that we steal from. We prefer to live by ourselves, not with Him but continue to ask Him to help us to live longer and stronger. “Lord, help me to live with good health, protect me from the police and my neighbors so that they never see me stealing or killing. I ask this in your name. Amen,” We proudly say. Some information in the Bible also provides prayers that can help us address sins. One states, “I come to You, reflecting on the sacrifice of Your shoulder wound. Heavenly Father, through the shoulder wound of Jesus, I receive Your perfect peace. I take refuge in You and the power of Your shoulder wound.” We can also create our own prayers of forgiveness. We can reach out to Jesus by saying, “I come knowing that my parents and I sinned against you. The shoulder wound, other wounds, the scourging, piercing Your hands and feet and numbering all Your bones, insulting You, covering Your face with blood, sweat, dust and spittle, and other transgressions inflicted on You are but too numerous. In greatest humility, I ask for Your forgiveness of my parents and me. They’re reach out prayers sharing with Jesus the torment we inflicted on Him that He must forgive us for, and forget the past. We’re not asking for Him to give us bread.

I also ask Him that I pray for all sinners to come to Your yard and ask that You pray with us for forgiveness from God Your Father. I realize that sometimes You fight with Your own Father, the Lord on our behalf. When He gets angry and wants to destroy us, You stand between asking for our messy. We’re aware Jesus that often, You carry all mankind on Your shoulders, away from Your Father’s wrath when our sin overwhelms Him. Thank you, Jesus. We promise to reduce our sins to shred each day. I remind Him too, “I will no longer pray to ask you to give me all the good things that I want. Instead, I’ll reach out to you for tutorials that help me reduce the backlog of sins that my parents and I owe you. I’m aware that a debtor doesn’t go back to the lender to ask for more money before he clears earlier debts. I ask you Jesus that you help me and other sinners to adopt this approach to prayer. I also surrender myself to You and ask that on the basis of this approach, You’ll decide how much I have fulfilled in reducing the sin-backlog and consequently whether I qualify for You to buy me bread or not even when I don’t ask.”

I further remind Jesus that He washed the feet of His apostles before the last Supper for a great purpose, one of which is to remind us sinners that we can always recover our innocence through the Sacrament of Penance. Yes, ‘recover our innocence’ from the backlog of guiltiness I referred to earlier, that we reduce the sin-deficit instead of asking Him for bread. We must pray and put in practice what we pray in order for Him to forgive our sins. Some actions may look little but they matter. They can include planting flowers and trees in the yard of the Church to simply facelift the place, watering the yard, cleaning the inside of the Church, helping and showing communities how to pray, making simple monetary donations, showing great humility whenever we’re dealing with other people, winning sinners, loving and helping the poor, thanking and praising Jesus, etc.

Jesus, You ask about Your Shoulder Wound and say, “Reveal it to men and let it be known that any grace asked in virtue of this Wound will be granted. And to all those who, in memory of it, will honor Me daily by reciting 3 Our Father, 3 Hail Mary, 3 Glory Be’s, I will pardon them, all their mortal and venial sins. They’ll not die an unexpected death and at the last hour, they will be visited by The Blessed Virgin and will obtain Grace and Mercy.” And I promise You that I will reveal it whenever opportunity knocks. Amen.

Accepting that my parents and I sinned, I will pray, like St. Veronica who, as a sign of love and compassion offered You a veil to wipe the blood and sweat from Your face as You carried Your cross, I too offer my best new white towel to wipe the same blood and sweat from Your face and ask for Your forgiveness of my most disturbing sins and those of all sinners. I also accept advice of Sister Marie de Saint Pierre who wrote, “Man is invited to repair the outrages made to His God, and in a loving return He promises to restore image in our souls. Let us therefore wipe the august Face of the Saviour, soiled with the spittle of blasphemers, and He’ll wipe our soul, soiled with the spittle of sin.” Also, “Eternal Father, we offer You the Holy Face of Jesus, covered with blood, sweat, dust and spittle, in reparation for the crimes of communists, blasphemers, and for the profaners of the Holy Name and of the Holy Day. So, I will pray for Jesus to repair my outrages and those of other sinners instead of asking Him for bread.”

We pray, “Lord, each time we see priests, again, it’s a one-sided partnership. We ask them to bless our new rosary, our new house, our children, our parents, and our house, etc. Each parishioner coming to Church and speaking to the priest says nothing else but ask for favors. We wish to alter this from today. From today, we’ll say nothing but direct our prayers on the salvation of priests. God help our priests to be strong, healthy and sinless. Our priests have problems like us, and perhaps even more. Our priests are human like us. Hence, they encounter same and similar problems like us. Therefore, let us remind our Lord to continue to look after them with wisdom and to bless them that they don’t fall into temptation to sin.”

Then, “Jesus, give my heart the very sanctity of Thy Heart, or rather plunge it in Thy Divine Heart, that in It I may love and serve and glorify Thee, and lose myself in Thee for all eternity.” “O Thou who knewest all my misery before Thine eyes were fixed on me – Thou didst not turn away from my wretchedness… but because of it Thou didst love me with a love sweeter and tender. I beg pardon for having corresponded so little to Thy love… I beg of Thee to forgive me, and to purify my actions in Thy Divine Blood. I am deeply grieved at having offended Thee, because Thou art infinitely holy. I repent with heartfelt sorrow and I promise to do all in my power to avoid these faults in the future.” Jesus, I don’t ask for bread. I also ask all sinners and I to also reach out to disciples to ask for fogginess of our sins. Remember Jesus “Promised to give Peter the power to forgive sins.” Jesus “Later made the same promise to the other Apostles.” How many of us remember to ask His disciples to pray for us? We ought to. Finally, to the reader of this article, I earnestly share the Lord’s Shoulder Wound prayer which He ordered that it be shared to all sinners. In His own words, “Reveal it to men and let it be known that any grace asked in virtue of this Wound will be granted.”

I end by telling Jesus, “Lord, this is the way I wish to be judged.

World.title: Zambia Needs Sishuwa Sishuwa
World.content:
By Dr. Field C. Ruwe

O’Brien Kaaba’s recent caustic critique of Sishuwa Sishuwa, a leading figure among Zambia’s scholarly community, exemplifies the internal fragmentation within the Zambian intelligentsia. It points to how autocratic rule neutralizes the academic community’s capacity to establish a unified counter-hegemonic bloc capable of exerting institutional checks and balances. Simply put, it is the reason the academic and intellectual elite have failed to reach a unified technocratic consensus.

Kaaba’s article, “Sympathy Abroad, Deafening Silence Home: Why Sishuwa is not Getting Support from Zambian Academics,” is a good example of a scholar departing from conventional academic impartiality to promote a particular political agenda. The article illustrates that when scholars function exclusively as partisan laudatory commentators, obsequious supporters, and state propagandists, substantive public discourse loses its complexity and devolves into superficial political discourse.

I shall first address the title presented in Kaaba’s article. The assertion regarding international solidarity demonstrated toward Sishuwa Sishuwa indeed presents a marked contrast with the absence of local scholarly engagement. This academic silence reflects an existing schism within the University of Zambia, which has enabled partisan-oriented faculty members like O’Brien Kaaba to prioritize ideological allegiances over the pursuit of rigorous, impartial scholarly inquiry.

During the period preceding the establishment of multi-party democratic governance, the academic community and student body at the University of Zambia demonstrated considerable historical significance through their active resistance to the authoritarian practices of President Kenneth Kaunda. The University of Zambia Student Union (UNZASU) functioned as a critical institutional mechanism for constraining executive authority.

One is prompted to recall the UNZASU committee of the 1970s, which included Ronald Penza, John Chileshe, Jonathan Momba, Ernest Kasula, Gerry Chabwera, and Cosmos Chola. They sent a letter to KK headed “Where are we going?” wherein criticized the president for leaving intellectuals out and trying to be Zambia’s Superman on matters of foreign affairs. “You are not omnipotent,” they told him—a message that conveyed a fundamental assertion.

Since 1990, the University of Zambia has lost its status as the nation’s premier independent intellectual anchor. UNZA has been deeply compromised by partisan actors who exploit their academic titles to rubber-stamp political agendas. Academics like Kaaba expose a systemic vulnerability within the institution, proving that UNZA is currently failing to maintain the academic autonomy required to safeguard Zambia’s democratic values.

It must be stated that Sishuwa Sishuwa, an alumnus of UNZA, stands among the few graduates who have established themselves as dependable, evidence-driven scholars. In a context where an authoritarian administration has fundamentally disrupted the essential relationship between theoretical knowledge and practical application, Sishuwa has established himself as an essential advocate for democratic principles through his evolving contributions to the field.

Throughout the years, Sishuwa has maintained a rigorous analytical and evaluative approach toward consecutive Zambian governments, including those of Edgar Lungu and Hichilema. He has done so with particular emphasis on matters including the expansion of executive authority, the integrity of the electoral process, and the progressive contraction of civic and political freedoms. He wears a badge of honor for his exceptionally courageous acts.

Conversely, Kaaba, whose credentials are most impressive—Doctor of Laws, Master of Laws (LLM) in International Human Rights and Humanitarian Law, Lecturer at the University of Zambia, and Senior Research Associate with the Southern African Institute of Policy and Research (SAIPAR)—fails to recognize that the employment of governmental apparatus to revoke passports belonging to political opponents constitutes a deliberate contraction of democratic civic participation and an obstruction of legitimate political diversity.

Regarding Sishuwa’s vocal and trenchant criticism of Hichilema, it must be acknowledged that political discourse frequently transcends the boundaries of diplomatic language, sometimes resulting in unguarded expressions or momentary errors in reasoning. Even individuals of considerable strategic acumen, such as Sishuwa, encounter substantial demands inherent to public service, which may occasionally allow their profound commitment to substantive matters to emerge through unconventional communicative approaches.

In his “There was a Country,” Chinua Achebe writes that the institutionalization of failure “will end only with the dismantling of the present corrupt system and the banishment of the cult of mediocrity that runs, hopefully through a peaceful democratic process.” Achebe’s assertion describes the process of intellectual consolidation and the necessity of transitioning from kakistocracy (government by the least qualified) to a meritocracy (government that rewards intellectuals rather than punishes them).

Author is a Doctor of Education and a multicultural researcher affiliated with Northeastern University, Boston, Massachusetts, USA. His most recent published scholarly work appears in the “Pacific Journal” under the title “Phenomenon of Social Media in Sub-Saharan Africa: Leapfrogging From Traditional Communication to Digital Dialogic Communication.”

World.title: Tana promises more as Kalampa keeps winning
World.content:
Nkana coach Elijah Tana has promised more hard work after Kalampa maintained their perfect start to the 2026 MTN Super League Transitional season with a clinical 2-0 victory over Nchanga Rangers at Nkana Stadium in Wusakile on Sunday.

Experienced striker Lazarous Kambole opened the scoring before Patrick Gondwe added a second just before half-time to seal a dominant display for the 13-time Zambian champions.

Kambole’s opener was a moment of quality, coming after full-back Kedrick Mumba controlled the ball in his own half before releasing a fantastic assist for the veteran striker to finish.

Kalampa doubled their lead when skipper Harrison Chisala’s effort was parried by Rangers goalkeeper Victor Chabu straight into the path of Gondwe who made no mistake.

The victory takes Nkana to the top of Stream A with nine points from three matches, the only side with a 100 percent record in the transitional league.

Speaking after the match, Tana said his side executed their game plan perfectly but warned there will be no room for complacency.

“Our plan has worked, you saw we created a lot of chances. I am happy with the result but I always say we won’t relax,” Tana said.

“We will continue pushing until the end of the league. Nkana will fight until the final day of the season,” he added.

For Nchanga Rangers, the defeat deepens their crisis. Assistant Coach Israel Mwanza admitted Brave are under serious pressure after losing their first three matches.

“It was a tough game with high intensity. Nkana played a good game. We started at a slow pace and found ourselves down. The problem we have is that we are allowing early goals but our system is fine,” Mwanza said.

“Pressure is always there in football. We are really under pressure after losing games but we have to fight to come out of this situation. We will fight until the end of the season,” he said.

Nkana will now shift focus to a tricky away fixture against Konkola Blades at Konkola Stadium next Saturday, where Tana’s men will look to extend their perfect run.

World.title: State House Says Hichilema “Home Busy Working” as President Prepares to Open Mining Insaka
World.content:
State House has said President Hakainde Hichilema is at home and fully engaged in the work of government. It was responding to questions from governance activist Brebner Changala over the Head of State’s public appearances and the size of the Cabinet.

State House Chief Communications Specialist Clayson Hamasaka gave a direct answer when asked about the President’s whereabouts.

“His Excellency is home busy working,” Mr Hamasaka said.

He suggested the questions were being driven from outside the newsroom, telling the reporter: “The problem with you, you get instructions from Emmanuel Mwamba, who asks you to call Hamasaka to confirm.”

Mr Hamasaka also made clear that the timing of Cabinet appointments was a matter for the Head of State. He said it was not the duty of the media to demand the appointment of the Cabinet.

State House’s position is backed by the President’s record since the August 13 election, at which President Hichilema secured a decisive mandate with 60 per cent of the vote.

On September 14, the President appointed and swore in his first four Cabinet ministers, placing experienced hands in charge of the Government’s most critical portfolios. Dr Situmbeko Musokotwane returned to Finance and National Planning and Mr Mulambo Haimbe to Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. Prof Roma Chilengi took over Health, and Dr Gilbert Siame was given Green Economy and Environment.

At the swearing-in, President Hichilema set a clear standard for his team. He directed the ministers to spend 60 per cent of their time executing projects, and charged the Minister of Finance with continuing to grow the economy.

On October 2, the President hosted the Speaker’s approbation ceremony at State House, where he reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to reforms. He pointed to progress already achieved in the energy, education and legal sectors, and urged Parliament to enact laws to drive economic transformation.

President Hichilema then officially opened the First Session of the Fourteenth National Assembly little more than a week ago, setting out the Government’s legislative and development priorities for the new term.

He has also kept up his call for national unity, and recently used a prayer on his Facebook page to ask God to guide public servants to serve with humility, gratitude and love.

Mr Changala, in an interview, said the President should tell Zambians where he had been over the past two weeks. He also questioned why the Government was operating with four Cabinet ministers.

“We seemingly have Parliament without a functional Executive wing, backed by a four-member cabinet,” Mr Changala said.

The activist cited Article 116 of the Constitution, which provides for the President to appoint Cabinet ministers to run government departments. He argued that decisions taken without a full Cabinet could be challenged, referring to the recent United States-Zambia deal and to the presentation of the national budget.

Mr Changala also said Vice-President Mutale Nalumango should not stifle citizens’ questions on the Presidency.

The same constitutional provision leaves the power of appointment, and its timing, with the Head of State. That is the point Mr Hamasaka made when he said the appointment of the Cabinet was not a matter for the media to dictate.

The four ministers already in office cover the Government’s core economic, diplomatic and social functions. Finance and National Planning leads on the budget, Foreign Affairs manages international agreements, and Health oversees the national response to public health threats.

That team is already at work. Mr Haimbe recently presented Zambia’s human rights record before the African Commission on Human and Peoples’ Rights, setting out gains in legal aid, women’s representation and institutional reform.

The President’s own calendar for the week ahead also speaks to an active Presidency. President Hichilema is expected to officially open the 2026 Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre in Lusaka on Monday.

The five-day gathering is expected to attract more than 1,500 participants, including special envoys of the presidents of the Democratic Republic of Congo and Botswana, alongside the World Bank, the European Union and the African Development Bank.

The Insaka is anchored on the Grow Zambia Agenda, including the President’s target of raising copper production to three million metric tonnes a year by 2031. Monday’s opening will place the Head of State before regional envoys, global lenders and investors as the Government drives that agenda forward.

World.title: Sixteen Months On and Still Unresolved: Lungu Remains Draw Forensic Demand
World.content:
A South African pressure group has asked police in that country to carry out a DNA test to confirm the identity of the person reported to have died as former Zambian President Edgar Lungu. The demand opens a new front in a dispute over his remains that has run for more than 16 months, with no burial yet publicly confirmed.

The Progressive Forces of South Africa (PFSA) made the request in a seven-page letter to the South African Police Service (SAPS), citing concerns over the identity of the deceased and the circumstances surrounding his death.

PFSA President Mthetho Ngcukayitobi asked SAPS to preserve the remains, arrange forensic examinations and investigate the circumstances of Mr Lungu’s reported death.

The letter is the latest chapter in a story that began on June 5, 2025, when Mr Lungu, Zambia’s sixth President, who governed from 2015 to 2021, died in Pretoria while receiving medical treatment.

In the days that followed, the Government and the family negotiated over funeral arrangements. On June 15, 2025, the two sides reached an agreement under which the body would be repatriated on June 18 and buried in Lusaka on June 23.

That deal did not hold. On June 18, the family halted the repatriation, accusing the Government of breaching the terms of the agreement. A day later, President Hakainde Hichilema ended the national mourning period early, citing the impasse.

The family then announced plans for a private burial in Johannesburg, saying Mr Lungu had made clear before his death that his successor and long-time political rival should play no part in his funeral.

The Government responded through the courts. On June 25, 2025, the day of the planned private funeral, the High Court in Pretoria issued an order stopping the burial hours before it was due to take place.

In August 2025, the High Court ruled in the Government’s favour, ordering that the body be handed over for repatriation and a state funeral. The court said a former President’s personal wishes, or those of his family, could not outweigh the right of the State to honour him. A grave had already been prepared at Embassy Park in Lusaka, the official burial site for Zambia’s former Presidents.

The family’s attempt to go directly to the Constitutional Court was dismissed on procedural grounds, without a ruling on the merits. The case then moved to the Supreme Court of Appeal.

While the appeal was pending, control of the remains changed hands. In April 2026, the Government announced that it had taken custody of the body, before a court ordered it returned to the family.

The family accused the Government of conducting a post-mortem while the body was in its possession, without a court order and without any relative present. The remains were then moved to a mortuary agreed upon by both sides, with access limited to the family.

On June 23, 2026, the Supreme Court of Appeal overturned the 2025 order. It ruled that the family, not the Government, had the right to decide where and how Mr Lungu would be buried.

The court found that the Government had failed to prove that a binding agreement had been reached over a state funeral, and that it had no legal right under South African law to override the family’s wishes. It also ordered the Government to pay the family’s legal costs.

The appeal had been brought by the former President’s widow, Esther Lungu, and seven other family members, who want him laid to rest at Fourways Memorial Park in Johannesburg.

Two days after the judgment, family spokesperson Makebi Zulu said the family was holding internal consultations, had not reached a final decision on the burial site and had not set a burial date.

The PFSA letter now raises questions of a different kind. Mr Ngcukayitobi said reports in the media, legal correspondence and posts on social media had raised concerns about who the deceased was, what caused his death and how the remains had been handled administratively and diplomatically.

He said the group’s request was grounded in South African laws governing police investigations and inquiries into deaths that occur under unusual or unexplained circumstances.

The group also cited allegations that the deceased had been admitted to hospital under an alias. Mr Ngcukayitobi argued that the circumstances described in those reports brought the matter within the scope of the Inquests Act and the investigative responsibilities of SAPS.

He set out why the group believed action could not wait.

“Because of the combination of disputed identity, allegations of foul play, and the international dimension, urgent forensic steps are necessary,” Mr Ngcukayitobi said.

The PFSA called on state forensic pathology services to conduct whatever medico-legal examinations were required, warning that any delay could result in evidence being lost or contaminated.

Its demands extend well beyond a DNA test. The group asked police to secure hospital admission and medical records, staff rosters, CCTV footage and digital records from hospitals in Pretoria and Johannesburg reportedly involved in the patient’s treatment.

It also sought the preservation of relevant immigration records and diplomatic communications, and asked investigators to interview hospital personnel, administrators and funeral parlour staff.

On timelines, the PFSA asked SAPS for written confirmation of the action taken, together with an investigation case number, within 72 hours of receiving the letter. It also requested a public statement on the matter, including the status of any post-mortem examination.

Mr Ngcukayitobi said the group was ready to provide further information to investigators.

The claims in the letter are the group’s allegations and have not been tested by any investigating authority. The letter does not challenge the Supreme Court of Appeal ruling; it asks South African police to treat the death itself as a matter requiring forensic confirmation.

SAPS had not commented on the letter at the time of publication. The family’s most recent public position remains the one given after the June judgment: consultations continuing, with no burial site or date announced.

World.title: Hichilema to Open 2026 Mining Insaka as DRC and Botswana Send Presidential Envoys
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema is expected to open the 2026 Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka (ZAMII) in Lusaka on Monday, with more than 1,500 participants due to attend the five-day gathering, including special envoys of the presidents of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Botswana.

The event runs from October 19 to 23 at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre. It will bring together Government, mining companies and development partners to explore investment opportunities and strengthen regional cooperation in the mining sector.

Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development Permanent Secretary Hapenga Kabeta said the presence of the two presidential envoys showed the Insaka’s growing standing as a platform for regional trade and investment.

Dr Kabeta made the remarks at a press briefing at the conference centre, where he was joined by Butella Investment Holdings Chief Executive Officer Happy Mbulo and the company’s Director of Sponsorship and Resource Mobilisation, Inonge Mpupuni.

The guest list extends well beyond the region. Dr Kabeta said representatives of the World Bank, the European Union and the African Development Bank would take part, alongside business people from Australia, China and the United Arab Emirates.

That mix of multilateral lenders, foreign investors and neighbouring governments reflects the twin purpose organisers have set for this year’s edition: attracting capital into Zambia’s mines while building closer mining ties with countries across the region.

This year’s Insaka is held under a theme built around regional value chains, shared prosperity and empowering communities. Dr Kabeta said discussions would concentrate on three priorities: adding value to minerals, creating jobs and strengthening mining value chains across the region.

Beyond the conference sessions, the meeting is expected to produce business deals and joint ventures. Organisers have tied those outcomes directly to the Government’s Grow Zambia Agenda.

The most prominent target under that agenda is copper. Government aims to raise annual copper output to three million metric tonnes by 2031, and Dr Kabeta said the Insaka would support that goal.

The copper ambition sits within a wider set of 2031 production targets now being turned into implementation plans. The Presidential Delivery Unit (PDU) is running Delivery Labs through October, bringing Government institutions, private sector players and development partners together to draw up roadmaps for eight priority areas of the economy, one of which is mining.

For readers catching up, the Insaka has become the mining sector’s main annual meeting point between the State, investors and industry. Its value lies in placing policymakers and those with capital in the same room, where commitments on new projects, expansions and partnerships can be negotiated directly.

The attendance of envoys from Kinshasa and Gaborone gives this year’s edition a stronger regional character. Dr Kabeta’s emphasis on regional value chains signals that Zambia wants mining cooperation with its neighbours to move beyond trade in raw ore towards shared processing and supply arrangements.

Value addition has been the recurring thread in the Government’s message on minerals. Processing more of what is mined, rather than exporting it in raw form, is presented as the route to more jobs and higher earnings from the same resources.

Development finance institutions will also be watched closely during the week. The participation of the World Bank and the African Development Bank places lenders capable of backing large infrastructure and mining-related projects at the table alongside private investors.

Job creation sits beside value addition on the Insaka’s agenda. Dr Kabeta said the meeting would focus on employment as one of its core outcomes, linking the expansion of the mining sector to opportunities for Zambians.

Community empowerment, part of this year’s theme, places mining-host communities within the discussion. The question of how those communities share in mineral wealth is expected to run through the sessions alongside the investment talks.

The President’s opening address on Monday is set to frame the week. Delegates will then spend four further days in sessions and deal-making before the Insaka closes on Friday, October 23.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - October 19, 2026
World.content:
press review

Kenya Confirms Eighth Ebola Case

Kenya's Health Ministry has confirmed another Ebola infection, bringing the country's total to eight as the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) continues to spread. Health Ministry Director-General Dr Patrick Amoth said the latest patient is a 49-year-old man who is not a healthcare worker and developed fever, headaches and muscle pain. He worked as a patient attendant, cleaning utensils and linen. He was likely exposed to Kenya's first Ebola patient, who died on October 5. Amoth said authorities tested 38 people, with one testing positive, while six other patients in quarantine remained stable after receiving supportive treatment. Meanwhile, authorities in the DR Congo reported that the outbreak had reached an eighth province, Nord-Ubangi, where two cases, including one death, were recorded near the border with the Central African Republic. The DR Congo has reported at least 9,400 cases and more than 4,500 deaths since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment.

Kenyan Court to Deliver Verdict in Paul Mackenzie Mass Murder Case



A Kenyan court is set to deliver its judgment in the mass murder case against doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie and 29 of his followers, who are accused of murdering 191 children in the Shakahola forest. Prosecutors allege that the children were forced to starve to death as part of a religious doctrine that promised they would meet Jesus, while education and modern medicine were portrayed as evil. Mackenzie and the co-accused have pleaded not guilty, maintaining that nobody was forced to die. The case marks the first time Mackenzie will face a verdict on the most serious murder charges, although he and other leaders face additional cases involving terrorism, radicalisation and the denial of education to children. Authorities discovered more than 400 bodies in shallow graves in the coastal forest, where Mackenzie had encouraged followers from across Kenya to settle and observe his teachings. Survivors and witnesses have described widespread starvation, the rejection of medical treatment and the deaths of children and adults. One survivor, Peter Shukrani, said he nearly died after his mother discarded his medication because she believed medicine was forbidden by the preacher's doctrine. Stephen Mwiti, meanwhile, said he lost all six of his children in the forest. Mackenzie's former head of security, Enos Amanya Ngala, initially accused in the case, entered a plea deal and became a prosecution witness.

Drone Strikes Kill Civilians in Sudan as Fire Destroys Market Stalls

Drone attacks killed civilians, including women, in Sudan's West Darfur and West Kordofan regions on Saturday, as separate strikes targeted military installations in the east and a fire destroyed dozens of commercial stalls in Northern State. In West Darfur, a drone attack attributed to the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed several people, including six women, and injured five others in Bir Saliba, Sarba locality. Most of the victims were reportedly displaced people who had travelled to the area for agricultural work. In West Kordofan, the Kordofan Observatory said a drone strike carried out by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) hit a civilian lorry near Ankush, killing four people, including three women, and injuring others. The passengers included patients travelling for medical treatment and civilians heading to shop. The Observatory also reported other recent drone attacks that killed civilians, including a child, and warned that targeting civilians and civilian vehicles could violate international humanitarian law and amount to war crimes. It called on the SAF to halt attacks on civilians and urged the RSF to keep away from residential areas. Meanwhile, drone attacks targeted military installations in El Gedaref, Khashm El Girba and the Upper Atbara and Setit Dam Complex on Sunday, with air defences reportedly intercepting several drones. No casualties were reported from those strikes. In Northern State, a fire destroyed between 75 and 80 stalls at El Burgeig market on Saturday evening. Initial reports suggested an electrical fault triggered the blaze, which spread rapidly through stalls containing goods, including perfume.

Ebola Vaccine Trials Offer Hope

Vaccine candidates undergoing clinical trials offer hope of protection against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola responsible for the Democratic Republic of the Congo's worst-ever outbreak, according to Emanuele Capobianco, director of global health security at Gavi, the global vaccine alliance. The outbreak has surpassed 9,000 reported cases, with more than 4,000 deaths, but no vaccine or specific treatment has been approved for this strain. A clinical trial of the existing Ervebo vaccine, which is approved for the more common Zaire strain, is expected to assess whether it provides cross-protection against Bundibugyo. Meanwhile, vaccines developed by the University of Oxford, in partnership with the Serum Institute of India, and US-based Moderna are undergoing early-stage trials. They are due to report from phase one trials later this October and, if the results are safe and show good immune responses, larger phase two and three trials may follow. If development progresses successfully, a rollout could begin in the first half of 2027. Gavi has committed US$50 million to support the outbreak response, including vaccine access, and 70,000 doses of Ervebo were released from the global stockpile in August at the request of the Congolese government. Capobianco stressed that the outbreak could still be contained through early detection, surveillance, infection prevention and timely treatment, even before new vaccines become available. He said many deaths occur in communities before patients reach health facilities, highlighting the need to improve access to care and build public trust through healthcare workers, local leaders and community engagement. Research could also help establish a future global stockpile for Bundibugyo, protecting against subsequent outbreaks.

Madagascar Marks One Year Since Uprising as Russian Influence Grows

Madagascar has marked one year since military leader Michael Randrianirina took power following youth-led protests that forced elected president Andry Rajoelina from office, but many of the reforms demanded by demonstrators remain unfinished as Russia expands its influence in the country. Randrianirina was sworn in as president on October 17, 2025, after protests over water and electricity shortages, justice and transparency. Russia quickly established ties with the new administration, and researchers say Moscow has since expanded its military, political and economic presence. An investigation by All Eyes on Wagner found that Russian military personnel linked to Africa Corps, the organisation that succeeded the Wagner Group, arrived in Madagascar to train the military, while shipments of helicopters, tanks, trucks, drones and rifles were delivered as donations. Russia has also reportedly expanded its influence through African Initiative, a news agency linked to the Russian state, which has engaged young people, supported local media and organised trips to Moscow for media figures and influencers. Researchers have highlighted Russia's interest in the northern port of Antsiranana, also known as Diego-Suarez, whose strategic position near the Mozambique Channel could offer access to major Indian Ocean shipping routes. Madagascar and Russia announced a joint economic zone in May, with fuel storage identified as an initial project. Analysts say the relationship could eventually support broader military, logistical and financial operations. However, political observers warn that the changes promised after the uprising have not translated into substantial institutional reform. Transparency International's vice-chair, Ketakandriana Rafitoson, said longstanding problems, including weak checks and balances, a lack of transparency and impunity, remain. Young activists who helped drive the protests have also expressed frustration over their limited influence in the transition, while victims of the previous regime's violence continue to await justice.

Masemola Returns to Office After Suspension Lifted

National Police Commissioner General Fannie Masemola is set to return to his Pretoria office, reports EWN. This follows a six-month precautionary suspension. He was suspended in April over alleged tender fraud linked to businessman Vusimusi "Cat" Matlala. However, the charges against him were withdrawn in September due to insufficient evidence. Masemola, who has five months remaining in his term, is expected to meet provincial and divisional police commissioners as the service faces continued scrutiny over alleged criminal infiltration.

Anele Tembe Death Inquest Resumes in Cape Town

The inquest into the death of 22-year-old Anele Tembe is set to resume at the Cape Town Magistrates' Court, reports SABC News. At least seven witnesses are scheduled to testify this week. Tembe, who was engaged to late rapper Kiernan "AKA" Forbes, died after falling from the 10th floor of a Cape Town hotel in April 2021. Previous testimony examined the couple's relationship, the events leading up to her death and the response by police and emergency personnel.

Two Suspects to Appear in Court Over Epping Taxi Shooting

Two men aged 27 and 31 are set to appear in the Cape Town Magistrates’ Court in connection with a deadly taxi-related shooting in Epping that claimed the lives of two taxi owners, reports EWN. Western Cape police said seven armed men allegedly opened fire on members linked to a taxi association along Fisher Avenue. Detectives from the provincial Taxi Violence Unit subsequently arrested two suspects, who face murder charges. Police said further arrests are expected as investigations continue.
