This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Solange Omon

Omon was born in Cameroon and has lived, studied and worked in Maine, she told People magazine in an interview published after the show. Before modeling, she worked as a program coordinator at nonprofits, helping mostly Black and immigrant teenagers apply for jobs and teaching them about climate change.

Viewers of the series first met her at the casting in Chicago, where she earned a place in the top 10. “I was speechless,” she said of the call that moved her forward, adding that she decided on the spot to drive to her mother’s to share the news.

Hillary Super, chief executive of Victoria’s Secret & Co., told the magazine that Omon “has a spark that’s entirely her own.” Adam Selman, the group’s chief creative officer, said what made her stand out “wasn’t just her presence, it was her authenticity.”

The Dominican Finalist

Martínez was born in Santiago de los Caballeros, the Dominican Republic’s second city, and was raised in New York, where she studied psychology and Latin American studies. She won Miss Dominican Republic Universe in 2021 as the delegate of the Dominican community in the United States, but missed that year’s Miss Universe after contracting COVID-19.

She was sent to the next edition, Miss Universe 2022, held in New Orleans in January 2023, and finished as second runner-up, behind the winner from the United States and the first runner-up from Venezuela. The business magazine Revista Mercado had noted before the final that a win would have made her the first Dominican to hold the Angel title officially.

Before the result, she thanked her followers in a message quoted by the newspaper Hoy, writing that she was deeply grateful and already felt like an Angel. “I don’t know what is going to happen, but I know this is only the beginning,” she wrote, in the Spanish version Hoy published.

How Angels Among Us Worked

Victoria’s Secret opened the search on 1 April as an open casting across America, promising the winner a runway walk and an exclusive IMG Models contract. More than 100,000 hopefuls applied, and a team led by Selman held in-person castings in Los Angeles, Miami, Houston and Chicago.

A top 10 then trained in New York with runway coaching, photo shoots and fittings, while models Gigi Hadid, Paloma Elsesser and Ashley Graham appeared as mentors and judges. Eliminations cut the group to Omon, Martínez and Tinsley, a model born and raised in New York with commercial and runway experience.

The process was filmed as a seven-episode YouTube docuseries produced with Boardwalk Pictures and directed by Nadia Hallgren, whose earlier work includes the documentary Becoming. Episodes have run on Sundays and Thursdays since 27 September, and the last one airs on 22 November, five weeks after the reveal.

What It Means for You

Victoria’s Secret & Co., based in Reynoldsburg, Ohio, and listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker VSXY, runs about 1,430 stores in roughly 70 countries. Its second-quarter net sales rose 10% to US$1.611 billion, and in September it raised its full-year sales forecast to between US$7.100 billion and US$7.180 billion.

Super named the Angels Among Us docuseries and a bigger fashion show among the campaigns meant to carry that momentum through the rest of the year. For investors, the contest is a test of whether a public casting call can win new customers, a question only the coming quarterly results can answer.

For viewers, the show and every episode of the series stream free on the brand’s YouTube channel. Selman has said the idea grew out of “thousands of DMs” after last year’s show from fans asking how they could become an Angel.

What Is Not Known

The value and length of Omon’s IMG Models contract have not been published, and the brand has not said whether she will appear in its advertising campaigns. Victoria’s Secret has also not released audience figures for the docuseries or the live stream.

It is not known whether the brand will offer Martínez or Tinsley further work after the show. Any effect of the contest on sales will only become visible in the group’s next quarterly results.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who won Victoria’s Secret Angels Among Us?

Solange Omon, a 21-year-old model born in Cameroon who lives in Maine, won on 18 October 2026. She was revealed as the newest Angel at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show in Los Angeles.

Is Solange Omon Dominican?

Solange Omon is not Dominican. She was born in Cameroon, and the Dominican finalist was Andreína Martínez, who reached the top three but did not win.

What does the winner of Angels Among Us get?

The winner walks in the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show and receives an exclusive contract with IMG Models. The terms of the contract have not been published.

Where can I watch Angels Among Us?

The seven-episode docuseries streams free on Victoria’s Secret’s YouTube channel. The final episode airs on 22 November.

World.title: Guinea U20 Beats Liberia 1-0 to Reach Semis
World.content:
Guinea’s senior national team (right, in red) lines up beside Ghana before their Africa Cup of Nations quarterfinal in Malabo, Equatorial Guinea, on 1 February 2015. Photo: Ben Sutherland, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons

GUINEA · MALI · FOOTBALL

Key Facts — What happened Guinea’s under-20 national team beat Liberia 1-0 in Bamako, Mali, on Sunday 18 October 2026 and secured a place in the semifinals of the West African zonal qualifier.

— The goal Thierno Diallo scored the only goal around the half-hour mark. Guinea had already beaten the hosts, Mali, 1-0 in the opening game on Thursday 15 October.

— The tournament The UFOA-A U20 tournament is the under-20 qualifier for Zone A of the West African Football Union. It runs from 15 to 30 October in Bamako with seven teams in two groups.

— The prize The two finalists qualify for the 2027 U20 Africa Cup of Nations in Ghana. The top four there go on to the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

— What comes next Guinea play Gambia on Wednesday 21 October for first place in Group A. The semifinals are on Sunday 25 October and the final on Friday 30 October.

— For US travelers Mali is under a Level 4 “Do Not Travel” US travel advisory, the highest level. The advisory tells Americans not to travel to Mali for any reason.

Guinea U20, the West African country’s under-20 national football team, beat Liberia 1-0 in Bamako, Mali, on Sunday 18 October 2026. The win put Guinea into the semifinals of the UFOA-A U20 tournament and left the team one victory away from a place at the 2027 U20 Africa Cup of Nations in Ghana.

For American readers, the stakes reach beyond West Africa. The top four teams in Ghana will represent Africa at the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan, the tournament where Morocco knocked the United States out in 2025 on its way to the title.

How Guinea U20 Beat Liberia

Thierno Diallo scored the only goal around the half-hour mark at the Ouezzin Coulibaly stadium in Bamako, the Guinean outlets Guineematin and Africaguinee reported. Guineematin timed the goal in the 30th minute and described Diallo as a defender who had pushed forward, while Africaguinee put it in the 29th minute and named him as Guinea’s number 4.

Liberia pressed for an equaliser after the break, according to Guineematin, but the score did not change. The result gave the team of coach Mohamed Lamine Sylla, known as Leandro, two wins from two games without conceding a goal.

Guinea had opened the tournament on Thursday 15 October with a 1-0 win over the hosts at the Stade Mamadou Konaté, a result the Malian site Kibaru Sports also reported. Mohamed Abédi Bangoura scored shortly before half-time, according to Guineematin and Guinee360.

The squad of 24 players, three goalkeepers, seven defenders, eight midfielders and six forwards, was named by Sylla on 12 October, the Guinean Football Federation (FEGUIFOOT) said. The team had prepared at a camp in Khoria, in Guinea, where it beat the Conakry club Horoya AC 2-1 in a warm-up match.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the UFOA-A Tournament Is

UFOA is the French acronym for the West African Football Union, known in English as WAFU, a regional body of national federations within the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Its Zone A covers the western part of the region: Cape Verde, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Senegal and Sierra Leone.

CAF, the governing body of African football, runs the U20 Africa Cup of Nations, and the West African places at that championship are decided in zonal events like this one. The draw for the Bamako edition took place on 1 October at the Radisson Collection hotel in the Malian capital, and Mali is hosting the matches from 15 to 30 October.

Eight teams were drawn into two groups of four: Mali, Guinea, Liberia and Gambia in Group A, and Senegal, Mauritania, Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau in Group B. Guinea-Bissau later withdrew and the organisers reduced Group B to three teams, while Cape Verde was not in the draw.

The top two in each group reach the semifinals on Sunday 25 October, where the Group A winner meets the Group B runner-up and the Group B winner meets the Group A runner-up. The final and the third-place match are scheduled for Friday 30 October at the Stade Mamadou Konaté, according to the schedule published by the Senegalese sports sites Wiwsport and Senegal7.

Senegal are the defending champions after winning the 2024 edition in Sierra Leone. They began their title defence with a 2-1 win over Mauritania on Friday 16 October, the Mauritanian outlet Madar reported.

What the Tournament Qualifies For

Only the two finalists go through to the 2027 U20 Africa Cup of Nations, which CAF has awarded to Ghana and which it says will feature 12 teams. CAF said in April that the top four teams in Ghana will qualify for the FIFA U-20 World Cup.

FIFA’s Council picked Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan on 2 October 2025 to co-host that World Cup in 2027, the Azerbaijani football federation announced. For Guinea, winning the semifinal in Bamako is therefore the first step on the only road to that tournament.

Where the Group Stands

Guinea lead Group A with six points from two games, ahead of Gambia on four, Liberia on one and Mali on none. Gambia beat Mali 1-0 on Sunday evening and knocked the hosts out, the Senegalese site Seneweb reported.

Guinea play Gambia, the Young Scorpions coached by Abdoulie Bojang, on Wednesday 21 October in their last group game. A draw or a win keeps Guinea top, while a Gambian win would lift Gambia above them and drop Guinea to second.

First place would mean a 4 p.m. GMT semifinal against the Group B runner-up, which is noon in New York. Second place would mean a 7 p.m. GMT semifinal, 3 p.m. on the US East Coast, against the winner of a group that Senegal led after the first round of games.

What It Means for US Readers

The clearest link is the FIFA U-20 World Cup, where US youth teams face the African qualifiers. At the 2025 edition in Chile, the US under-20 team lost 3-1 to Morocco in the quarterfinals in Rancagua on 12 October, and Morocco went on to beat Argentina 2-0 in the final in Santiago.

That made Morocco only the second African winner of the tournament, after Ghana in 2009. Any West African team that comes through Bamako and then Ghana could meet the United States in Azerbaijan or Uzbekistan in 2027 if the Americans qualify.

Travel is the other practical point for Americans. The US State Department keeps Mali at Level 4, “Do Not Travel”, citing crime, terrorism, unrest, health and kidnapping, and says US government staff in the country may not travel outside Bamako.

What Is Not Known

Guinea’s semifinal opponent will not be known until Group B is finished, and the published schedule does not name a semifinal venue. Guinea’s first two games were played at two different grounds in Bamako, the Stade Mamadou Konaté and the Ouezzin Coulibaly stadium.

CAF said in August that the Ghana tournament would be staged in February and March 2027, while Wiwsport and Senegal7 have since published dates of 27 April to 18 May 2027. CAF has not published exact match dates on its own site, and it is not clear whether any US broadcaster or streaming service will carry the matches from Bamako.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the UFOA-A U20 tournament?

It is the under-20 football qualifier for Zone A of the West African Football Union, known in French as UFOA and in English as WAFU. The 2026 edition runs from 15 to 30 October in Bamako, Mali.

Who scored for Guinea against Liberia?

Thierno Diallo scored the only goal around the half-hour mark of Guinea’s 1-0 win on Sunday 18 October 2026. It was Guinea’s second straight 1-0 win after the opening victory over Mali.

What does the tournament qualify for?

The two finalists qualify for the 2027 U20 Africa Cup of Nations in Ghana. The top four teams there qualify for the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup in Azerbaijan and Uzbekistan.

When are the semifinals and the final?

The semifinals are scheduled for Sunday 25 October and the final for Friday 30 October, both in Bamako. Guinea first play Gambia on Wednesday 21 October to decide first place in Group A.

Can Americans travel to Mali to watch?

The US State Department advises Americans not to travel to Mali for any reason and rates the country at Level 4, its highest warning. It also says US government employees in Mali are not allowed to travel outside Bamako because of safety risks.

World.title: Trinidad Budget Debate Turns on 2.2% Decline
World.content:
Port of Spain skyline from a highway approach in Trinidad and Tobago (Photo: Christianwelsh, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons)

TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country Trinidad and Tobago is a twin-island Caribbean republic whose economy runs on natural gas, liquefied natural gas (LNG) and petrochemicals.

— Why it matters The budget sets tax, spending and borrowing for a Caribbean gas producer, so the fight over its numbers touches energy investors and creditors.

— Why now Finance Minister Davendranath Tancoo presented the budget on Monday 12 October 2026, and the Opposition has attacked its figures in the Trinidad budget debate since.

— What happened Opposition MP Colm Imbert, a former finance minister, told the debate the economy is in recession and will crash within months if it has not already.

— The numbers The Ministry of Finance projects a 2.2% fall in real output in 2026 and a fiscal 2027 deficit of TT$3.639 billion (about US$540 million).

— What it means for you US readers with energy, bond or travel interests should treat the crash warning as a political claim and follow the official data.

— Still open Whether the economy is in a technical recession, and whether the Government can halve its deficit in one year.

Opposition MP Colm Imbert told the Trinidad budget debate that the economy is in recession and may crash within months. The Trinidad Express reported his remarks on Sunday 18 October 2026, six days after the budget was presented on Monday 12 October.

For US readers, the dispute matters because Trinidad and Tobago is a Caribbean gas, LNG and petrochemical producer. Its budget sets the tax, spending and borrowing climate for energy investors, creditors and visitors.

Imbert belongs to the People’s National Movement (PNM), which is now in opposition. The Government is led by Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar of the United National Congress (UNC).

What Happened in the Trinidad Budget Debate

Tancoo presented the 2026-2027 budget on Monday 12 October 2026. It projects spending of TT$63.368 billion (about US$9.4 billion) and revenue of TT$59.729 billion (about US$8.8 billion).

That leaves a fiscal 2027 deficit of TT$3.639 billion (about US$540 million), which the Ministry of Finance puts at 2.1% of GDP. The revised deficit for fiscal 2026 is TT$7 billion (about US$1.0 billion).

The budget assumes oil at US$77 a barrel and gas at US$5 per MMBtu, against US$73.25 and US$4.25 in 2026. Oil revenue is projected at TT$14.355 billion (about US$2.1 billion).

Imbert said he cannot support the package and repeated the Opposition Leader’s claim that the country is in recession. The Express quoted him calling the budget figures a “mirage”, “fictitious” and “nonsense”.

Opposition Leader Pennelope Beckles made the same recession claim in her budget reply in Parliament, which CNC3 reported on Friday 16 October. She also called for Tancoo to resign, accusing him of giving the International Monetary Fund (IMF) misleading information, and the Express report carried no reply from him.

What Imbert Claimed

Imbert said the country, “if it has not already crashed, will crash within the next couple of months”. That is a prediction, and the budget documents reviewed contain no such forecast.

He said growth in business lending fell from 11.4% in April 2025 to 0.6% in July 2026, citing Central Bank documents. The Ministry’s review points the same way, with business lending growth of 0.8% in June 2026 against 6.6% in October 2025.

He tied the slowdown to the closure of Nutrien and curtailments at Proman, two petrochemical producers. The Ministry’s review confirms a controlled Nutrien shutdown from October 2025 and a temporary suspension of Proman’s melamine plant from January 2026.

Imbert said the Government imposed at least 70 new taxes and fees between May 2025 and September 2026, including an asset levy on commercial banks and landlord registration fees. The count of 70 is his own and was not checked line by line, though the Budget Statement reports that the bank and insurance asset levy raised TT$397 million (about US$59 million).

He also argued that the Government still cannot balance the books despite what he called an energy windfall of TT$3 billion (about US$440 million). He said the deficit could have been TT$12 billion to TT$15 billion (about US$1.8 billion to US$2.2 billion) at the oil prices international agencies expected.

What the Government Documents Show

The Ministry of Finance’s Review of the Economy 2026 says the Central Statistical Office recorded a 0.5% fall in output in 2025. It projects a 2.2% decline in 2026, mainly from lower energy activity.

Real GDP fell 1.8% year on year in the first quarter of 2026, after a 1.2% fall in the fourth quarter of 2025. Unemployment rose to 5.4% in the first quarter from 4.3% in the previous quarter.

Natural gas output averaged about 2.44 billion standard cubic feet a day in the first eight months of fiscal 2026, 5.1% below a year earlier. The Budget Statement blames the former PNM administration for a 45% slide from the 2014 peak, including the permanent closure of Atlantic LNG Train 1.

The Budget Statement also reports headline inflation of 0.6% in July 2026 and net official reserves of US$5.4 billion, or 6.2 months of import cover. It says the Government borrowed more than TT$21 billion (about US$3.1 billion) in 18 months to refinance debt, with TT$70 billion (about US$10.3 billion) due over five years.

Imbert said the rise in reserves came from borrowing and withdrawals from the Heritage and Stabilisation Fund rather than export earnings. The Express report carried no response to that claim.

Is Trinidad and Tobago in a Recession?

Beckles used a rule of two consecutive quarters of negative growth. The official readings of minus 1.2% and minus 1.8% fit that pattern, though they are year-on-year comparisons rather than quarter-on-quarter changes.

The IMF’s October 2026 regional outlook, which the Trinidad Guardian reported on Saturday 17 October, shows a 0.5% fall in 2025 but growth of 0.2% in 2026. That sits 2.4 percentage points above the Ministry’s own projection of a 2.2% decline for the same year.

Beckles said the IMF’s June report cited 0.8% growth for 2025, while the Ministry’s earlier review had projected a 0.8% contraction. That is her allegation, and no response from Tancoo was found.

Economist Marla Dukharan, based in Barbados, questioned whether the Government can halve its deficit in one year. She told the Trinidad Guardian that, if the numbers are correct, “this could constitute a shock to the economy”.

What It Means for US Readers

Energy and chemicals investors should watch gas output, which sits behind the Ministry’s forecast of a 2.2% decline. The Nutrien and Proman cuts show how supply limits reach exports and jobs.

Bond holders and lenders can use the TT$3.639 billion (about US$540 million) deficit target as a benchmark for later data. The Budget Statement says financial-market contacts and rating-agency reports show confidence that the Government will meet its obligations.

For background, our explainer Trinidad and Tobago Explained: Gas, Politics, the Two Islands and What to Watch covers the energy base. Our report Trinidad Cabinet Realignment Moves Housing Schemes covers the Government’s recent changes.

What Is Not Known

Imbert’s warning of a crash within months is a prediction, and no official source reviewed here supports or tests it. The Government’s reply to his speech was not found.

The parliamentary record of the Trinidad budget debate was not available, so Imbert’s words and figures come from the Trinidad Express. The IMF figures come from a press description rather than the IMF’s own text.

It is not known whether quarterly data after March 2026 show further falls. The next Central Statistical Office releases will show whether the contraction deepens or eases.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Colm Imbert say about the Trinidad economy?

He said the economy is in recession and will crash within the next couple of months if it has not already. The Trinidad Express reported the remarks on Sunday 18 October 2026.

Who is Colm Imbert?

He is an Opposition MP and a former finance minister from the People’s National Movement. He criticised the budget that Finance Minister Davendranath Tancoo presented on 12 October.

What does the 2027 budget project?

It projects spending of TT$63.368 billion (about US$9.4 billion) and revenue of TT$59.729 billion (about US$8.8 billion). The deficit is TT$3.639 billion (about US$540 million).

Is Trinidad and Tobago in a recession?

The Ministry of Finance projects a 2.2% fall in output in 2026 after 0.5% in 2025, while the IMF outlook shows 0.2% growth. The two official views differ, so the label remains disputed.

What does it mean for US readers?

It shapes the outlook for investors and creditors tied to a Caribbean gas producer. Official data on gas output and quarterly GDP are the best guide.

World.title: Nilton Condori Arrest Order Cites 2 Crimes
World.content:
The Legislative Palace on Plaza Murillo in La Paz, with the new Legislative Assembly tower behind it. Nilton Condori holds a suspended alternate seat in the Senate, one of the two chambers of the assembly (Photo: Casi metro y medio, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BOLIVIA · LA PAZ · POLITICS

Key Facts — The country Bolivia is a landlocked Andean country short of dollars and fuel, governed since November 2025 by President Rodrigo Paz of the Christian Democratic Party (PDC).

— Why it matters Nilton Condori, a suspended alternate senator, helped lead the May and June road blockades that demanded Paz’s resignation, and the case against him also names former president Evo Morales.

— What happened Plainclothes police detained him on Sunday 18 October near the Mercado Campesino in El Alto, before a political meeting he had called, and took him to anti-crime police cells in La Paz.

— The accusation A prosecutors’ order dated 16 October lists public instigation to commit crimes and terrorism, linked to a 26 September meeting of Morales supporters where speakers talked of encircling La Paz.

— Power Index Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 in Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 28.4 points (October 2026 edition).

— What comes next A judge must decide whether he awaits trial in jail, under lighter measures or free. The constitution bars preventive detention of legislators during their term, except when caught in the act.

— Still open The order does not spell out which acts he is accused of, and no court has ruled on whether a suspended alternate senator keeps that protection.

The Nilton Condori arrest came on Sunday 18 October, when plainclothes police detained the suspended alternate senator in El Alto, the high plateau city above La Paz. Prosecutors accuse him of public instigation to commit crimes and terrorism over a September meeting with supporters of former president Evo Morales, who is named in the same case.

For foreign readers, the case matters because Condori was one of the faces of the road blockades of May and June, which demanded the resignation of President Rodrigo Paz. How the courts treat him will show whether Bolivia’s government can restore order without being accused of jailing its critics.

Who Is Nilton Condori

Nilton Condori Alanoca is a former schoolteacher who calls himself an Aymara leader and was elected in 2025 as the alternate of Soledad Chapetón, a La Paz senator for Unidad. Unidad is the centre-right alliance of businessman Samuel Doria Medina, who has said Condori was recruited for his reach in the rural provinces of La Paz.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Bolivia ranks 12th of 14 with 28.4 points. Strongest pillar: military means (55); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (13). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (CCC+); economy contracting (-1.2%); inflation of 20%. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

He was no newcomer, having been a leader of the Third System Movement (MTS), the party of former La Paz governor Félix Patzi, and an official in the departmental government. He broke with Unidad in late 2025 by demanding deep pay cuts for legislators, and in April 2026 he called an open assembly that gave the government two weeks to cut salaries and scrap lifetime pensions for former leaders.

That assembly, taken up by the Túpac Katari peasant federation of La Paz, turned into a demand for Paz’s resignation and fed the blockades that the government counts as 53 days long. On 12 August the Senate suspended Condori for eight months without pay over disparaging remarks about the legislature, a case the newspaper El Deber called the first ouster proceeding against a lawmaker since the lower house expelled Morales in 2002.

Since then he has moved toward Morales, attending the September meeting and floating a new party he calls the Popular Movement of the People. On 15 October Unidad said it would ask the electoral court to strip him of the seat for switching sides.

What the Nilton Condori Arrest Is About

The arrest order was issued on Friday 16 October by La Paz prosecutors from the anti-corruption and financial crimes unit, in a case opened on a complaint by deputy Manolo Rojas. Rojas belongs to Paz’s PDC and chairs the justice committee of the Chamber of Deputies.

The order cites Articles 130 and 133 of the Penal Code, public instigation to commit crimes and terrorism, and invokes risks of flight and obstruction under Article 226 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Terrorism carries 15 to 20 years in prison, but the order does not say which specific acts Condori is accused of.

Rojas filed the complaint on 29 September, three days after a meeting of Morales supporters in Lauca Ñ, in the Chapare coca region, where speakers talked of encircling La Paz with new protests. The news agency ANF quoted Condori telling that gathering: “If we do not put these thieves before a firing squad, Bolivia will have no future.”

The case also names Morales, president from 2006 to 2019 for the Movement for Socialism (MAS), and two of his allies, Román Gutiérrez and Rosario Vargas, but the order only directs police to arrest Condori. Morales already faces two other arrest warrants, one in a human trafficking case in Tarija and one over the May and June blockades, and has not been detained.

Presidential spokesman José Luis Gálvez tied the arrest to the blockades, telling radio Panamericana that Condori was held “for instigation to commit crimes associated with the 53 days.” His defence calls the Lauca Ñ remarks words spoken “in the heat of politics” and says he will seek to face the case in freedom.

Human rights bodies have long questioned how Bolivia uses its terrorism law. The Inter-American Commission on Human Rights and the GIEI, an independent expert group that investigated the 2019 crisis for the commission, have called the definition too broad and open to use against political opponents.

How the Arrest Unfolded

Witnesses told local media that about eight men in plain clothes, some of them hooded, seized Condori while he ate near the Mercado Campesino and pushed him into a van. La Paz police commander Colonel Ricardo Terrazas confirmed the arrest and linked it to alleged incitement to violence.

Condori declined to answer prosecutors’ questions on Sunday evening, and his lawyer Yaco Conde said the file holds little more than printouts and press clippings. El Deber reported that prosecutors then told Condori he is formally charged and would file the charge with a judge on Monday.

Vice President Edmand Lara, whose office presides over the Legislative Assembly, voiced concern and said justice “must not be used as a tool to silence voices.” Condori’s supporters declared a national state of emergency and warned that “the people will rise up” if he is not freed by Monday.

What It Means for You

For American travelers, the immediate risk is a return of road blockades around La Paz and El Alto, the city that hosts the main airport serving La Paz. The US State Department rates Bolivia at Level 2, exercise increased caution, and warns that roadblocks are a common form of protest that visitors should never try to cross.

For investors and policymakers, the case tests whether Paz’s government can enforce the law against blockade leaders in an economy short of dollars and fuel. The May and June blockades disrupted food and fuel supplies between cities, and prosecutors had opened 148 criminal cases over them by July.

It is also a test of due process in a country where successive governments have been accused of using terrorism charges against rivals. A final conviction would cost Condori his seat under the constitution, while a release would leave him free to pursue the 2030 candidacy he has been eyeing.

What Is Not Known

The order does not identify the statements or acts behind the terrorism charge, and prosecutors have not published the formal charge. It is also unclear whether prosecutors will ask for preventive detention, as Rojas wants, or for lighter measures such as house arrest.

No court has yet ruled on whether Article 152 of the constitution, which bars preventive detention of legislators during their term, protects an alternate who is suspended. It is not known whether Morales, Gutiérrez or Vargas will be summoned, or whether Condori’s supporters will carry out their threat of protests.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Nilton Condori?

Nilton Condori is a former teacher elected in 2025 as an alternate senator for La Paz on the list of the centre-right alliance Unidad. He broke with the alliance, helped lead the May and June blockades and was suspended from the Senate for eight months in August.

Why was Nilton Condori arrested?

Prosecutors in La Paz ordered his arrest on 16 October for alleged public instigation to commit crimes and terrorism. The complaint centres on a 26 September meeting of Evo Morales supporters at which speakers talked of encircling La Paz.

Can a Bolivian senator be held in preventive detention?

Article 152 of Bolivia’s constitution says legislators have no immunity but cannot be held in preventive detention during their term, except when caught in the act. Whether that applies to a suspended alternate senator like Condori is for the judge to decide.

Is Evo Morales also under arrest?

Morales is named in the same case, but the order only directs police to arrest Condori. He already faces two other arrest warrants that have not been carried out.

Is it safe to travel to La Paz now?

The US State Department rates Bolivia at Level 2 and warns that roadblocks are a common form of protest. Travelers should follow local news, avoid demonstrations and never try to cross a roadblock.

World.title: Suriname Work Permits Face October Survey
World.content:
Aerial view of the Staatsolie Tout Lui Faut refinery complex in Suriname (Photo: NullAspect, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

SURINAME · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country Suriname is a small South American country on the Atlantic coast whose first offshore oil project is due to start producing in 2028.

— Why it matters Firms from the United States and elsewhere that send specialists to Suriname generally need a work permit for each foreign employee.

— Why now The national business association asked its members for evidence on permit delays, in a call first published on Saturday 17 October 2026.

— What happened The Vereniging Surinaams Bedrijfsleven (VSB) asked firms about work and residence permits for foreign staff in the oil, gas and mining sectors.

— The numbers The ministry’s published folder gives 30 days for a permit decision, with a fee of US$500 per application in the oil, gold and timber sectors and US$100 elsewhere.

— What it means for you US employers and contractors should plan permits early and not rely on a business visa for any paid work in Suriname.

— Still open Whether delays are real and widespread, and how the labour ministry will respond, has not been shown.

Suriname work permits are under review by the country’s main business association, according to the Paramaribo outlet Starnieuws on Saturday 17 October 2026. The Vereniging Surinaams Bedrijfsleven (VSB), which represents private firms, wants members to describe their problems with hiring foreign specialists.

For US readers the point is practical, because any American firm that places staff in Suriname falls under the same permit rules. The offshore oil project that drives the hiring is run by TotalEnergies of France with APA Corporation of Houston.

GFC Nieuws, a Paramaribo news site, carried the same call on Sunday 18 October 2026. It added that unclear procedures, long handling times and weak coordination between agencies can hold firms back, but neither report gives survey results.

Why Suriname Work Permits Matter for Oil Hiring

The VSB expects demand for specialised foreign staff to grow as the oil, gas and mining sectors develop. It says a workable system for admission, residence and employment of foreign workers is needed to support that growth.

The VSB says specialists bring technical knowledge and experience that is not always available locally. Unclear procedures and slow handling between government bodies can make it harder to put them to work.

The association wants to hear how long applications usually stay in handling and which administrative obstacles firms meet. It also asks which government bodies are responsible for admitting and employing foreign workers.

A second question concerns flexible rules for specialists who work for set periods or take turns on rotation schedules. The VSB asks whether current rules fit temporary projects and such work patterns.

The VSB also stresses that foreign experts should pass knowledge to Surinamese staff and widen local employment. It says its goal is a business-friendly framework that supports competitiveness while protecting the local labour market.

Members were asked to send experiences and recommendations as soon as possible. The VSB says the answers will support its advocacy and lobbying towards the government and other bodies.

What the Permit Rules Already Say

The Ministry of Labour, Employment and Youth Affairs has handled foreign work permits since 1981 under the Work Permit for Foreigners decree. Any employer who wants to hire someone who is not Surinamese needs a permit granted by the labour director.

The ministry’s folder says a decision must come within 30 days of filing, with a possible extension of 30 more days in special circumstances. A refused applicant can appeal to the minister within 30 days of the decision.

When it assesses a request, the ministry looks at whether Surinamese workers are available for the post. It also weighs the foreigner’s length of stay, integration in Suriname and fit with the job requirements.

The fee is US$500 per application for work in the gold, oil and timber sectors, and US$100 per application elsewhere. Some groups need no permit, among them foreigners married to Surinamese citizens, refugees, returning nationals of Surinamese origin and skilled CARICOM nationals.

On Monday 14 July 2025 the ministry warned that some expatriates enter Suriname on a business visa while actually working. It said that is against immigration and labour law, and that a business visa cannot be used to apply for a work permit.

Our guide Suriname Visa and Residency 2026, Fees, Permits, Timelines sets out the steps for individuals and employers. The VSB inquiry into Suriname work permits asks whether real waiting times match the legal ones.

The Oil Project Behind the Hiring Call

TotalEnergies took the final investment decision on its GranMorgu project on Tuesday 1 October 2024, with a total investment estimated at about US$10.5 billion. The development is in offshore Block 58, with a floating production unit sized at 220,000 barrels a day and first oil expected in 2028.

At that decision the partners estimated more than US$1 billion of local content and more than 6,000 jobs in Suriname, of which 2,000 direct. Staatsolie, the state oil company, said on Monday 21 September 2026 that it holds a 20% interest.

Staatsolie also said that vessel construction, component fabrication and drilling preparations are on schedule, with first oil planned for 2028. It added that more than 100 Surinamese firms supply the project, with new exploration planned in Block 58 for 2027.

Our analysis Suriname Geopolitics Explained 2026 covers the wider stakes. A separate piece, Suriname Oil Shock Risks 13.5% Inflation, looks at the price risks before oil income arrives.

A Separate VSB Complaint on Import Rules

The VSB also wrote again to the Ministry of Economic Affairs, Entrepreneurship and Technological Innovation about the amended “Negative List” decree on imports. Starnieuws reported on Saturday 17 October 2026 that firms still lack clarity on documents and procedures before the rules apply from 1 November.

De Ware Tijd, a Paramaribo daily, repeated the complaint on Sunday 18 October 2026. The VSB says goods waiting at the port can cause extra storage costs, and it wants an answer before 31 October.

What It Means for US Readers

For Suriname work permits, American firms that send engineers, inspectors or managers should file through the employer well before travel. A business visa is not a route to paid work, according to the ministry’s July 2025 notice.

Budget planning for Suriname work permits should include the US$500 oil-sector fee and allow for a 60-day wait if the ministry extends. Those figures come from the ministry folder and may not reflect later changes.

Investors in APA or other project partners have no evidence from these reports of any delay to the 2028 start. Staatsolie described the project as on schedule on 21 September 2026, and the VSB call is about a process, not a slippage.

What Is Not Known

The reports do not say how many firms have complained, how many foreign workers are expected, or when the VSB will publish its findings. We found no statement on the VSB’s own website, so the call rests on two Surinamese news outlets.

It is not known how long permits take in practice or whether the ministry has replied. The ministry folder is a published guide, and current practice, fees and the One Stop route for oil-sector hires may differ.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did the VSB ask Surinamese firms to do?

It asked members to share experiences and recommendations on work and residence permits for foreign staff. The answers will support its lobbying towards the government.

How long do Suriname work permits take by law?

The ministry says a decision must come within 30 days of filing. In special circumstances the period can be extended by another 30 days.

How much does an oil-sector work permit cost?

The ministry folder lists a fee of US$500 per application for the gold, oil and timber sectors. Other sectors pay US$100 per application.

Can a US visitor work in Suriname on a business visa?

No, according to a ministry notice of 14 July 2025. A business visa cannot be used to apply for a work permit.

When is Suriname’s first offshore oil expected?

TotalEnergies and Staatsolie both give 2028 as the planned start for the GranMorgu project. Staatsolie said on 21 September 2026 that work was on schedule.

World.title: Trinidad Banking Row Follows 14 Oct CEO Exit
World.content:
Independence Square in Port of Spain, with bank buildings including a Republic Bank branch (Photo: Grueslayer, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO · BANKING

Key Facts — The country Trinidad and Tobago is a twin-island Caribbean energy producer whose biggest bank group, Republic Financial Holdings Ltd (RFHL), is listed on the local stock exchange.

— Why it matters RFHL runs banks in several Caribbean markets, and State-linked holders own about half of its shares, so a dispute over who leads it touches investors and the wider financial system.

— Why now Former prime minister Stuart Young spoke on Friday 16 October 2026, two days after RFHL lost its chief executive in waiting, and CNC3 carried his remarks on 17 October.

— What happened Richard Sammy left RFHL on Wednesday 14 October, and Karen Yip Chuck was named chief executive from 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approval.

— The numbers The central bank held its policy rate at 3.50% on 30 September, July inflation was 0.6% and first-quarter unemployment was 5.4%.

— What it means for you US investors, exporters and travellers should treat the interference claim as an allegation, and watch US dollar availability and the regulatory approval of the new chief executive.

— Still open Why the RFHL board changed course, whether any outside pressure played a part, and whether the Government and the central bank can show that dollars are easier to obtain.

The Trinidad banking row sharpened on Friday 16 October 2026, when former prime minister Stuart Young told a People’s National Movement (PNM) meeting in Port of Spain that political interference in banks could “bring collapse to Trinidad and Tobago”. CNC3 reported his remarks on the evening of Saturday 17 October, two days after Republic Financial Holdings Ltd (RFHL) announced that Richard Sammy, its chief executive in waiting, had left.

For US readers the row involves a bank group that the Trinidad Guardian calls a regional banking giant and puts its total assets at about US$19.9 billion at 30 June 2026. It also touches the availability of US dollars, which Young says is still scarce, while the Prime Minister has thanked US partners for advice on the banking sector.

Young’s claim is an allegation made at a party meeting, and the Finance Minister has rejected the related suggestion of lobbying by party financiers. This article separates what company notices and news reports document from what was said at the rally.

How the Trinidad Banking Row Began

Sammy left RFHL on Wednesday 14 October after 18 years with the group, both the Trinidad Express and a second daily reported. RFHL confirmed the change in a news release on Thursday 15 October.

On 30 January 2026 RFHL had named Sammy to succeed Nigel Baptiste, who has led the group since 2016. Sammy was due to become group president and chief executive on 1 January 2027.

A notice to the Trinidad and Tobago Stock Exchange (TTSE) dated 16 October names Karen Yip Chuck as group president and chief executive of RFHL and as president and managing director of Republic Bank Limited from 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Yip Chuck became one of three group vice-presidents in November 2022 and was elected president of the Trinidad and Tobago Chamber of Industry and Commerce in April.

The Express wrote that it understands Sammy neither resigned nor was dismissed, and that the departure was by mutual agreement. RFHL’s stock exchange notices give no reason, and a second daily noted that the group did not explain why its board changed course.

A further TTSE notice dated 17 October names Parasram (Vic) Salickram as senior group vice-president and David Robinson as group vice-president from 1 January 2027, also subject to regulatory approval. Salickram joined Republic in 2004 and Robinson in 1996, according to the same daily.

What Young Said at the PNM Meeting

Young, a former prime minister whose PNM lost the April 2025 general election, spoke at City Hall in Port of Spain on Friday night. He told supporters that Sammy’s exit deserved close public scrutiny and asked them to “keep your eyes on it very, very close”.

“If what we hear on the ground is true,” Young said, people were being removed because they were not giving money to “certain friends and financiers of the UNC”, and “we in real trouble in this country”. The UNC is the United National Congress, the governing party led by Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar.

Young presented the claim as something heard on the ground, and CNC3’s report gives no evidence for it. He also said that interference was aimed at putting “their people in place” so that they could “dip their hand”, which remains his allegation.

Young also rejected Government claims that foreign exchange is easier to obtain, saying people “can’t even get a hundred US” at a bank. That is his assertion, and the report cites no bank or central bank data to test it.

PNM leader Pennelope Beckles used the same meeting to urge unity before local government elections. Former finance minister Colm Imbert separately listed what he called ten warning signs of a drift towards authoritarian rule.

How the Government and the Bank Responded

Persad-Bissessar dismissed concerns that recent executive changes at First Citizens Bank and Republic Bank signal instability, calling them “minor internal remodelling”. “The banking system is very stable,” she said, adding thanks to “our foreign friends, especially those from the US”.

The Express published her remarks late on Friday 16 October, and she gave them in answer to questions about the executive changes rather than to Young’s speech. The Express report does not include a reply to Young’s speech.

Finance Minister Davendranath Tancoo called the suggestion that UNC financiers had lobbied for Yip Chuck “absolute and complete rubbish”, the daily reported. It also wrote that reports had circulated since early September that elements within the Government wanted Sammy replaced, and those reports are not established.

RFHL chairman Yashmid Karamath called Sammy a man of “unquestionable integrity”, and Sammy said he wished the group “every success in the future”. Central Bank Governor Larry Howai, speaking from the IMF meetings in Thailand, described Yip Chuck as an “excellent banker”, the same daily reported.

Why the State Stake Matters

That daily cited RFHL’s 2025 annual report in saying that the National Investment Fund Holding Company held 29.92% of the group and the National Insurance Board 18.81%. After the National Insurance Board bought a further 4.43 million shares on 2 September, the two State-linked holders together hold roughly 51.43%.

That stake is why the question of who runs the bank is political in Trinidad and Tobago, and the sources reviewed do not show that the Government directed the leadership change. RFHL’s notices say that each new appointment still needs regulatory approval.

The Economy Behind the Argument

The central bank held its repo rate at 3.50% on 30 September, with July headline inflation at 0.6% and first-quarter unemployment at 5.4%, up from 4.9% a year earlier. It also reported sales of foreign exchange to authorised dealers between June and August, and its next policy announcement is due on 23 December 2026.

Economist Dave Seerattan told a post-budget panel of the Trinidad and Tobago Manufacturers’ Association that foreign exchange shortages will persist after new gas projects start in 2027 unless structural weaknesses are fixed, that daily reported. His argument concerns the economy’s structure and does not touch the Republic leadership change.

What It Means for US Readers

Investors in Caribbean banks should note that Yip Chuck’s appointment still needs regulatory approval, and that RFHL’s stock exchange notices give no reason for the switch. The Trinidad banking row so far rests on a party speech and on denials, not on a finding by a regulator or a court.

US exporters and firms with Trinidad customers can expect the US dollar supply to stay a talking point, whichever side is right about it. Our company profile of Republic Financial Holdings Limited and our guide Trinidad and Tobago Explained give the background on the bank and the country.

Visitors should see no change in day-to-day banking from a boardroom reshuffle, and nothing in the reports suggests that deposits are at risk. The Prime Minister calls the system very stable, while Young warns that political meddling could change that.

What Is Not Known

It is not known why the RFHL board replaced Sammy with Yip Chuck, because the company has given no reason. It is also not known whether anyone outside the group pressed for the change, and no source reviewed provides evidence either way.

The account of Young’s speech comes from CNC3, which belongs to the same media group as the Trinidad Guardian, so it is a single-source report. We did not find a second outlet that covered his remarks on the bank.

Regulatory approval of Yip Chuck and the new vice-presidents is pending, and it is not known when it will come. Nor is it known whether Young’s remarks on US dollars reflect conditions across all banks, since no bank-level figures were published.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is leaving Republic Financial Holdings?

Richard Sammy left on Wednesday 14 October, after 18 years with the group. He was due to become chief executive on 1 January 2027.

Who will lead RFHL from January?

Karen Yip Chuck is named group president and chief executive from 1 January 2027, subject to regulatory approval. She is currently a group vice-president.

What did Stuart Young allege?

Young said at a PNM meeting on Friday 16 October that political interference in banks could bring collapse, and that people were being removed over money for UNC financiers if reports he had heard were true. He offered no evidence in the reported remarks, and the Finance Minister rejects the related lobbying suggestion.

Is the Trinidad banking sector stable?

Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar calls it very stable and describes the executive changes as minor internal remodelling. The reports reviewed show no regulatory finding of instability.

What does the Trinidad banking row mean for US readers?

It matters to investors in a major Caribbean bank group and to firms that need US dollars in Trinidad. The claim remains an allegation, and approval of the new chief executive is still pending.

World.title: Help needed to recover bag with passport, US cash and visa left at Western Border
World.content:
Help needed to recover bag with passport, US cash and visa left at Western Border

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A San Ignacio family is asking the public for help to recover a bag left behind at the Belize Western Border.

According to the family, a woman forgot her black Michael Kors tote bag on a bench outside the money exchange booth near the taxi stand on the night of Monday, October 12, while waiting for her ride.

The bag contained US cash, her passport with an American visa, a credit card and other personal belongings.

The family says video footage appears to show a woman in red shorts and a black blouse picking up the bag and getting into a red car.

They are asking anyone who can help identify the person or vehicle to come forward. A reward is being offered.

If you have information, please call or WhatsApp 610 8117.

World.title: 24 live rounds and suspected cocaine found hidden under cement block in Orange Walk
World.content:
24 live rounds and suspected cocaine found hidden under cement block in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Orange Walk police have recovered live ammunition and suspected cocaine hidden in an empty lot in Orange Walk Town.

Police say that around 8:00pm on Friday, October 16, officers from the Orange Walk GI3 Unit acted on information that someone had hidden something in a bushy lot at the corner of Chips Alley and Cabbage Street.

During checks, an officer found a green plastic bag tucked under a cement block.

Inside were 24 live 9mm rounds, 13 Luger brand and 11 S&B brand, along with a small plastic bag of white powder suspected to be cocaine.

The suspected cocaine weighed 7.3 grams.

No one was in the area at the time, and both the ammunition and drugs were sealed and logged as found property.

World.title: Teen reports being beaten with belt by stepfather in Orange Walk
World.content:
Teen reports being beaten with belt by stepfather in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 13 year old boy from Orange Walk District has reported to police that he was struck with a belt by his stepfather.

The boy visited the Orange Walk Police Station on Friday, October 16, accompanied by his biological father.

He told police that earlier that afternoon, his stepfather became upset after seeing his younger sibling walking with some boys the teen knew from school. He said his stepfather then lashed him with a belt on his hand and lower back.

According to the report, the boy was then told to pack his belongings and leave to stay with relatives. He later made his way to his father’s home, and his father took him to the police station.

A medico legal form was issued. The boy has been placed in the care of his father, and both parents have been instructed to report to the Human Services Department on Monday, October 19, for a follow up.

World.title: ATM Cave and Barton Creek closed as river levels rise
World.content:
ATM Cave and Barton Creek closed as river levels rise

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Actun Tunichil Muknal (ATM) and Barton Creek Archaeological Reserves are closed to visitors today because of elevated river levels.

The Institute of Archaeology of the National Institute of Culture and History (IA/NICH) made the announcement early Sunday morning, October 18.

All water related tour activities have also been suspended at the Nohoch Che’en Archaeological Reserve, a popular cave tubing destination.

All other archaeological reserves remain open for visitors.

The IA/NICH says it is monitoring conditions and will provide updates as necessary.

The closures come after days of heavy rain across the country, with an excessive rainfall warning issued by the National Meteorological Service.

World.title: Swerving Toyota stop ends with taxi driver arrested and car impounded
World.content:
Swerving Toyota stop ends with taxi driver arrested and car impounded

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 51 year old taxi driver of Savannah Street, Orange Walk Town, has been charged with failing to provide a specimen.

He is Jaime Gomez.

Police say officers on burglary patrol on San Antonio Road around 10:50pm on Thursday, October 15, saw a white Toyota Corolla swerving from side to side on Savannah Street.

When officers stopped the car, Gomez allegedly got out of the driver’s side staggering, leaving the engine running and headlights on. Officers say they smelled a strong odour of alcohol on his breath.

He was arrested for driving under the influence and taken to the Orange Walk Police Station, where he was asked for a urine specimen. Police say he refused three times.

He was then taken to the Northern Regional Hospital, where, in the presence of a doctor, he again refused to give a urine or blood sample.

Gomez was charged on Friday morning and granted bail to appear in the Orange Walk Magistrate’s Court on Monday, October 19. His car was impounded.

World.title: Excessive rainfall warning remains as Belize braces for another 2 to 4 inches of rain
World.content:
Excessive rainfall warning remains as Belize braces for another 2 to 4 inches of rain

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): An excessive rainfall warning remains in effect for Belize this Sunday, though the rain is expected to ease somewhat later in the day.

The National Meteorological Service says an additional 2 to 4 inches of rain is likely over some areas in the next 12 to 24 hours. Residents are advised to monitor the weather and stay tuned to official updates.

A moist east northeasterly airflow continues over the country. Skies will be cloudy with sunny breaks today and cloudy at times tonight.

Showers and periods of light rain are affecting most areas this morning, but the activity is expected to decrease somewhat by the afternoon. Tonight, a few showers and some light rain will affect mainly the coast, with isolated thunderstorms possible.

Coastal areas will reach a high of 86°F (30°C) with a low of 79°F (26°C). Inland areas will hit 90°F (32°C), cooling to 73°F (23°C). The hills will see a high of 79°F (26°C) and a low of 68°F (20°C).

Today’s forecast was issued by forecaster Derrick Rudon.

World.content:
Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware is hosting a public auction of industrial equipment, commercial tools, generators, office machinery and surplus supplies.
