NEW DELHI: As the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) intensifies its campaign demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumarâs resignation, a group calling itself the Laal Hit Janta Party has emerged as a satirical counter to the outfit.At a meeting in the national capital on Sunday, the outfit called for constitutional values, accountability and responsible public participation, while reiterating its opposition to the CJP's demonstrations, according to a statement issued by the organisation.The outfit urged young citizens, particularly Gen Z, to engage in democratic processes through peaceful protests, factual communication and legal channels. Its motto is: âNation First, Respect for the Constitution, Democracy as Our Identity,â while its guiding principle is: âStrong in Opposition, Peaceful in Action, Committed to the Nation.âAccording to news agency PTI, the meeting was held at Malviya Smriti Bhawan on Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg and was addressed by convenor Ayan Bhatnagar and filmmakers Richa Gupta, Pawan Nagpal and Atul Gangwar.The group's name appears to be a satirical reference to a popular insect-control brand, mirroring the CJP's name.The outfit had earlier held a gathering at Janpath, where around 200 people assembled to denounce alleged assaults on police personnel and abusive language directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi during protests.Speaking to IANS, Bhatnagar had said the group was not formed to challenge the CJP through public debate."The Lal Hit Janta Party was not formed to contest elections, as we have already made clear. We stand against CJP and its protests. We oppose cockroaches who want to weaken the country's democracy and attempt to create anarchy in the country," he said."We will gather in different groups, on both large and small scales, present our views and arguments, and take our message forward. We will show them that a party like the 'Lal HIT Janta Party' now exists to challenge them. If you have the courage, come and debate," Bhatnagar added.In its statement on Sunday's meeting, the organisation said political debate over electoral processes should be based on verified evidence, transparent procedures and constitutional mechanisms. It also stressed the importance of preserving the independence and credibility of constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, amid calls for Kumar's resignation.These developments come against the backdrop of widespread demonstrations against the CEC regarding alleged irregularities in electoral roll revisions. The protesters, including opposition parties, the CJP and several student groups have claimed that the exercise led to the deletion of lakhs of votersâ names and raised questions over changes to Form 6, which is used to register as a voter. These allegations, however, remain subject to verification.The counter-outfit called for questions about political organisations, their funding and alleged links to unlawful activities to be examined through verified documents, lawful investigations and official findings.

World.title: Delhi SIR: Public audit in two booths finds over 100 voters wrongly marked absent, shifted, or dead
World.content:
At least 100 voters from two polling booths in Delhi’s Okhla constituency were found to have been wrongly classified as absent, shifted, dead or duplicate (ASDD) during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, a public audit covering 258 households over seven days found.

Also read | Muslims disproportionately flagged in Delhi SIR

These voters, who said their names were wrongly missing from Delhi’s draft electoral roll, turned up for a Jan Sunwai, or public hearing, held in the Batla House area of the national capital on Sunday (October 18, 2026). The event was organised by civil society organisations such as Jan Sarokar, Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS), Voter Adhikar Manch, and the National Federation of Indian Women (NFIW).

The hearing was intended for residents of G and K blocks, covering polling booths 61 and 65, but repeated announcements drew voters from other booths as well. More than 150 voters registered to present their cases before a panel comprising Supreme Court advocates Nayantara Roy and Sumita Hazarika and transparency activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri.

Okhla had more than 1.85 lakh voters in the draft roll published after the SIR enumeration phase, of which over 67,000 names were placed on the notice list and nearly 1.6 lakh appeared in the ASDD list. This constituency saw the second highest rate of deletions.

Decades-long residents affected

Among those who turned up were Faiyaz Ahmed, 74, a retired professor of mechanical engineering at Jamia Millia Islamia University. Despite living at the same address for more than five decades, Mr. Ahmed was marked “untraceable/absent”, while his wife, Anjum Ara, 62, was listed as “permanently shifted” in the ASDD list published on August 31.

“Should one person or one institution have the power to remove a citizen’s name from the electoral roll like this? I have voted in nearly every election since the 1970s,” Mr. Ahmed asked.

Their son, Babu Sardar Khan, said he had submitted duly filled enumeration forms for both his parents to the area’s booth-level officer (BLO). However, only his own name appeared in the draft roll. Mr. Khan collected Form 6, meant for new voter enrolment, which is used by voters left out of the draft roll, for both his parents. He will have to submit the forms to the BLO or the constituency’s voter centre.

Naeemuddin, 48, who said he had lived at the same address for 30 years, was similarly marked as “permanently shifted”. He said he had visited the BLO, who had taken his photographs and obtained his signature on a form.

Furious, he showed his driving licence from the 1990s and an arms licence, which he said had required extensive documentation and verification. “How can it be that now I register as a new voter and swipe off all my voting records? And why is no one from the Election Commission telling me this, but social workers?” said Mr. Naeemuddin, a former government adviser.

Unaware of special camps

The Delhi Chief Electoral Officer’s office has been holding special camps every weekend since September 20 at all polling stations, with a stated objective of ensuring that “no eligible voter should be left out”. Earlier this week, it also directed field officers to re-verify ASDD entries through door-to-door visits and restore the names of eligible voters.

However, around 20 people who spoke to The Hindu said they were unaware of the special camps. Some attended the hearing because they did not know who their BLO was, while others said their BLOs had not contacted them.

“We had also invited the respective BLOs, Electoral Registration Officer, District Magistrate, and ECI officials through the CEO Delhi office, but they did not come,” a statement from the organisers said.

‘Only option is to enrol afresh’

Tanvir Anwer said that when he went to collect the enumeration form, the BLO told him that his brother’s form was unavailable and his name was not on the voter list. He was told that his brother had been deleted before the revision. However, Md. Farid Anwar’s name appeared in the ASDD list, indicating that his enumeration form had been marked “uncollectable”. Mr. Anwer attended the hearing seeking clarity on the next steps. A volunteer told him that the only available option was to apply for fresh enrolment.

Like him, at least 110 people collected copies of Form 6 and a declaration seeking details of their or their relatives’ previous SIR records. Organisers said they had printed the forms available online and were directing voters to polling stations where BLOs were present, as they were not authorised to collect the applications themselves.

All the applications received through Form 6 till October 30 will be considered for inclusion in the final roll to be published on December 4.

There was also a curious case of Ravi, 37, a resident of Okhla village. His wife Anita found out at the hearing through the EPIC ID number mentioned on the voter ID card that he has been shown as ‘dead’. However, his record was present in the draft roll through a different EPIC number. “This is the EPIC card I was issued in 2023, and how am I supposed to know that my EPIC number has been changed on the same address? I don’t have EPIC cards,” he said.

World.title: Israel Police arrest eight suspects over settler attacks on diplomats, U.S. photojournalist in West Bank
World.content:
Israeli police have arrested eight suspects in connection with weekend attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians, European diplomats and Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine in the occupied West Bank, The Times of Israel reported.

Ms. Levine was assaulted and injured while covering Palestinians harvesting olives on Friday (October 17, 2026), while European diplomats from France, Belgium and Poland were targeted near the Palestinian Christian village of Taybeh on Saturday (October 18, 2026).

The arrests were made under an operation dubbed “Olive Leaf,” launched at dawn in coordination with Israel’s Shin Bet security agency and with an escort from the Israel Defence Forces (IDF), police said.

“So far, eight suspects have been arrested and several vehicles have been seized,” the police said, adding that IDF and Border Police forces were also “conducting enforcement operations” to dismantle illegal settler outposts, address violations of military-issued restraining orders and investigate an “intrusion into a Palestinian home.” The eight suspects have been taken for questioning, while the operation remains ongoing, the police added.

Ms. Levine underwent surgery at Beilinson Hospital on Saturday after the assault in the Binyamin region of the West Bank. Her condition was reported as moderate, and she sustained injuries to her limbs, according to The Jerusalem Post.

The attack on the photojournalist came a day before the assault on European diplomats near Taybeh, east of Ramallah, which prompted condemnation from European governments and Canada, with officials calling for accountability and protection for diplomats and civilians.

Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand said Ottawa joined the European Union and its allies in condemning the attack, calling it part of a broader pattern of settler violence.

“This unacceptable attack in Taybeh is part of a broader pattern of settler violence that threatens Palestinian communities and undermines peace efforts,” Ms. Anand said in a statement shared on X. Welcoming the investigation launched by Israeli police, she said Israel, as the occupying power, must ensure those responsible are held accountable and guarantee the protection of diplomats and civilians in the West Bank.

Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar also condemned the violence, saying a police investigation had been opened and forensic investigators were collecting evidence to identify those responsible. Mr. Sa’ar, however, noted that the diplomatic delegation’s visit had not been coordinated with the IDF in advance, saying such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors.

The IDF separately condemned the attack and confirmed that police officers and forensic investigators had entered the area alongside Israeli soldiers to collect evidence and record witness testimonies. According to a preliminary military inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene when the attack occurred.

The military also said the initial report had been sent to a brigade operations room designated to receive reports from security personnel rather than civilians, adding that the circumstances surrounding the incident would be examined.

World.title: A rift in the U.S.-Israel special relationship
World.content:
(This article is part of the View From India newsletter curated by The Hindu’s foreign affairs experts. To get the newsletter in your inbox every Monday, subscribe here.)

“Donald J. Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time,” U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance said on June 18 in an unusual direct rebuke to the Israeli critics of the U.S.-Iran memorandum of understanding. “If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world,” he said, adding: “The other thing that I would say is that over the last three months, two-thirds of the defensive weapons that have protected your homeland have been built by American hands and paid for by American tax dollars.”

Also Read: Israel Police arrest eight suspects over settler attacks on diplomats, U.S. photojournalist in West Bank

In an interview, Mr. Vance , who had reportedly opposed the U.S.-led war on Iran, said Israel “cannot kill its way out of every security challenge” it is facing. In a different podcast, he criticised Israeli advocates for conflating criticism of the state of Israel to antisemitism. “If everything is Jew-hatred, then nothing is Jew-hatred,” he said. In the same interview, he said President Trump has “some disagreements” with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on how to bring the war to an end. “They’re a good partner in the same way that the United Kingdom or France are good partners -- that doesn’t mean that we’re always going to have aligned interests,” he added.

Mr. Trump was more measured in his criticism, but, while speaking to reporters in France, he also raised some uncomfortable questions about Israel’s conduct of the war in Lebanon. “You don’t have to knock down an apartment house every time you’re looking for somebody,” Mr. Trump said about Israeli attacks on Lebanon’s civilian areas. “There are a lot of people in those apartment houses. And they’re not all Hezbollah.” He also said Israel was fighting Hezbollah “too long” and “too many people have been killed”. In the recent past, Axios had reported that Trump had angry phone calls with Mr. Netanyahu in which he used expletives to slam Israel’s bombing of Lebanon.

The public criticisms from America’s top leadership about its “special ally” point to a growing rift between the two countries over the Iran question. And the criticism became public only after the MoU was reached between the U.S. and Iran on June 15. The main reason for the rift is the disagreement between Mr. Trump and Mr. Netanyahu on how to end the war on Iran. Israel would not prefer a diplomatic settlement that would lift sanctions on Iran and leave the country conventionally more powerful in West Asia. But the U.S., having failed to meet its objectives through 40 days of bombing, wants to end the conflict, remove the bottleneck in the Strait of Hormuz that has held the global economy for ransom, and address the nuclear question diplomatically.

There are three important factors that are driving this rift. The first is public opinion in America. The war on Iran is unpopular in the U.S. and the economic costs of the war are rising. Mi-term primaries will begin shortly and Mr. Trump wants to extricate himself from the war at the soonest. In the U.S., the public opinion about Israel is also undergoing a transformation. According to a February Gallup poll, for the first time in over two decades, Americans are no longer more sympathetic towards Israelis than Palestinians: 41% Americans now sympathise with Palestinians, while 36% sympathise with Israelis. According to a recent Pew research poll,60% of U.S. adults have an unfavourable view of Israel, while 59% have little or no confidence in Mr. Netanyahu.

The second factor is that sections of Mr. Trump’s MAGA base have started revolting against the war on Iran and America’s ties with Israel. Popular conservative podcaster Tucker Carlson has emerged the champion of this revolt. They argue that Mr. Netanyahu led Mr. Trump into the war on Iran—or that the U.S. was fighting this war on behalf of “a foreign power”. They ask Mr. Trump to put American interests first and leave the war with Iran.

The third factor is Lebanon. The very first clause of the memorandum of understanding states that the ceasefire should come into force on all fronts, including Lebanon. It also calls for ensuring Lebanon’s “territorial integrity and sovereignty”--meaning Israeli troops should pull back from Lebanon. Both Prime Minister Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz have said the Israeli troops will not withdraw from southern Lebanon. This keeps Lebanon as a flashpoint with a potential for escalation. Mr. Netanyahu seems determined to use the Lebanon card, making the U.S.-Iran peace process complicated. Iran, which has started direct talks with the U.S., has said that it had closed the ‘Strait of Hormuz ’ in response to Israel’s attacks on Lebanon. So if Mr. Trump wants a successful final agreement with Iran, he should find a way to rein in Mr. Netanyahu or even force him to withdraw troops from Lebanon. Israel’s unrelenting attacks on Lebanon, which has complicated the peace process, has deepened the frustration in the White House. To understand the U.S.-Iran deal and its implications for West Asia, see this explainer in The Hindu FAQ: What does the U.S.-Iran agreement say? | Explained

The Top Five

1. Group of Seven | A platform for the globalised elite

The grouping of industrialised nations, founded in the 1970s, has weathered major geopolitical storms across the 20th and 21st centuries to remain a key forum for discussions and decision-making on global conflicts and economic challenges, writes Kallol Bhattacherjee.

2. Telegram | Mass messaging and more

The ‘WhatsApp alternative’ with a strong commitment to user privacy, which has over 15 crore users in India, is facing a week-long ban in the country, writes Aroon Deep.

3. EU passes law allowing offshore deportation centres

The Return Regulation approves the deportation of irregular immigrants to third-party countries; states can now form agreements with non-EU countries and set up deportation centres there; even as European Commission head Ursula von der Leyen hailed the law as ‘fair and firm’, critics say it has ‘little regard for people’s safety, dignity and rights, and fails to uphold the EU’s fundamental values’, writes Joan Sony Cherian.

4. How Herat defied the Taliban regime, chanting ‘women, work and freedom’

The protests in the Afghan city in the first week of June were triggered by the enforcement of a dress code, which requires women to wear burqa in public; many women, including those wearing traditional Afghan wear of manto, were arrested, but released later as entire communities protested, writes Smriti Sudesh.

5. Britain after Brexit, divided, uncertain and stagnant

Ten years after Brexit, Britain still searches for direction, writes Priyanjali Malik.

World.title: Israeli PM Netanyahu warns of potentially hostile future U.S. President, calls for alliances with India, Latin America
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday (October 18, 2026) warned that a future U.S. President could be hostile towards Israel, calling for new alliances with countries such as India and those in Latin America to strengthen his country's position.

Also Read: Israel Police arrest eight suspects over settler attacks on diplomats, U.S. photojournalist in West Bank

Mr. Netanyahu made the remarks at an event where he presented his security doctrine, nine days before Israel's October 27 election.

The remarks came hours before a strong endorsement he received from U.S. President Donald Trump, who publicly expressed his support for Mr. Netanyahu's re-election bid days before the country goes to the polls.

"In two years, a President, man or woman, could come to power who is very hostile to Israel," Mr. Netanyahu said.

"How would you deal with that? How would you operate in relation to the United States? And beyond that, what solutions would be necessary?", he questioned.

The Israeli Premier stressed that Israel must use the remaining years of Trump's presidency to strengthen its position while preparing for a potentially dramatic shift in American policy.

"First, we must do everything we can during these two years, and during the following two years, in the American arena, through good times and bad," he said.

"The second thing is to create other alliances. That is what I am working on now with many countries in our region and outside it. India is not a small country, and there are many others," the Israeli Prime Minister emphasised.

He pointed to political developments in Latin America as another opportunity to expand Israel's network of allies.

"There is a major shift in Latin America, and there could be an enormous change in Brazil in just a few days," Mr. Netanyahu pointed out adding, "We must expand our pool of alliances and develop capabilities that make us valuable to everyone."

Mr. Netanyahu has often evoked India and his relationship with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to argue that Israel is not isolated globally and to demonstrate his government's diplomatic successes.

Countering issues of delegitimisation and alliances amid a prolonged war, Mr. Netanyahu, in May this year, in a much publicised statement, said that his country enjoys a "unique relationship" with "huge power" India where there is "crazy love" for Israel.

Many analysts in Israel feel that the growing apathy among Democrats in the U.S. results from poor choices Mr. Netanyahu made over the years.

His relations with Democratic Party-led Presidents Barack Obama and Joe Biden were often tense, which he presented to his supporters as the courage of a strong leader willing to stand up against American Presidents to safeguard Israel's interests, the analysts believe.

This has been a cornerstone of Mr. Netanyahu's election campaigns and a recipe for electoral success, they said. He is Israel's longest-serving Prime Minister.

Gadi Eisenkot, the main challenger to the Israeli Prime Minister in the upcoming polls, sharply criticised the presentation, describing it as an empty political exercise rather than a serious national security strategy.

"Nine days before the election and three years after the gravest failure and disaster in Israel's history, with every war front still open, Netanyahu decided to present his 'security doctrine' to the public," Mr. Eisenkot said.

"Two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing whatsoever to do with a security doctrine, reveal more than anything the strategic vacuum Mr. Netanyahu has left the State of Israel in and his disregard for the security of Israeli citizens," he asserted.

Mr. Eisenkot, a former Chief of Staff of the Israel Defence Forces, accused Mr. Netanyahu of attempting to manipulate public opinion and spread fear ahead of the election.

"This is Mr. Netanyahu's method: manipulating perceptions, frightening people and trying to divert attention from the parade of lies and racism surrounding his campaign tonight," he said.

World.title: BJP veteran leader L. K. Advani discharged from Delhi hospital after improvement in health
World.content:
BJP veteran leader L. K. Advani was discharged from a Delhi hospital on Monday (October 19, 2026) after his medical condition improved.

Mr. Advani was admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on October 16, following a chest infection and pulmonary complications. He was under the care of Dr. Vinit Suri, senior consultant in neurology. Mr. Advani showed improvement in his medical condition, according to a statement issued by the hospital.

In a press statement the hospital authorities said: “Mr L.K. Advani, who was admitted to Apollo Hospitals on 16th October with a chest infection, is being discharged today. He has been under the care of Dr. Vinit Suri, Senior Consultant - Neurology and has shown improvement in his medical status.”

Mr. Advani served as the BJP president on multiple occasions and was India’s deputy Prime Minister from 2002 to 2004. He played a key role in the party’s rise as a major national political force.

World.title: Albanian PM refuses to quit as violent protests enter sixth day
World.content:
Albanian police fired water cannon and tear gas on Sunday (October 18, 2026) as violent anti-government protests entered a sixth day and Prime Minister Edi Rama rejected demonstrators' demands that he resign.

Violent demonstrations have rocked Tirana since Tuesday (October 13, 2026) with protesters calling for action over poor university conditions, high tuition fees and corruption.

Hundreds of protesters gathered again at noon in front of the Education Ministry chanting "Rama, resign" amid a tense standoff with police.

After police bid to disperse the crowds the protests scattered across the city centre, escalating in hours-long violent clashes.

Protesters set ablaze litter bins in the streets, smashed windows, including at the headquarters of the governing Socialist party, and set fire to a police station and the entrance of the Interior Ministry.

Chaotic clashes extended to the main boulevard and square, with demonstrators throwing rocks, Molotov cocktails and firing pyrotechnic devices, as the police responded with rubber bullets and tear gas, according to an AFP journalist.

Ambulances were seen rushing in and out of the scenes of clashes to pick up the injured.

The Ministry of Health told AFP that 16 police officers were injured — 14 of them when protesters attacked the police station.

Albert Nushi, from the police public security department, said on Sunday (October 18, 2026) evening that a police station in Tirana was attacked with Molotov cocktails and pyrotechnic devices that endangered both officers and people held in custody.

"An attack on a police station is not a protest. Violence against police officers, attacks on institutions, and actions that endanger human lives cannot be tolerated," he said.

He urged protesters to stay away from masked individuals behind the violence and "assemble in a peaceful manner".

According to the Ministry of Health, 28 people were injured on Sunday — 19 police officers, four protesters, four passers-by and a journalist.

Before the protest, shops and offices in the city centre secured their doors and windows with metal shutters, while city workers removed paving stones to prevent them being thrown by protesters.

In a video broadcast lasting more than an hour, Mr. Rama ruled out resigning, stating that the protests are the "work of an outside hand".

According to Austrian federal press service Rama's official visit to Federal Chancellor Christian Stocker scheduled for Monday, has been cancelled by the Albanian side.

Buildings on fire

Writer and activist Lura Elezi, 38, told AFP that she is protesting for "a better life, rule of law and against crime and corruption".

"I love my country, but my government does not respect us - it defies us. Every citizen must take responsibility for their country, taking on the duty to lead, to love, and not to destroy one's own nation", she said.

Tirana saw its harshest violence on Saturday when protesters threw rocks, Molotov cocktails, metal objects and pyrotechnic devices at police, and torched cars and litter bins to use as barricades against advancing police.

Buildings including a court, banks and a post office were set on fire or severely damaged.

According to a Health Ministry report issued Sunday, 65 people were injured, including 37 police officers, with 12 people hospitalised during Saturday's protests.

Since Tuesday, 272 people have been injured in the clashes, including 169 police, the Ministry said.

Albania's close ally the United States reacted late Saturday. Its embassy in Tirana urged "restraint and calm on all sides".

The European Commission in a written statement "condemned the use of violence in Tirana and other cities", adding that the response to it "must remain proportionate".

Also Read : Protest in Albania over Trump-linked resort project | Green Humour by Rohan Chakravarty

"In a candidate country firmly committed to the EU accession process... grievances should be handled through constructive dialogue and in a peaceful manner," the statement said.

The unrest follows months of anti-government protests in the Balkan nation, initially sparked by a controversial resort development linked to U.S. President Donald Trump's family.

World.title: Four friends clicking selfies on overbridge killed after truck hits SUV in Varanasi
World.content:
Four people were killed and three seriously injured after a speeding truck rammed into their SUV while they were taking selfies on an overbridge in Varanasi on Monday (October 19, 2026) morning, police said.

The group of friends, residents of Shivpuri, Varanasi, was returning from the Vindhyachal temple in Mirzapur. On the way, they stopped their Scorpio on the overbridge near Rupapur, on the Prayagraj-Varanasi highway, to click selfies, according to police. A speeding truck coming from the Prayagraj side rammed into the SUV from behind and ran over the youths standing nearby, they said.

Police rushed to the spot after receiving information about the incident and launched a rescue operation. Those trapped in the vehicle were freed with the help of a gas cutter, and the injured were taken to hospital for treatment.

The deceased have been identified as Aman Yadav, Golu Yadav and Alok Mishra; the identity of the fourth victim is yet to be ascertained, police said. Two of the injured, Kanhaiya Yadav and Nikhil Kumar, are in critical condition; efforts are being made to identify the third injured person, they said.

World.title: Mamata’s party asks if BJP government put spectacle over safety in awarding Chorbagan puja
World.content:
The Mamata Trinamool Congress on Monday (October 19, 2026) questioned whether spectacle had been prioritised over public safety in awarding the 'Best of the Best Durga Puja' to Chorbagan Sarbojonin, where 19 people died in a stampede.

The Information and Cultural Affairs Department, in association with the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, had conferred the 'Serar Sera-3' (Best of the Best) Devi Durga Samman 2026 on Chorbagan Sarbojonin Durgotsav Samity.

In a social media post, the party questioned the recognition given to the puja, which had also won awards for best lighting, best pandal and best environment-friendly puja.

"The CM blamed the theme and low lighting for the problems faced by visitors. Yet the same Puja was recognised for Best Lighting, Best Pandal and Best Environment-Friendly Puja," it said.

"So, what exactly was being judged? Spectacle over safety? Awards over accountability," the party asked, adding, "When a Puja is celebrated as the best, who takes responsibility when public safety fails?.

The stampede occurred on Saturday (October 17, 2026) evening during Saptami, killing 19 people and injuring 25 others.

Following the incident, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari urged organisers of theme-based Durga Pujas to ensure adequate lighting at venues and provide sufficient entry and exit gates for visitors.

"Many pandals are dimly lit in the name of theme puja," he said, asking organisers to follow the advice of the authorities.

Durga Puja organisers across Kolkata and other parts of West Bengal compete to attract visitors with elaborate theme-based pandals and installations.

Meanwhile, a high-level committee constituted to review safety arrangements at major Durga Puja pandals across the State visited several community pujas in Kolkata on Sunday (October 18, 2026).

The panel includes Disaster Management Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh, Director General of Fire Services Anuj Sharma and STF Director General Jawed Shamim.

Residents of Chorbagan said sudden rain, a narrow lane, a heavy rush of visitors and inadequate deployment of volunteers and police personnel for crowd management contributed to the stampede.

World.title: Army major martyred, 4 terrorists killed in Balochistan IBOs: ISPR
World.content:
An army major was martyred and four terrorists were killed during intelligence-based operations in Balochistan, the military’s media wing said on Monday.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement that security forces conducted a series of operations in areas of Shadi Kaur and Pasni in Gwadar, and Jattakabad in Kalat district, on the reported presence of multiple hideouts of Fitna al Hindustan.

The state has designated Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.

In the first operation on October 18, security forces conducted an IBO in the general area of Jattakabad, during which four terrorists were eliminated.

“A large cache of arms and ammunition was also recovered,” it added.

In the second operation, ISPR added that security forces conducted a series of clearance operations in the general area of Shadi Kaur, Pasni, in Gwadar.

It added that 34-year-old Major Wajahat Waheed, a Lahore resident who was leading the operation, was martyred in an improvised explosive device (IED) attack.

“Sanitisation operations will continue to eliminate any other terrorists found in the area. The relentless counterterrorism campaign under the vision of ‘Azm-e-Istehkam’, as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on the National Action Plan, will continue at full pace.”

“Security forces and law enforcement agencies remain committed to eliminating the menace of foreign-sponsored and supported terrorism from the country,” ISPR added.

President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday, in separate statements, commended security forces for the successful operations.

They also paid tribute to Major Wajahat Waheed, extending their condolences to his family.

President Zardari, in a statement posted on X, reaffirmed that conspiracies of “the terrorists’ foreign patrons and their local facilitators will be thwarted”.

PM Shehbaz reiterated the resolve to continue the fight against foreign-sponsored terrorism until its complete eradication, state media reported.

Intensified operations

Balochistan has witnessed an increase in terrorist activities in recent years, prompting security forces to intensify counter-terrorism operations.

A day earlier, security forces killed eight “India-sponsored” terrorists during IBOs conducted in the Quetta, Nushki and Khuzdar districts of Balochistan.

On the night of Oct 12/13, security forces busted a terrorist hideout and killed five terrorists during an IBO in Washuk, ISPR said .

Days later, Balochistan government officials said that six terrorists affiliated with the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), two would-be female suicide bombers, and two commanders of a banned organisation had been arrested during IBOs across the province.

They said around 90 arrested terrorists were being held at a centre where investigations and legal proceedings were under way.

Earlier this month, five terrorists were eliminated in Balochistan’s Mastung district, state media reported .

World.title: Recriminations grow over failure of PTI protest plan
World.content:
• Salman Akram Raja tries to quell talk of ‘disagreement’ among core committee members

• Insiders say march date was announced without consultation; protest plans kept under wraps, even from party leaders

ISLAMABAD: Controversy over its failure to hold a protest march continues to plague the PTI, with the fallout suggesting differences within its leadership over who is to blame for the botched mobilisation, even as party leaders continued to publicly deny any disarray.

With questions mounting, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja turned to social media on Sunday to play down talk of a “disagreement” during a meeting of the party’s core committee and to answer the allegations made against Sohail Afridi, the non-functional chief minister of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

“There should be no ambiguity,” Mr Raja wrote on X, calling Mr Afridi “a brave young man” who has stayed steadfast with the ideology of PTI founder Imran Khan. He said, however, that the administrative aspects of the protest march needed to be critically reviewed to counter the “narratives” being propagated against Mr Afridi.

He accused critics of presenting core committee discussions “out of context” and distorting them as part of “conspiratorial narratives”.

Meanwhile, a senior party leader who attended the meeting and spoke to Dawn on condition of anonymity, painted a less rosy picture. The leader said the party’s core committee meetings had started to discuss why the protest march failed and that the discussion was still ongoing.

“On Saturday night, the meeting started after 10pm and ended after 2am. As many as 16 members of the committee got an opportunity to speak, and the remaining will speak in upcoming sessions,” he said.

“At the outset, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar said the meeting was called to discuss the current situation and the way forward. However, Raja suggested that they first discuss how the date for the protest march, Sept 27, was announced,” the leader added.

“During the meeting, it was revealed that in August, Afridi had called a meeting in KP which was attended by Gohar, Raja, Asad Qaiser, Shafiullah Jan, Mina Khan, Shahid Khatak and Taimur Jhagra,” he said.

Afridi had announced that the march would be held on Sept 27, but this information was leaked to some vloggers subsequently. When criticism started that it had not been discussed in the political committee and core committee, the meetings of both committees were called on the same day, and in the evening Afridi made the announcement at a public meeting.

The insider further disclosed that the leadership was kept in the dark regarding the operational strategy for the protest and the party’s broader negotiation tactics.

“It was also revealed that Afridi was asked a number of times what the plan was, but he kept his cards close to his chest,” he said.

“The meeting also heard that the PTI team had decided to walk out over the issue of terrorism, and when they realised it could trigger criticism, it was decided to use the name of Imran Khan and a meeting with him.”

The leader said that during the meeting, Raja asked Ali Asghar Khan, son of the late Air Marshal Asghar Khan, why the party did not hold the protest march after Afridi’s arrest.

Ali Asghar Khan, who is PTI secretary general in KP and head of the coordination committee for the protest march, said he was not aware of any such plans.

“Asghar claimed that he had asked Afridi and Junaid Akbar many times, but they said details would be shared soon,” the leader said.

“It annoyed many members of the core committee, as they said more than 1,400 workers and leaders were arrested under the Maintenance of Public Order law, but PTI in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa did not have any plan.”

Another leader said Haleem Adil Sheikh confessed that the opposition was 70 per cent responsible and the government 30pc responsible for the failure of talks.

“The agreement was finalised as Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi brought an amended agreement that both sides agreed to without meeting Imran Khan,” he said.

“Soon after that, a call also came from Afridi to say that the meeting could not be held without first consulting Imran Khan.”

The committee also discussed reports claiming that Barrister Gohar had given approval to establish offices of TTAP at the district level, the leader claimed.

“Raoof Hasan objected and asked how it was possible, and Barrister Gohar said that he did not give any such approval.”

The source further claimed that during the meeting, Seemabia Tahir suggested that the party should go for another protest march, but a majority of the members said that it was not possible during the current circumstances.

When contacted for a response, PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram declined to comment on the matter.

Published in Dawn, October 19th, 2026

World.title: Oil-rich Alberta vote to determine next step towards possible separation from Canada
World.content:
Alberta decides Monday if it wants to pursue a binding referendum on leaving Canada, with Prime Minister Mark Carney warning a separatist win would bring dangerous uncertainty during a trade war with the United States.

Polls indicate less than a quarter of people in the western Canadian province support independence.

But attention has focused on turnout in the days before the vote, and whether a motivated separatist camp could defy the polls, helped by complacent federalists.

“Don’t let anyone tell you this is already decided. Turnout will determine the outcome,” Carney told a rally on Thursday.

Carney, who grew up in Alberta, has called the referendum “a dangerous bluff” as US President Donald Trump imposes punishing tariffs and levels annexation threats aimed — the prime minister says — at breaking Canadian resolve.

“Vote like Canada depends on it, because it does,” Carney said.

Alberta has the world’s fourth-largest proven oil reserves and separatist momentum has been driven by anger over Ottawa’s management of the sector.

Many Albertans loathed Carney’s predecessor, Justin Trudeau, who they accused of trying to suppress oil production to advance his pro-climate agenda.

“If you want me to pinpoint who is responsible for the separatist sentiment, I think it’s Justin Trudeau,” Alberta Premier Danielle Smith told the Canadaland podcast this month.

At a separatist rally in Edmonton on Saturday, 61-year-old Sandy Martel said people connected to the oil industry feel “robbed, cheated (and) mistreated.” “It’s time to stand up and say stop,” she told AFP.

The vote comes days after a fire at a military base in the province left at least four soldiers dead and wounded dozens, prompting a national outpouring of condolences.

Smith, a conservative, says she wants Alberta to remain in Canada but called the referendum to settle the divisive issue.

If a majority votes to separate, she has pledged to move forward with a binding referendum.

If the federalists win, Smith says the secession question should be considered closed.

Analysts have compared Smith’s tactics to those of former UK prime minister David Cameron, who had hoped to resolve the debate over Britain’s European Union membership with a vote.

Carney led the Bank of England through the turmoil that surrounded Brexit, and issued a warning to Albertans about that experience on Thursday.

“It wasn’t clear what ‘Brexit’ meant at the time,” he told a Calgary television station.

“For the next few years, while that was being determined, there was huge uncertainty, investments stopped, the economy started to underperform,” he added, cautioning over unintended economic consequences.

AI influence

Monday’s referendum features 10 questions, including several related to immigration, but focus is on question 10, which asks: “Should Alberta remain a province of Canada?” or should the province take the legal steps required for a definitive independence vote? Alberta’s election authority says ballots for question 10 will be counted first, with results expected in the early hours Tuesday.

The pre-referendum period was clouded by avalanches of manipulated AI content.

Carney has urged “a decisive result,” but experts are concerned about a contested outcome no matter the numbers.

“A very likely result of this referendum is going to be a community that sees this election as stolen or at least unfair,” said Aengus Bridgman, director of the Media Ecosystem Observatory at McGill University.

Close Trump allies have also inserted themselves into the discussion, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who in January described Alberta as a “natural partner” for the United States.

After a separatist party won Quebec’s provincial election on October 5, tech billionaire Elon Musk posted that “they would be better off” if they seceded.

“Alberta and Saskatchewan should separate too,” he added.

Asked about alleged foreign interference, Carney said Thursday that foreign governments, including the US, should not “get themselves involved in our elections.”

World.title: Mangrove loss raises flood, erosion risks along Karachi coast
World.content:
Satellite images from 2000 and 2025 show mangroves near Mai Kolachi replaced by reclaimed land.—Courtesy Suparco

ISLAMABAD: New satellite images from 2000 and 2025 released by the country’s space agency show a fundamental shift in land cover along Karachi’s coastal zone near the Mai Kolachi Bypass, where mangrove stands and natural tidal creeks have increasingly given way to reclaimed land and urban development.

In a note on the development, the Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Comm­ission (Suparco) said areas once characterised by continuous mangrove cover and natural tidal creeks had progressively been converted into reclaimed land and urban plots.

“This transformation refle­cts a transition from ecosystem-based coastal protection to hard, land-intensive development. Mangrove removal directly weakens the coastal system’s ability to respond to climate stress,” the agency said.

Suparco observed that mangroves played a key role in regulating coastal temperatures, trapping sediments and absorbing atmospheric carbon. Their clearance not only eliminated an important blue-carbon reservoir but also disrupted hydrological connectivity, increasing surface runoff and altering tidal flows, it said.

“Over time, this raises the likelihood of localised flooding, shoreline instability and long-term land subsidence. From a climate perspective, the conversion of mangrove wetlands into built-up land represents a loss of natural resilience at a time when sea-level rise and extreme weather events are accelerating,” it said.

Unlike engineered structures, mangroves adapt and regenerate, offering protection that strengthens over time. Their replacement with static infrastructure transfers climate risk directly to urban assets and populations, the agency observed.

Satellite images from 2000 and 2025 show mangroves near Mai Kolachi replaced by reclaimed land.—Courtesy Suparco

When contacted, Senator Sherry Rehman, chairperson of the Senate Standing Committee on Climate Change, declined to comment. Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab did not respond to messages.

Climate policy specialist Mohammad Saleem Shaikh warned that Pakistan must protect its mangrove forests and natural tidal creeks, stressing that their destruction threatened coastal communities, livelihoods and economic stability.

Referring to Suparco’s satellite evidence showing changes along Karachi’s coast near Mai Kolachi Bypass between 2000 and 2025, Mr Shaikh called for urgent measures to prevent further environmental degradation.

He said mangroves stored carbon, reduced coastal erosion, weakened storm surges and sustained fisheries and biodiversity. Their loss could increase Pakistan’s vulnerability to rising sea levels, cyclones and other climate-related threats, particularly along Karachi’s coastline and the Indus Delta, he warned.

Mr Shaikh urged the federal and Sindh governments to strengthen environmental enforcement, prevent encroachment and ensure that coastal development projects underwent comprehensive environmental assessments.

He also called for transparent satellite monitoring, community participation and scientifically planned restoration using native species. He said mangroves should be treated as natural climate infrastructure essential for disaster resilience and future generations.

Meanwhile, satellite imagery acquired between 2019 and 2026 and posted on Suparco’s Spa­ce4Cli­mate webpage showed a substantial mangrove afforestation event in the Shah Bandar region of Sujawal.

Comparative analysis of 19 Areas of Interest showed a 115pc increase in mangrove forest cover relative to 2019 baseline area of 116.46 hectares.

Newly established mangrove vegetation of 151.24 hectares accounted for around 6.5pc of the total 2,321.8-hectare study area.

World.title: LPG stakeholders seek daily pricing amid soaring rates
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: As liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surge following the closure of the Rahimdad-250 border post, market stakeholders on Sunday urged the government to shift from monthly to weekly or daily pricing, in line with petroleum products, and delink rates from Saudi Aramco’s Contract Price (CP).

The demand comes ahead of winter, when LPG consumption traditionally rises, increasing the risk of hoarding, blackmarketing and artificial price hikes, particularly in remote and hilly areas. Stakeholders say the LPG policy, unchanged for over a decade, no longer reflects market realities. Although prices are benchmarked to Saudi CP, supplies largely come from Iran, Oman, the UAE and Iraq, including Iranian LPG allegedly routed through alternative sea channels.

They argue that advance monthly prices notified by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) discourage major state-owned enterprises (SOEs) from importing LPG, leaving the market vulnerable to private importers and land-route suppliers amid weak enforcement. Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and ministry spokesman Zafar Abbas did not respond to written queries.

Border closures, outdated pricing and weak oversight fuel LPG market crisis

The Ministry of Commerce’s October 16 memorandums withdrawing electronic import form (EIF) exemptions for Iranian imports and shipments to Central Asian Republics (CARs) and Azerbaijan via Iran have further disrupted supplies. More than 4,500 tonnes of LPG are reportedly stranded on the Iranian side.

Pakistan consumes nearly two million tonnes of LPG annually, of which 30 per cent is produced domestically and 70pc imported. Of the 1.2 million tonnes imported, around 250,000 tonnes arrive through Port Qasim and nearly one million tonnes through Iranian routes, including Taftan, Mand and Rahimdad-250. Taftan has remained closed for nearly six months over security concerns, while Mand faces intermittent disruptions, increasing reliance on Rahimdad-250.

Mohammad Ali Haider, vice chairman of the LPG Marketing Association, representing over 200 companies, said prices rose by Rs100 per kilogram over the weekend following withdrawal of the trade exemption and could climb further without immediate intervention.

He said no imports were currently arriving at Saudi CP-based prices. Before the war, Iranian auctioned LPG reached the border at $100-150 per tonne below Saudi CP. War-related insurance and freight premiums have since pushed costs to around $300 per tonne above CP, making Ogra’s benchmark increasingly unrealistic.

Mr Haider said oil prices had shifted to daily adjustments after the war began, while LPG remained tied to advance monthly notifications disconnected from actual costs. Consequently, major players, including SSGC, SNGPL and Pak-Arab Refinery, avoid imports at notified rates, fearing accountability investigations.

Border disruptions have also shifted pressure to Gwadar, pushing freight costs from $60-80 to as high as $380 per tonne. Mr Haider alleged that manipulated freight arrangements, questionable import declarations and the absence of digital tracking of tankers, transporters and distributors facilitated profiteering and tax evasion.

He also criticised a petroleum division directive requiring SOEs to auction LPG against signature bonuses, arguing that the mechanism favoured cash-rich companies. Pakistan Petroleum Limited had previously allocated production through transparent bidding, offering 25 tonnes monthly to each successful bidder. A relatively obscure company reportedly offered a Rs220 million signature bonus for a five-tonne quota, prompting allegations of money laundering and consumer exploitation. Litigation has stalled the process.

Mr Haider urged the government to review the LPG policy with stakeholders, revise the Rs35,000-per-tonne marketing margin fixed in 2016, digitally track imports and distribution, and publish daily prices on Ogra’s website. He also questioned the use of a Rs4,690-per-tonne petroleum levy introduced in 2016 to cushion consumers against price shocks, saying it was not serving its intended purpose.

World.title: Pakistan stresses diplomacy as Iran rejects US ‘threats’
World.content:
• Dar discusses evolving regional situation in call with Araghchi

• Iranian FM says Tehran rejects intimidation but remains open to dialogue

• Insists seven-day Hormuz reopening proposal remains on table

• Pakistani, Egyptian FMs condemn Houthi attacks, discuss R-4 coordination

• Iran’s new defence minister threatens ‘enormous damage’ to US if attacks renewed

ISLAMABAD: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Sunday stressed the need for continued dialogue and diplomacy in a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi as regional tensions persisted amid the US-Iran conflict and renewed fighting in Yemen.

The Foreign Office said the two ministers discussed the evolving regional situation as well as the ongoing meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation’s (OIC) Council of Foreign Ministers in Baghdad.

Mr Dar “underscored the importance of continued dialogue and diplomacy in addressing regional challenges”, the FO said, adding that the two sides agreed to remain in close contact.

Mr Dar also held a telephone conversation with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and exchanged views on recent regional developments.

The ministers strongly condemned Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia and reaffirmed their solidarity with the kingdom as well as support for its sovereignty, territorial integrity and security. They also discussed cooperation under the Regional Four (R-4) framework comprising Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia. The two ministers looked forward to the next R-4 meeting to coordinate further on regional issues.

Iran rejects ‘threats’

Meanwhile, Mr Arag­hchi told the OIC meeting in Baghdad that Iran “does not accept coercion, threats, or intimidation” by the US and “will not relinquish its sovereign rights under pressure”. “But it remains ready for dialogue based on mutual respect and credible guarantees,” he added. Speaking to the media in Baghdad, Mr Araghchi said Iran’s offer to reopen the strategic waterway within seven days remained on the table.

“Our situation is clear and based on the seven-day proposal presented to the US. They shared comments which we are reviewing, but our proposal is still on the table,” Mr Araghchi said.

He said that if the US showed “honesty”, the path towards reopening the Strait of Hormuz was clear. Iran’s conditions incl­ude lifting the US blockade on its ports, removing sanctions on its oil exports and ending hostilities across regional fronts. Mr Araghchi added that if Washington accepted Tehran’s conditions, the strait could reopen within six days, followed by the resumption of talks the next day.

US warned

Iran’s newly appointed defence minister Mehrdad Akhlaghi warned that any renewed US military attack would cause “enormous damage” to Washington and its regional allies.

“People can rest assured that they will most likely not dare to attack us,” Mr Akhlaghi told reporters shortly after securing parliament’s vote of confidence. “If they do, they themselves and the region will suffer enormous damage,” he said.

World.title: Cotton arrivals jump 7.5pc as textile crisis deepens
World.content:
• Industry says 500 ginning factories, over 150 textile mills closed

• Ginners allege imported inputs meant for re-export are being sold locally

LAHORE: Cotton arrivals at ginning factories rose 7.53 per cent year-on-year to 4.08 million bales by Oct 15, but the domestic cotton and textile industries are facing a deepening crisis, with around 500 ginning factories, over 150 textile mills and nearly half of the country’s power looms reportedly lying idle.

Industry representatives have attributed the crisis to rising production costs and alleged misuse of the Export Facilitation Scheme (EFS), under which imported yarn and fabric are reportedly being sold in the domestic market instead of being re-exported.

According to the Pakistan Cotton Ginners Association (PCGA), arrivals reached 4,081,265 bales by Oct 15, up 285,628 bales from 3,795,637 bales a year earlier.

Punjab recorded arrivals of 1.64m bales, up 7.79pc, while Sindh’s arrivals increased 7.35pc to 2.44m bales. Bahawalnagar led Punjab with 418,750 bales, followed by Bahawalpur with 294,606, Dera Ghazi Khan 236,514, Rahim Yar Khan 169,949 and Layyah 122,327.

In Sindh, Sanghar topped the list with 1.14m bales, followed by Sukkur with 264,500 bales, Naushehro Feroze 223,200 and Khairpur 213,900.

A total of 471 ginning factories were operational nationwide. Textile mills had purchased around 3.45m bales and exporters 97,000 bales, leaving 531,530 bales unsold. Arrivals during the preceding fortnight totalled 872,863 bales.

However, Cotton Ginners Forum Chairman Ihsanul Haq warned that adverse weather could leave national production below initial estimates.

He also pointed to a discrepancy between PCGA figures and those of the Punjab Crop Reporting Service, which put provincial production at 2.983m bales against the PCGA’s 1.638m bales in arrivals by Oct 15.

Mr Haq said the alleged misuse of the EFS, coupled with rising production costs, had undermined the domestic industry. He cited estimates that 40m to 50m metres of fabric had been imported from China alone under the scheme, while exports had shown little corresponding growth.

Figures released by the All Pakistan Textile Mills Association (Aptma) showed man-made yarn imports rising from 3,056 tonnes in the first quarter of 2025-26 to 12,773 tonnes in the corresponding quarter of 2026-27. Man-made fabric imports increased from 660 tonnes to 8,628 tonnes over the same period.

Mr Haq alleged that some imports intended for re-export were instead being sold locally, where an 18pc sales tax applied, putting domestic manufacturers at a disadvantage.

Aptma has welcomed Customs action against alleged misuse of the scheme and called for restrictions on imports of man-made yarn and fabric under the EFS. It said around 500 ginning factories and more than 150 textile mills had closed, while nearly half of the country’s power looms were inactive.

Sajid Mahmood, head of the Transfer of Technology Department at the Central Cotton Research Institute (CCRI), Multan, said cotton revival required policies focused not only on production but also on farmers’ profitability, production costs, market access and lint quality.

If cotton continued to offer lower returns than competing crops, farmers could reduce acreage in the next season, he warned.

With 15 to 20 days of picking remaining, he urged farmers to follow agricultural experts’ advice to protect yields and quality. The CCRI has recommended a spray containing 2kg of urea per 100 litres of water in fields with eight to 10 green bolls per plant to encourage boll opening.

Farmers should also monitor pink bollworm infestation, pick mature bolls promptly and harvest in dry weather to prevent contamination.

Mr Mahmood said the success of cotton revival should be measured by farmers’ net income per acre, not merely the volume of arrivals at ginning factories.

Karachi Cotton Brokers Forum leader Naseem Usman urged the government not only to announce a cotton support price but also to devise a procurement mechanism in case market prices fell below the support level.

He hoped that the undocumented cotton business would see a decline this year due to strict government measures and might lead to some increase in the overall cotton production.

World.title: 18 marble workers abducted in Khuzdar
World.content:
QUETTA: As many as 18 labourers working at a marble mine in the Naal area, about 40 kilometres from Khuzdar city, were kidnapped on Sunday, police said.

A large group of armed men entered the mine premises, held the labourers at gunpoint and abducted 18 of them, along with the son of a mine factory’s owner, officials said. The abductors also opened fire on a worker when he attempted to flee, they added.

The abducted labourers are locals from the Wadh and Naal areas.

The mine belongs to Sardar Alam Khan Bizenjo, son of Sardar Aslam Bizenjo, the tribal chief of the Bizenjo tribe. Aslam Bizenjo is affiliated with the National Party and has served as a minister in several Balochistan governments.

While fleeing the scene, the armed men also took away a loader and two vehicles, officials said. Officials said security forces had launched a search operation in the area to trace the abd­u­cted labourers. No group has so far claimed res­ponsibility for the kidnapping.
